entries.t: Namo Bharat Regional Rapid Transit System
entries.head:
GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF HOUSING AND URBAN AFFAIRS 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 3000 
TO BE ANSWERED ON AUGUST 06, 2026 
 
NAMO BHARAT REGIONAL RAPID TRANSIT SYSTEM 
NO. 3000 DR. HEMANG JOSHI: 
    SHRI PRADEEP KUMAR SINGH: 
  SHRI ARUN GOVIL: 
  SHRI JANARDAN MISHRA: 
  SHRI MANISH JAISWAL:  
 
 Will the Minister of HOUSING AND URBAN AFFAIRS be pleased to state: 
(a) the details of  the milestones achieved under the Namo Bharat 
Regional Rapid Transit System  (RRTS), particularly following the full 
operationalisation of the 82- kilometre Delhi-Ghaziabad-Meerut corridor 
in February, 2026;  
(b) the details of the current ridership metrics and punctuality standards 
including the framework for multimodal convergence with existing 
metro networks and bus terminals to facilitate seamless commuter 
mobility; 
(c) the details of the current status and projected roadmap for  the 
subsequent Phase- I corridors and the proposed linkage to Jewar 
Airport to ensure interoperable regional connectivity; and 
(d) the details of the specific interventions implemented by the National 
Capital Region Transport Corporation (NCRTC) to foster transit -
oriented development, integrate renewable energy solutions and 
provide inclusive fare structures for marginalised categories?   
 
ANSWER 
       THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE 
 MINISTRY OF HOUSING AND URBAN AFFAIRS 
     (SHRI TOKHAN SAHU) 
 
(a): The 82.15 Km long India’s first Namo Bharat Regional Rapid 
Transit System (RRTS) corridor namely, Delhi -Ghaziabad-Meerut RRTS 
corridor (which includes 23 km of Meerut metro network on same 
infrastructure) has become fully operational since February, 2026.  
  
…2/- 
 
 
 

-2- 
(b): National Capital Region Transport Corporation Ltd. (NCRTC), the 
implementing agency for Namo Bharat RRTS, has informed that as on 
date, over 3.8 crores commuters have availed the Namo Bharat services 
since beginning of operation with a punctuality level of over 99%. Further, 
on Delhi -Ghaziabad-Meerut Namo Bharat RRTS corridor, effective multi -
modal integration has been established with 03 Metro lines, 02 Railway 
stations and 04 Bus terminals , conforming to the guidelines outlined by 
Unified Traffic and Transportation Infrastructure (Planning and 
Engineering) Centre, DDA. 
 
(c): In Phase- I, three Namo Bharat RRTS corridors have been 
prioritized namely, (i) Delhi -Ghaziabad-Meerut, (ii) Delhi -Gurugram-Alwar 
and (iii) Delhi -Panipat. The Delhi -Ghaziabad-Meerut Namo Bharat RRTS 
corridor is fully operational since February, 2026. Further, NCRTC has 
submitted the Detailed Project Reports (DPRs) for the Namo Bharat RRTS 
corridors from Delhi to Karnal, Delhi to Bawal, Bawal to Behror and 
Ghaziabad to Noida International Airport. The Namo Bharat RRTS projects 
are cost intensive proposals and therefore, undergo intensive 
examination at different levels in Central Government. After such 
examination, Central Government considers financial assistance to RRTS 
projects, based on feasibility of the proposal and availability of resources. 
 
(d): NCRTC has informed that it has implemented several specific 
interventions across the Delhi -Ghaziabad-Meerut Namo Bharat RRTS 
corridor, such as, (i) TOD Zones of the Delhi -Ghaziabad-Meerut have been 
delineated and notified in Masterplans of Ghaziabad and Meerut along 
with special areas for TOD, (ii) Under Delhi TOD policy, 2021, NCRTC has 
prepared Influence Zone Plans (IZP) for the TOD Nodes at Jangpura and 
Sarai Kale Khan. Further, as per provisions of Delhi TOD Policy, 2026, any 
new RRTS corridor will automatically be considered under TOD in Delhi. 
NCRTC has further informed that a cumulative rooftop solar capacity of 
7.8 MWp has been successfully installed to harness green energy. In 
respect of fare structure, NCRTC has informed that a 35% discount on 
base fare is being provided to all commuters. Additionally, NCRTC has 
also introduced concept of loyalty points, which are earned by commuters 
by traveling on RRTS network, which is used for availing discount.

entries.t: Widening of Aroor to Edappally Stretch on NH-66
entries.head:
GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS 
  
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 3001 
ANSWERED ON 6TH AUGUST, 2026 
  
WIDENING OF AROOR TO EDAPPALLY STRETCH ON NH-66 
  
3001. SHRI HIBI EDEN: 
  
Will the Minister of ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS 
सड़क परिवहन औि िाजमार्ग मंत्री  
be pleased to state:  
  
(a) whether the Government proposes an eight -lane elevated highway on the 
Aroor to Edappally stretch of National Highway (NH)-66; 
  
(b) if  so, the details and the present status thereof and if not, the reasons 
therefor; 
  
(c) whether the Aroor to Edappally stretch of NH -66 is among the most 
congested National Highway stretches in Kerala and if so, the comparative 
traffic data thereof; 
  
(d) whether there are any alternative arrangements proposed to address the 
severe traffic congestion on the Aroor to Edappally stretch of NH -66, which 
has multiple major junctions and crossings of the Kochi Metro corridor, if so, 
the details thereof and if not, the reasons therefor; and 
  
(e) whether the Aroor to Edappally stretch of NH -66 in Kerala is the only 
National Highway stretch without a clear decision or timeline from the 
Government, if so, the details thereof? 
  
  

ANSWER 
  
THE MINISTER OF ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS 
 
(SHRI NITIN JAIRAM GADKARI) 
  
(a) to (e)    Government keeps on undertaking Detailed Project Report (DPR)/ 
feasibility study to upgrade the National Highway (NH) network   with the aim 
to improve logistic efficiency and reduce the travel time.  The existing 4-lane 
carriageway on Aroor –Edappally stretch of NH -66 accommodates Kochi 
Metro Corridor. In order to address traffic congestion in this stretch, which 
passes through busy locations such as Angamaly, Aluva, Kalamassery, 
Edappally, Palarivattom, Vyttila and Kundannoor  in Ernakulam district, work 
of DPR for Ernakulam Bypass (Kochi Outer Ring Road)   has been awarded, 
connecting Angamaly (near Cochin International Airport) to Aroor. The 
alignment of the said project was approved in the meeting of the Alignment 
Approval Committee (AAC). Decision for project implementation and 
investment is taken based on the outcome of DPR and compliance with the 
Policy for decongestion of urban areas issued on 29th May, 2026.

(a) to (d) Petroleum and Natural Gas Regulatory Board (PNGRB) is the authority to grant authorization to 
various entities to Lay, build, operate and expand Natural Gas Pipelines (NGPL). As on March 2026, 
PNGRB has authorized approximately 33,027 Km of common carrier natural gas pipeline across the 
country to create a National Gas Grid. All the States and Union Territories, except Ladakh, Andaman &

The details of the Common Carrier Natural Gas Pipeline network including the States of Madhya Pradesh, 
Rajasthan, and Jharkhand are enclosed as Annexure-I. In the Dewas - Shajapur Parliamentary Constituency 
of Madhya Pradesh, approximately 84.67 km of operational natural gas pipeline network is deployed under 
the National Gas Grid. This operational infrastructure comprises major trunk and spur lines, including 
sections of Hazira - Vijaipur (24.91 km), Dahej - Vijaipur (DVPL I) (24.93 km), Dahej - Vijaipur (DVPL II) 
(24.95 km), Sanwer - Dewas (8.52 km), Dewas - HR Johnson (1.30 km), and the HR Johnson - Roca spur 
line (0.07 km), providing robust natural gas connectivity across the constituency.  
Providing Piped Natural Gas (PNG) connections and establishment of Compressed Natural Gas (CNG) 
stations is part of the development of City Gas Distribution (CGD) Network, which inter alia include 
creation of pipeline infrastructure and other facilities for the supply of PNG to domestic, commercial and 
industrial units and CNG to transport sector which is being carried out by the entities authorized by

development of CGD network in 309 Geographical Areas (GAs), covering the entire mainland area of the 
country. Details of CGD progress in the states of Madhya Pradesh, Rajasthan and Jharkhand and CGD 
progress in the Pali Parliamentary Constituency, North-East Delhi, Ratlam and Jhabua Districts, Alirajpur 
District, Dewas District and Shajapur District are given at Annexure – II.

infrastructure rollout and investmentsare made by the authorized CGD entity in accordance with the 
authorization granted by PNGRB and the approved project plan.

gas from non-priority se

3003.  SHRI DARSHAN SINGH CHOUDHARY 
 पेĚोͧलयम और Ĥाकृ Ǔतक गैस मंğी  
 
 Will the Minister of PETROLEUM AND NATURAL GAS be pleased to state: 
(a) whether the Government has implemented any special policy, incentive scheme or action plan 
during the year 2026 to promote the production, use and supply of Sustainable Aviation Fuel 
(SAF), if so, the details thereof; 
(b) whether the Government is taking any special initiative in collaboration with Oil Marketing 
Companies, aviation companies, research institutions and the private sector to enhance the 
production capacity, blending, quality standards and supply chain of SAF for increasing its use 
in the aviation sector, if so, the details thereof; 
(c) the details of the pilot projects approved, research and development activities, investments, 
production capacity and financial assistance relating to SAF during the year 2026; and 
(d) whether the Government is implementing any time-bound action plan to promote the 
indigenous production of SAF from agricultural residues, used cooking oil, bio-waste and other 
bio-based feedstocks with a view to reducing dependence on imported aviation fuel and 
lowering carbon emissions, if so, the details thereof? 
ANSWER 
पेᮝोिलयम और ᮧाक ृ ितक गैस मंᮢालय मᱶ रा᭔य मंᮢी 
(᮰ी सुरेश गोपी) 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF PETROLEUM & NATURAL GAS  
 (SHRI SURESH GOPI) 
(a) to (d): The Government has approved indicative blending targets of 1% by 2027, 2% by 2028, 
and 5% by 2030 for Sustainable Aviation Fuel (SAF) in conventional Aviation Turbine Fuel (ATF),  
initially for international flights. Public sector Oil Marketing Companies are actively engaged in 
achieving the stated blending targets.  
 
Further, the Government has taken several steps to support the development of a SAF ecosystem in the 
country. These include: 
 
(i) Notification of amendment to the Aviation Turbine Fuel (ATF) (Regulation of Marketing) 
Order, 2001 (ATF Control Order) vide notification dated 17 April 2026, as an 
administrative measure to bring Aviation Turbine Fuel blended with Sustainable Aviation 
Fuel (SAF) under the ambit of the ATF Control Order. 
(ii) Recognition of the National Accreditation Board for Certification Bodies (NABCB) for 
accreditation of SAF certification bodies under the International Sustainability and Carbon 
Certification (ISCC) scheme. 

(iii)  Facilitation of long-term SAF supply arrangements between Oil Marketing Companies 
(OMCs) and airlines, including the signing of Memoranda of Understanding between 
OMCs and Airlines, 
(iv) Conducting stakeholder consultations and awareness programmes on SAF. 
 
Indian Oil Corporation limited (IOCL) and Bharat Petroleum Corporation Limited (BPCL) have 
received ISCC Carbon Offsetting and Reduction Scheme for International Aviation (ISCC CORSIA) 
certification for SAF production at their Panipat and Mumbai refineries, respectively.  
 
To facilitate Advanced Biofuel production including SAF, the Government notified the "Pradhan 
Mantri JI- V AN (Jaiv Indhan- Vatavaran Anukool Fasal Awashesh Nivaran) Yojana" in 2019, amended 
in 2024, with the objectives to establish advanced biofuels projects including projects for SAF 
production in the country using lignocellulosic biomass and other renewable feedstocks. The total 
financial outlay for PM JI-V AN is Rs. 1,969.50 crore, of which Rs. 1,800 crore is allocated for 
commercial-scale advanced biofuel projects and Rs. 150 crore for demonstration- scale advanced 
biofuel projects. The total cost of the project inter-alia includes biomass supply chain and handling, 
technology charges, cost of the total equipment etc. Under the PM JI-V AN Yojana, the maximum 
financial assistance of Rs.150 crore per project for commercial scale projects and Rs. 15 crore per 
project for demonstration scale projects have been prescribed for improving commercial viability as 
well as promoting R&D for development and adoption of technologies in the field of production of 
advanced biofuels. 
 
In June 2026, financial assistance was approved under the PM JI-V AN Yojana for three commercial-
scale and two demonstration-scale SAF projects. The details of the approved projects are as under:

entries.t: Development of Aviation Sector under UDAN Scheme
entries.head:
GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF CIVIL AVIATION 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. : 3004 
 ( TO BE ANSWERED ON THE  6th August 2026 )  
DEVELOPMENT OF AVIATION SECTOR UNDER UDAN SCHEME  
3004.    SHRI MALAIYARASAN D                      
Will the Minister of CIVIL AVIATION 
be pleased to state:- 
(a) the details and the current status of implementation of the Ude Desh ka Aam 
Nagrik (UDAN) scheme including the number of routes operationalised, 
airports/heliports/water aerodromes made functional, State/UT-wise, particularly in 
Kallakurichi Lok Sabha Constituency of Tamil Nadu; 
(b) the total funds allocated, released and utilised under the said scheme since its 
inception till date, year-wise; 
(c) whether several regional routes have been discontinued or suspended du e to 
low passenger traffic or financial viability issues and if so, the details thereof; 
(d) the steps taken to improve last-mile air connectivity in remote, hilly and coastal 
regions and to ensure long-term sustainability of subsidised routes; and 
(e) whether the Government proposes any modification or extension of the UDAN 
Scheme beyond its current phase and if so, the details thereof? 
ANSWER 
Minister of State in the Ministry of CIVIL AVIATION      (Shri Murlidhar Mohol) 
(a) to (e): Since inception of the  Regional Connectivity Scheme (RCS) -UDAN, a 
total of 679 RCS routes connecting 95 unserved and underserved airports, 
including 17 heliports and 02 water aerodromes, have been operationalised across 
the country under the UDAN Scheme. 
No aerodromes located in the Kallakurichi Lok Sabha Constituency of Tamil Nadu 
have been identified for development under the UDAN Scheme. 
For revival and development of un -served and under -served 
airports/heliports/water aerodromes identified under Regional Connectivity 
Scheme - Ude Desh ka Aam Nagrik (RCS-UDAN), an amount of Rs. 4500 crore in 
the Phase I and an amount of Rs.1000 Crores in Phase II of the Scheme has been 

allocated. Rs.4,839.48 crore has been incurred for revival/development of airports 
under RCS till date. 
Under the scheme, 156 routes discontinued services before completion of their 3 -
year VGF support tenure due to operational and airline related issues. 
The next phase of the UDAN Scheme was launched on 04.07.2026 to promote 
regional air connectivity in Tier 2 an d Tier 3 cities and remote regions across the 
country, targeting 120 new destinations and 4 crore passengers over the next 10 
years. The Scheme is being implemented from FY 2026 -27 to FY 2035-36 with an 
outlay of Rs 28,840 crore, including Rs. 12,159 crore  for Aerodrome development 
and Rs3,661 crore for development of 200 heliports in Hilly, North -Eastern and 
Aspirational (HINER) States/districts.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS 
  
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 3006 
ANSWERED ON 6TH AUGUST, 2026 
  
BHOOMI RASHI PORTAL FOR LAND ACQUISITION 
  
3006. SHRI SUKHJINDER SINGH RANDHAWA: 
 SHRI VIJAY BAGHEL: 
 SHRI JASWANTSINH SUMANBHAI BHABHOR: 
 SHRI PRAVEEN PATEL: 
 SHRI RAMESH AWASTHI:

 SHRI SANJAY HARIBHAU JADHAV:

 SHRI ASHISH DUBEY: 
 SHRI BUNTY VIVEK SAHU: 
  
Will the Minister of ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS 
  
सड़क परिवहन औि िाजमार्ग मंत्री 
  
be pleased to state: 
 
(a) whether the Government has reviewed the implementation of the 
Bhoomi Rashi Portal for land acquisition under National Highway (NH) 
projects, if so, the details thereof, State/UT-wise; 
  

(b) the details of land acquired, affected farmers/landowners and 
compensation paid to them  through the said portal, State -wise and 
district-wise; 
  
(c) the details of the progress made in digitisation of the land 
acquisition process and direct  disbursement of compensation through 
the portal and the present status thereof, State/UT -wise particularly in 
Punjab; 
  
(d) whether any special measures and  the steps have been taken to 
improve transparency,  reduce delays in land acquisition, resolve 
pending cases and address grievances of farmers  under National 
Highway projects, if so, the details thereof, State/UT-wise; 
  
(e) the impact of the said portal o n expediting project implementation, 
ensuring transparency  and improving timely disbursement of 
compensation to affected landowners, State/UT-wise; and 
  
(f) the details of ongoing and upcoming NH infrastructure project, 
State/UT-wise? 
  
ANSWER 
  
THE MINISTER OF ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS 
  
(SHRI NITIN JAIRAM GADKARI) 
  
(a) to (e)    The BhoomiRashi Portal is a centrally monitored portal and 
its development is regularly reviewed by the Central Government in 
Ministry of Road Transport and Highways. 
  
The intent of BhoomiRashi Portal is to provide single -point 
platform for online processing of notifications related to land 
acquisition under the National Highways (NH) Act, 1956 to accelerate 
highway infrastructure development projects in India and 

disbursement of the compensation to the recipient. The Portal has 
been made mandatory for processing land acquisition notifications. 
The Portal was launched for the said purposes in April 2018. The 
Portal supports the plotting of GIS -based acquisition maps, and h as 
been integrated with Public Financial Management System (PFMS) and 
Aadhaar-based authentication to improve accuracy and reliability in 
disbursement of compensation to land owners. The BhoomiRashi 
Portal through its online processing has reduced the aver age time 
taken for statutory notifications. 
  
          The land acquisition for National Highway projects is project -
based and a continuous process. The Competent Authority for Land 
Acquisition (CALA) is responsible for the preparation of the awards. 
The total land acquired through BhoomiRashi Portal is approximately 
1,88,690 hectare (details annexed at Annexure -A) and compensation 
disbursed is approximately ₹ 53,196 crore. However, title disputes and 
apportionment of compensation between contesting partie s claiming 
compensation is referred to the Principal Civil Court having jurisdiction 
and the assessed compensation amount is deposited in the court.   
  
          Government in Ministry of Road Transport and Highways has 
conducted various capacity building  trainings/ workshops of Central/ 
State officials involved in land acquisition process at Central/ State -
level institutes, State capitals, etc. Remedies such as objections and 
arbitration mechanisms under the NH Act, 1956, Centralized Public 
Grievance Redr ess and Monitoring System (CPGRAMS), etc. are 
available with the landowners for resolution of their grievances. 
  
          The progress of National Highway projects, including land 
acquisition, is regularly monitored by the Government at various 
levels, b y conducting coordination meetings led by the Chief 
Secretaries of States/ UTs where unresolved issues, if any, are 

escalated for further review through the Project Monitoring Group and 
also through “PRAGATI”.

3009.   THIRU ARUN NEHRU: 
 
Will the Minister of MICRO, SMALL AND MEDIUM ENTERPRISES be pleased to state: 
 
(a)  the total financial subsidies and margin money disbursed under the Prime Minister's 
Employment Generation Programme (PMEGP) within the Perambalur Lok Sabha constituency of 
Tamil Nadu over the last three years; 
 
(b)  the specific number of new agro -based and textile manufacturing micro -units successfully

period; 
 
(c)  whether the Ministry has noted a high rate of rejection of the applications or excessive demands 
for collateral by the regional rural banks, contrary to the central scheme guidelines and if so, the details 
thereof;

said constituency during the last three years; and 
 
(e)  the administrative steps being taken by the Government to simplify the online application 
process and conduct targeted entrepreneurship awareness camps in the rural blocks of Perambalur?

(a): Margin Money (MM) Subsidy amounting to Rs. 5.66 crore has been disbursed under the Prime 
Minister's Employment Generation Programme (PMEGP) in the Perambalur Lok Sabha constituency of 
Tamil Nadu during the last three years i.e. FY 2023-24 to FY 2025-26.

industries and 1 micro‑enterprise under textile manufacturing by entrepreneurs, including local youth, 
in the Perambalur district. Out of these, 9 micro‑enterprises we re established by women entrepreneurs

rates by Regional Rural Banks under PMEGP. As per RBI Master Directions on lending to MSMEs, no

entrepreneurship awareness camps under PMEGP throughout the country including rural blocks of

SLUM REHABILITATION SCHEME 
 
 
 
NO. 3013  DR. ALOK KUMAR SUMAN:   
 
Will the Minister of HOUSING AND URBAN AFFAIRS be pleased to state: 
(a) the present status of slum rehabilitation schemes in the country; 
(b) the steps taken by the Government to provide affordable housing in 
urban areas; 
(c) the progress made under housing schemes for the urban poor; 
(d) the present status of the land allocation policy for housing projects; 
and 
(e) the manner in which housing development is being undertaken under 
the Smart Cities Mission? 
 
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE  
MINISTRY OF HOUSING AND URBAN AFFAIRS 
(SHRI TOKHAN SAHU) 
 
(a) to ( d): ‘Land’ and ‘Colonisation’ are State subjects. Therefore, 
schemes related to housing, slum rehabilitation and land allocation for 
housing projects  for their citizens are implemented by States/Union 
Territories (UTs) in their respective areas. However, Ministry of Housing 
and Urban Affairs (MoHUA) supplements the efforts of States/UTs by 
providing Central Assistance under Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana – Urban 
(PMAY-U) since June 25, 2015 to provide pucca houses to all eligible 
urban beneficiaries including urban homeless and slum dwellers across 
the country. 
 
Based on the learnings from the experiences of implementation of PMAY-
U, MoHUA has revamped the scheme and launched PMAY-U 2.0 ‘Housing 
for All’ Mission with effect from 01.09.2024 for implementation in urban 
areas across the country to support 1 crore additional eligible 
beneficiaries. PMAY-U 2.0 is implemented through four verticals i.e., 
Beneficiary Led Construction (BLC), Affordable Housing in Partnership  
…2/- 

-2- 
(AHP), Affordable Rental Housing (ARH) and Interest Subsidy Scheme 
(ISS). The Scheme Guidelines can be accessed at https://pmay -
urban.gov.in/uploads/guidelines/Operational-Guidelines-of-PMAY-U-2.pdf. 
 
Based on the project proposal submitted by States/Union Territories 
(UTs), a total of 127.68 lakh houses including 16.20 lakh under PMAY -U 
2.0 have been sanctioned by the Ministry including slums in cities across 
the country as 13.07.2026. Out of which, 121.03 lakh houses have been 
grounded, 99.07 lakh are completed of which 96.73 lakh are occupied 
across the country as on 13.07.2026 under PMAY-U & PMAY-U 2.0. A total 
of ₹2.12 lakh crores of Central Assistance has been approved of which 
₹1.81 lakh crore have been released to States/UTs based on the 
compliances submitted by them.  Out of total houses sanctioned under 
the scheme, more than  29 lakh houses have been sanctioned to slum 
dwellers.   
 
(e): The Smart Cities Mission (SCM) adopted an integrated approach to 
urban development, wherein housing was as part of comprehensive city 
planning rather than as a standalone component. Since the SCM period 
is over on 31.03.2025, no new schemes are being undertaken now.

 Will the Minister of PETROLEUM AND NATURAL GAS be pleased to state:

Gas (LPG) distribution network in Tamil Nadu, particularly in Dharmapuri Parliamentary

so, the details thereof; 
 
(b) the number of LPG distributors, delivery points and LPG consumers in Dharmapuri 
Parliamentary Constituency and the steps taken to expand the distribution infrastructure 
during the last three years; 
 
(c) whether the Government proposes to establish additional LPG distributorships or 
strengthen delivery logistics in rural and remote areas of Dharmapuri to improve last-mile 
service delivery, if so, the details thereof; and 
 
(d) the measures taken to promote consumer safety, digital booking, doorstep delivery and 
timely refill supply and to further enhance LPG accessibility and service quality across Tamil

MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF PETROLEUM AND NATURAL GAS 
(SHRI SURESH GOPI) 
 
(a) to (d): Appointment of LPG distributorships by the Public Sector Oil Marketing 
Companies (OMCs) is a continuous process and locations for setting up of LPG 
distributorships are identified and advertised under Unified Selection Guidelines 2016.  
As on 01.07.2026, there are a total of 25,611 LPG distributorships of PSU OMCs across the 
country, including 1658 in state of Tamil Nadu, out of which 17,685 distributorships are 
serving rural areas. These are served through 214 LPG bottling plants of Oil Marketing 
Companies (OMCs) located across the country. In order to improve access of LPG in rural 
and remote areas, PSU OMCs have commissioned 8045 distributorships, during 01.04.2016 
to 30.06.2026 across the country, out of which 7452 (i.e. 93 %) are catering to rural areas.  
All distributors, except Durgam Kshetriya Vitraks, are mandated to make home delivery of 
LPG cylinders in their area of operation. 

Dharmapuri Parliamentary Constituency covers Dharmapuri and Salem districts and is served 
by a total of 110 LPG distributors of Public Sector Oil Marketing Companies (OMCs), out of 
which 02 LPG distributorship have been commissioned during last 3 Financial Years. As on 
01.07.2026, there were about total 15.80 lakh domestic LPG consumers in these two districts.  
To further improve last-mile delivery in remote and underserved habitations, OMCs have 
taken several measures, including commissioning of rural and remote-area distributorships, 
appointment of Common Service Center - Village Level Entrepreneur (CSC VLEs), etc. 
OMCs have 162 numbers of CSC VLEs in these aforesaid 02 districts to ensure the last mile 
availability of LPG.   
To ensure the timely availability of LPG refills, all domestic LPG consumers can book a refill 
by various methods including Interactive Voice Response System(IVRS), Short Message 
Service(SMS), Whatsapp, calling directly on the phone of distributor, e-commerce platforms, 
OMC mobile applications, OMCs web-portals etc. These different options provide enhanced 
user accessibility for seamless and hassle-free booking of LPG refills. 
 
The average refill delivery time in Tamil Nadu is 1.6 days as of 01.08.2026. 
 
To improve awareness amongst LPG consumers, a Basic Safety campaign was organised 
during 2024-2025 across the country under the theme “Khushiyan Ab Teen Guna” with the 
objective of reaching the doorsteps of domestic LPG customers. The campaign was designed 
to educate consumers on the safe usage of LPG, complemented by extensive mass awareness 
initiatives through print and electronic media, on-site safety checks at customer premises, and 
the replacement of Suraksha hoses. The campaign achieved significant progress with over 
12.12 crore free basic safety checks conducted at customer premises without any cost to 
consumer including 82.42 lakh in state of Tamil Nadu and more than 4.65 crore LPG hoses 
replaced at discounted rates including 41 lakh in state of Tamil Nadu.

implement drinking water supply schemes including those under Jal Jeevan Mission (JJM). 
Government of India supplements the efforts of the States by providing technical and financial 
assistance for the implementation of the mission 
In August, 2019, Government of India approv ed Jal Jeevan Mission to be implemented in partnership 
with States for a period of five years (2019-24) for making provision of tap water supply to every rural 
household.

have tap water connections in the country. So far, as reported by States/ UTs as on 18.07.2026, around

18.07.2026, out of 19.36 crore rural house holds in the country, around 15.89 crore (82.09%) 
households are reported to have tap water connections in their homes. 
(c) to (e) To complete the ongoing works, Hon'ble Finance Minister during her budget speech 2025-26 
announced extension of JJM until 2028. In March, 2026, Union Cabinet has approved extension of the 
JJM period up to December 2028, with an enhanced outlay and a restructured implementation 
framework focusing on structural reforms in the rural drinking water supply sector under JJM 2.0. The 
total outlay of the mission has been increased from Rs 3.60 lakh crore to Rs. 8.69 lakh crore with 
enhancement of total central assistance from Rs 2.08 lakh crore to Rs 3.59 lakh crore.  
JJM has been envisioned and implemented as a decentralized, demand -driven and community 
managed programme, wherein the Gram Panchayat (GP) and/ or its sub -committee/ user group i.e. 
Village Water & Sanitation Committee (VWSC)/ Pani Samiti have been empowered to plan, 
implement, manage, operate and maintain in -village water s upply system to provide regular and 
assured tap water supply in rural households. Further, provision has been made in the operational

village community, which inter alia includes strengthening of drinking water sources in convergence 
with other schemes. 
To promote Jan Bhagidari for sustainable and continuous service delivery under the JJM, a

Samiti members to ensure smooth handover of water supply schemes and sustainable operations. In 
addition, Jal Seva Ankalan has been initiate d as a Gram Panchayat led digital assessment tool for

operators, etc.

REPLACEMENT OF FAULTY DISTRIBUTION TRANSFORMERS 
 
†3019. SHRI BHARAT SINGH KUSHWAH: 
 
 Will the Minister of POWER 
be pleased to state: 
 
(a)  whether inordinate delays in t he replacement of faulty Distribution 
Transformers in rural and semi-urban areas are resulting in prolonged disruption 
of electricity supply and if so, the details thereof;  
 
(b)  whether overloading of Distribution Transformers, pending pole shifting at 
various locations and dilapidated electricity poles situated in densely populated 
areas are increasing the risk of accidents and if so, the details thereof;  
 
(c)  whether the Government is preparing any time -bound national action plan 
to ensure decentralis ation of Distribution Transformers, expeditious shifting of 
dilapidated electricity poles and poles located in densely populated areas, 
installation of underground/cable-based electricity lines and early electrification 
of long-inhabited majras, tolas, new colonies and settlements in coordination with 
the States; and  
 
(d)  if so, the details thereof? 
A N S W E R 
 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF POWER  
 
(SHRI SHRIPAD NAIK)  
 
(a) to (d) : Electricity is a concurrent subject and power distribution is handled by 
distribution utilities that function under the guidance of their respective State 
Electricity Regulatory Commission (SERC) and State Government. As per the 
Electricity Act, 2003, distribution of electricity is a licensed activity and it is the 
duty of the respective distribution licensee to develop and maintain an efficient 
and safe distribution system in its area of supply. Hence, the responsibility for 
taking necessary measures for the upgradation and maintenance of the 
distribution system and regularly checking the structural strength of poles and 
wires of High Tension (HT) and Low Tension (LT) lines to ensure quality and 
reliable power supply and necessary safety measures, rests with the respective 
distribution utilities, including taking action on complaints in this regard. 
 
………2. 

 
- 2 - 
 
CEA (Measures relating to Safety and Electric Supply) Regulations, 2023, 
specify safety measures for construction, operation and maintenance of power 
stations, sub-stations, transmission and distribution lines. These regulations lay 
down the safety measures for electrical installations and provide for periodic 
inspection and testing of electrical installations. In addition, the CEA (Technical 
Standards for Construction of Electrical Plants and Electric Lines) Regulations, 
2022, contain specific provisions for strengthening of poles and wires in disaster 
prone areas and coastal areas to withstand severe environmental stress. The 
above regulations are applicable to all entities who generate, transmit or 
distribute electricity. 
 
Government of India (GoI) has supplemented the efforts of the States to 
help them provide quality supply of power earlier through schemes like Deen 
Dayal Upadhyaya Gram Jyoti Yojana (DDUGJY) launched in 2014, Pradhan Mantri 
Sahaj Bijli Har Ghar Yojana (SAUBHAGYA) launched in October 2017, and 
currently under the Revamped Distribution Sector Scheme (RDSS) launched in 
July 2021. 
 
Under RDSS, financial assistance is being provided to Distribution Utilities 
for upgradation of distribution infras tructure works such as 
upgradation/augmentation of substations and distribution transformers, 
replacement of conductors, new HT/LT lines, feeder bifurcation, feeder 
segregation, Aerial Bunched Cables (ABC)/covered conductors, underground 
cables and smart m etering, based on proposals submitted by the Distribution 
Utilities. Under the scheme, loss reduction infrastructure works amounting to Rs. 
1.53 lakh crore and smart metering works amounting to Rs. 1.31 lakh crore have 
been sanctioned at the national level.  
 
Government of India is further supporting the States for grid electrification 
of left -out households under RDSS. Under RDSS, on -grid electrification works 
amounting to Rs. 6,521 crore have been sanctioned for electrification of 13.65 
lakh left -out hous eholds, wherever found feasible, including households 
belonging to Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Groups (PVTGs) identified under 
Pradhan Mantri Janjati Adivasi Nyaya Maha Abhiyan (PM -JANMAN); Scheduled 
Tribes (STs) under Dharti Aaba Janjatiya Gram Utkarsh  Abhiyan (DA -JGUA); 
Scheduled Castes (SCs) under Pradhan Mantri Anusuchit Jaati Abhyuday Yojana 
(PM-AJAY); and households in remote and border areas under the Vibrant Village 
Programme (VVP), wherever found feasible. As on 23.07.2026, 4.88 lakh 
households have been electrified under RDSS and state schemes.

3023.   THIRU THANGA TAMILSELVAN: 
Will the Minister of JAL SHAKTI be pleased to state: 
(a) whether the Union Government has any proposal t o undertake a 
comprehensive groundwater mapping exercise for the Vaigai basin and its 
adjoining areas and if so, the details thereof; 
(b) whether the Union Government has also any integ rated water management 
plan for the Vaigai river basin covering irrigation , drinking water and 
groundwater recharge; and 
(c) if so, the details thereof and if not, the reasons therefor? 
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR JAL SHAKTI  
(SHRI RAJ BHUSHAN CHOUDHARY) 
(a) to (c) Water resources projects relating to irr igation, drinking-water supply, 
groundwater recharge and conservation are planned, implemented and 
maintained primarily by the respective State Govern ments, as water is a State 
subject. The Union Government supplements the effor ts of the State 
Governments through technical guidance and various programmes relating to 
water-resource assessment, irrigation efficiency, d rinking-water supply, 
watershed development and groundwater recharge. 
Ministry initiated the National Aquifer Mapping and  Management 
(NAQUIM) Programme in 2012 under the Ground Water M anagement and 

2 
 
Regulation (GWMR) Scheme. Under NAQUIM 1.0, aquifer  mapping covering the 
entire identified mappable area of about 25.14 lakh  sq. km of the country has 
been completed. Subsequently, NAQUIM 2.0 was launch ed in 2023, under which 
scientific and region-specific groundwater maps, aquifer management plans and 
recharge plans are prepared using Geographic Inform ation System (GIS), 
advanced analytical techniques, remote sensing and satellite data. Aquifer 
mapping under NAQUIM 1.0 has been completed for the  Vaigai Basin, covering 
the identified mappable area of about 6,662 sq. km out of the total basin area of 
approximately 8,896 sq. km spread across parts of M adurai, Theni, Sivagangai, 
Ramanathapuram and Dindigul districts. 
Further, based on NAQUIM findings, the Central Grou nd Water Board has 
prepared an Aquifer Management Plan for the Vaigai Basin adopting an 
integrated approach to address declining groundwate r levels, sustainability of 
abstraction structures, low-yielding aquifers and s eawater intrusion. The Plan 
has been shared with the State Government and imple menting agencies to 
facilitate groundwater-management interventions in the Vaigai Basin.

TO BE ANSWERED ON 06.08.2026 
 
PENDENCY ON MSME SAMADHAAN PORTAL 
  
3028.   SHRI BRIJMOHAN AGRAWAL: 
 
Will the Minister of MICRO, SMALL AND MEDIUM ENTERPRISES be pleased to state: 
 
(a)  the total number of delayed payment applications currently pending on the Micro, Small and 
Medium Enterprises (MSME) Samadhaan portal nationwide and the cumulative financial amount 
locked up to the latest quarter of 2026; 
 
(b)  the structural reasons for the delay in full API integration between MSME Samadhaan Portal 
and the Government e -Marketplace (GeM) to automatically enforce the statutory 45 -day payment 
mandate under Section 15 of the Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises Development Act, 2006; 
 
(c)  the total number of pending disputes before the Micro and Small Enterprises Facilitation 
Council (MSEFC) in Chhattisgarh, specifically concerning SC/ST entrepreneurs, tribal cooperatives 
and micro-units in industrial corridors; and 
 
(d)  the timeline for rolling out the Online Dispute Resolution (MSE -ODR) framework under the 
Raising and Accelerating MSME Performance (RAMP) scheme and introducing automated penalty 
mechanisms for defaulting buyer departments? 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE FOR MICRO, SMALL AND MEDIUM ENTERPRISES 
(SUSHRI SHOBHA KARANDLAJE) 
(a):  Ministry of MSME launched MSME SAMADHAAN Portal on 30.10.2017. As on 30.07.2026, 
a total of 90,756 cases involving amount of Rs. 21,030 crore  are at various stages of adjudication with  
the Micro and Small Enterprises Facilitation Councils (MSEFCs).  
 
(b):  GeM has already been integrated with Trade Receivables Discounting System (TReDS) 
wherein there is a facility of invoice discounting available for faster payments to MSMEs. 
 
(c):  As on 30.07.2026, a total of 784 cases , including those pertaining to SC/ST entrepreneurs, are 
at various stages of adjudication with MSEFC in Chhattisgarh. Out of these, 432 applications pertain 
to micro enterprises. 
 
(d):  Ministry of MSME  launched Online Dispute Resolution (ODR) Portal on 27.06.2025. It is a 
digital, technology-enabled mechanism for ensuring speedy, cost -effective, and transparent resolution 
of delayed payment disputes involving Micro and Small Enterprises (MSEs). ODR also  provides 
facility of a pre -litigation, dialogue -based mechanism for voluntary mediation, conciliation or 
negotiation between the buyer and seller before the matter proceeds to MSEFCs for formal 
adjudication.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF CIVIL AVIATION 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. : 3029 
 ( TO BE ANSWERED ON THE  6th August 2026 )  
USAGE OF DRONES 
3029.    SHRI DILESHWAR KAMAIT                    
Will the Minister of CIVIL AVIATION 
be pleased to state:- 
(a) the manner in which the reduction of Goods and Services Tax (GST) on drones to five 
percent last year has impacted the adoption of drone -as-a-service models in the agricultural 
and logistics sectors; 
(b) whether the Government is on track to notify th e National Sustainable Aviation Fuel 
(SAF) Policy to meet the one per cent blending target mandate starting in 2027 and if so, the 
details thereof; 
(c) the progress made in the Namo Drone Didi initiative; and 
(d) the number of women Self -Help Groups trained successfully as drone pilots till February, 
2026? 
ANSWER 
Minister of State in the Ministry of CIVIL AVIATION      (Shri Murlidhar 
Mohol) 
(a) The Government of India has taken a significant step towards strengthening farm 
mechanization by reducing the Goo ds and Services Tax (GST) slab on agricultural 
machinery, including drones, from 12 -18% to 5%. This measure directly benefits farmers 
across the country, particularly those availing support under various farm mechanization 
assistance programs.  
 
The reduction in GST has lowered the purchase cost of drones, making them more affordable 
and accessible for farmers. When combined with financial support available under farm 
mechanization schemes, which provide subsidies of up to 40 -50% for the purchase of 
agricultural machinery, including drones, farmers gain the dual advantage of lower taxation 
and financial assistance. Under the Namo Drone Didi Scheme, subsidies amount to 80% of 
the drone package cost, up to a maximum of Rs 8 lakh per drone package. 
 
(b) The Go vernment has approved indicative blending targets of 1% by 2027, 2% by 2028 
and 5% by 2030 for Sustainable Aviation Fuels (SAF) in conventional Aviation Turbine Fuel 
for international operations. Public sector Oil Marketing Companies are actively engaged i n 
achieving the stated blending targets.  
 
(c) and (d) Namo Drone Didi Yojana (NDDY) was approved by the Government as a Central 
Sector Scheme with an outlay of Rs 1,261 crore for the period from Financial Year (FY) 
2023-24 to FY 2025 -26. The scheme aims t o provide 15,000 agricultural drones to selected 

Women Self-Help Groups (SHGs). In 2023, 1,094 drones were distributed to SHGs by Lead 
Fertilizer Companies using their internal resources. Out of these 1,094 drones, 500 were 
distributed under the NDDY schem e. All SHG members have been provided training at 
Remote Pilot Training Organisations.

entries.head:
1 
 
GOVERNMENT OF INDIA

INTEGRATED WATER GOVERNANCE AND SUSTAINABLE WATER RESOURCE 
MANAGEMENT 
3030.   Thiru D M KATHIR ANAND: 
Will the Minister of JAL SHAKTI be pleased to state: 
(a) whether the Government has examined the need fo r a holistic approach to 
water governance by treating rivers, aquifers, wetl ands and other water 
resources as interconnected ecological systems requ iring coordinated 
management instead of fragmented administrative ove rsight and if so, the 
details thereof; 
(b) the major institutional, legal, infrastructural  and inter-State challenges that 
impede equitable utilisation of water resources and  balanced distribution 
among agriculture, domestic consumption, industry a nd environmental 
requirements; 
(c) the reforms proposed to strengthen basin-orient ed planning, integrated data-
sharing, scientific hydrological assessment, real-t ime monitoring and evidence-
based water resources management; 
(d) the collaborative arrangements envisaged to enh ance coordination among 
State Governments, local bodies, research instituti ons, water user associations 
and civil society organisations for participatory decision-making; and 
(e) the long-term strategy of the Government to pro mote inclusive, sustainable 
and climate-resilient water governance based on the  principle of equitable 
access to water for every citizen? 

2 
 
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR JAL SHAKTI  
(SHRI RAJ BHUSHAN CHOUDHARY) 
 
(a)  The Union Government has recognized the need f or adopting a holistic and 
integrated approach to water governance, considering rivers, aquifers, wetlands 
and other water resources as interconnected compone nts of the hydrological 
and ecological system. Accordingly, the Ministry of  Jal Shakti promotes an 
integrated approach to water resources planning and  management with 
emphasis on river basin-based planning, scientific assessment, technological 
interventions and coordinated institutional mechani sms. The National Water 
Policy, 2012 advocates the principles of Integrated  Water Resources 
Management (IWRM) and emphasizes coordinated develo pment and 
management of water resources at the river basin le vel with a view to ensuring 
their sustainable, equitable and efficient utilization. 
(b)  Water is a State subject under Entry 17 of Lis t II of the Seventh Schedule to 
the Constitution and accordingly, the primary respo nsibility for planning, 
development and management of water resources rests  with the respective 
State Governments. Nevertheless, integrated water g overnance is confronted 
with a number of institutional, legal, infrastructu ral and inter-State challenges. 
These include fragmentation of institutional respon sibilities among multiple 
agencies, variations in State water laws and regula tory frameworks, inter-State 
river water disputes, inadequate storage and convey ance infrastructure, 
hydrometeorological variability across regions and increasing pressures arising 
from rapid urbanization, industrialization and agri cultural water demand while 
ensuring environmental flow requirements. The Gover nment of India addresses 
these challenges through policy support, technical guidance, financial 
assistance under various Central Sector and Central ly Sponsored Schemes, 
capacity-building initiatives and institutional mec hanisms including the 

3 
 
framework provided under the Inter-State River Wate r Disputes Act, 1956, for 
adjudication of inter-State river water disputes. 
(c)  The Government is implementing several initiat ives aimed at strengthening 
integrated water resources management. To support e vidence-based water 
resources management, the Government has implemente d various phases of 
Hydrology Projects,  aimed at improving the extent,  quality, and accessibility of 
water resources information. Under this project, th e National Water Informatics 
Centre (NWIC) has been established which manages (i ) Water Resources 
Information System (India-WRIS) as a robust, public -facing portal for integrated 
data-sharing; and (ii) Water Information Management  System (WIMS), which 
integrates continuous real-time data to generate fl ood forecasts and basin-level 
hydro-meteorological assessments. 
The Government of India has undertaken modernizatio n and expansion of 
surface water and groundwater monitoring networks, including setting up of 
telemetry systems to strengthen basin-oriented plan ning, integrated data-
sharing, scientific hydrological assessment, real-t ime monitoring and evidence-
based water resources management. Around 39,000 Rea l-Time Data Acquisition 
System (RTDAS) stations are currently operational in the country. 
(d)  The Government promotes participatory decision -making through multi-tier 
collaborative arrangements involving all key stakeh olders. To integrate

PROGRESS MADE UNDER NAQUIM 2.0 
†3031.  Shri JASWANTSINH SUMANBHAI BHABHOR: 
Will the Minister of JAL SHAKTI be pleased to state: 
(a) the progress made in preparation of high-resolu tion aquifer mapping and 
area-specific groundwater management plans for Daho d Lok Sabha 
Constituency under the National Aquifer Mapping and  Management Programme 
(NAQUIM 2.0); 
(b) whether any scientific datasets or resource map s prepared under NAQUIM 
2.0 have been shared with the local administration and block-level authorities of 
Dahod Lok Sabha Constituency to address regional wa ter scarcity and if so, the 
details thereof; and 
(c) whether the Government proposes to deploy any i nnovative water 
management solutions or technology consortia under the ANRF–Jal Shakti 
MAHA Water Mission to address drinking water and ir rigation challenges in the 
water-stressed areas of the said Constituency and if so, the details thereof? 
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR JAL SHAKTI  
(SHRI RAJ BHUSHAN CHOUDHARY) 
(a) & (b) Dahod Lok Sabha Constituency comprises pa rts of Dahod and 
Mahisagar districts. Under NAQUIM 1.0, CGWB complet ed aquifer mapping and 
preparation of Aquifer Management Plans for Dahod d istrict covering about 
3,642 sq. km and Mahisagar district covering about 2,512 sq. km. The studies 

2 
 
assessed aquifer characteristics, groundwater resou rces, groundwater quality 
and recharge conditions and recommended suitable su pply-side and demand-
side interventions for sustainable groundwater mana gement. The aquifer maps, 
groundwater data and Aquifer Management Plans have been shared with the 
concerned State Government agencies and the respect ive district 
administrations for use in groundwater planning and management. 
Under NAQUIM 2.0, high-resolution aquifer mapping i s undertaken in 
identified priority areas to address location-speci fic groundwater management 
issues. However, no separate high-resolution aquife r mapping study in Dahod 
Lok Sabha Constituency was undertaken under NAQUIM 2.0. 
(c)  The Mission for Advancement in High-Impact Are as (MAHA) Water 
Programme was launched on 01.06.2026. It is a joint  initiative of the 
Anusandhan National Research Foundation (ANRF), Dep artment of Science and 
Technology and Ministry of Jal Shakti to support mi ssion-oriented, solution-
based research to address key water challenges. The  five thematic areas of the 
MAHA Water Programme are: Water Resource Assessment  and Sustainable 
Management; Drinking Water; Water Quality, Human an d Ecological Health; 
Water Use Efficiency and Circular Economy; and Clim ate Resilience and 
Adaptation.

Will the Minister of JAL SHAKTI be pleased to state: 
(a) whether the Government has initiated implementa tion of the ANRF–Ministry

(b) the institutional framework established for sel ection, monitoring and 
evaluation of research projects and technology cons ortia under the said Mission 
including the mechanism for considering proposals from Dakshina Kannada; 
(c) the measures undertaken/being undertaken to fac ilitate participation of 
Start-ups, Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSM Es), academic institutions 

2 
 
such as Indian Institutes of Technology (IITs), Nat ional Institutes of Technology 
(NITs) etc., and other research organisations in de veloping innovative water 
management solutions; and 
(d) the manner in which technologies developed unde r the said Mission are 
proposed to be validated, deployed and integrated i nto water resources 
management and drinking water programmes like Jal J eevan Mission (JJM) 
across the country? 
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR JAL SHAKTI  
(SHRI RAJ BHUSHAN CHOUDHARY) 
(a) to (d)   Anusandhan National Research Foundatio n (ANRF), a statutory body 
of the Government of India, has been established un der the ANRF Act, 2023 to 
provide high level strategic direction for research , innovation and 
entrepreneurship in fields of natural sciences and scientific and technological 
interfaces of humanities & social sciences to promo te, monitor and provide 
support as required as per recommendations of the N ational Education Policy. 
Mission for Advancement in High-impact Areas (MAHA) is a program under ANRF 
to support priority-centric, solution-based researc h in Mission mode focusing on 
some key areas in alignment with nation’s prime req uirements. It is a multi-
disciplinary, multi-institutional and multi-investi gator project with industrial 
partnerships in the best-sorted areas of immediate concern. 
The MAHA Water program launched on 01.06.2026, is a  joint initiative of 
the ANRF, and the Ministry of Jal Shakti to support  mission-oriented, solution-
based research to address key water challenges. The  five thematic areas of the 
MAHA Water Programme are: Water Resource Assessment  and Sustainable 
Management; Drinking Water; Water Quality; Human an d Ecological Health; 
Water Use Efficiency & Circular Economy; and Climate Resilience & Adaptation.  
Under the ANRF MAHA Water Programme, proposals are invited in a 
consortium mode involving multiple Principal Invest igators (PIs) and 

3 
 
institutions/laboratories from academia, research o rganisations, DSIR-SIRO-
registered research organisations, and eligible Sec tion 8 companies. 
Participation by at least one Start-up/MSME/Industr y partner is mandatory, with 
a cash contribution of 10% of the total project cos t. Related information is 
available on the website: 
https://anrfonline.in/ANRF/mahawp_anrf?HomePage=New. 
The Bharat WIN Portal has been operationalised to f acilitate participation 
of Start-ups/MSMEs and accelerate the development a nd deployment of 
innovative water technologies. 
Further, the Jal Shakti Hackathon–2025 was organise d to encourage 
practical, scalable, and field-ready technologies t o address key water-sector 
challenges. 
Results of R&D in the water sector are shared with stakeholders, such as 
States & UTs, partner ministries and project implem enting agencies, for 
adoption and implementation as considered appropriate.

†3033. SHRI CHHOTELAL: 
 
 Will the Minister of POWER 
be pleased to state: 
 
(a)  whether electricity supply is not fully functional in several rural areas of 
Robertsganj Parliamentary Constituency including Sonbhadra district of Uttar 
Pradesh, if so, the details thereof; and  
 
(b)  the time by which complete and uninterrupted power supply is likely to be 
made available across Robertsganj Parliamentary Constituency? 
 
A N S W E R 
 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF POWER  
 
(SHRI SHRIPAD NAIK)  
 
(a) & (b) : Electricity is a concurrent subject and power distribution is handled by 
distribution utilities that function under the guidance of their respective State 
Electricity Regulatory Commission (SERC) and State Government. 
 
Further, as per the Electricity (Rig hts of Consumers) Rules, 2020, the 
distribution licensee shall supply 24x7 power to all consumers. However, the 
Commission may specify lower hours of supply for some categories of consumers. 
As informed by the State of Uttar Pradesh, electricity supply is being provided 
according to the roster in rural areas of Robertsganj Lok Sabha Constituency 
including Sonbhadra area. 
 
 
 
Government of India (GoI) has supplemented the efforts of the States in 
providing access to quality power earlier through schemes like Deen Dayal 
Upadhyaya Gram Jyoti Yojana (DDUGJY) launched in 2014, Pradhan Mantri Sahaj 
Bijli Har Ghar Yojana (SAUBHAGYA) launched in Oc tober 2017, and currently 
under the Revamped Distribution Sector Scheme (RDSS) launched in July 2021.

As reported by the States/UTs, all the inhabited un -electrified census 
villages in the country were electrified by 28 thApril, 2018. Under DDUGJY and 
thereafter during SAUBHAGYA, as reported by all States/UTs, electrification of all 
willing households was completed. Both the schemes stand closed as on 
31.03.2022. 
 
Under RDSS, works amounting to Rs . 2.84 lakh Cr have been sanctioned 
across the country for loss reduction infrastructure and smart metering works. 
This includes Rs. 40,739 Cr for the State of Uttar Pradesh including Rs. 21,782 Cr 
for loss reduction infrastructure works and Rs. 18,956 Cr for smart metering 
works. For the Lok Sabha con stituency of Robertsganj, loss reduction 
infrastructure works amounting to Rs.227.78 Cr and smart metering works 
amounting to Rs. 183.37 Cr have been sanctioned. 
 
The sanctioned loss reduction infrastructure works include upgradation 
and augmentation of substations, installation of distribution transformers (DTs), 
upgradation of DTs, replacement of old conductors, feeder bifurcation and 
segregation, network strengthening, and cabling works. 
 
The execution of the above works would improve the quality of powe r 
supply including in rural areas. The sunset period of the scheme is till 31.03.2028.

LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 3035 
TO BE ANSWERED ON AUGUST 06, 2026 
 
PEDESTRIAN INFRASTRUCTURE 
NO. 3035 THIRU DR. S JAGATHRATCHAKAN: 
Will the Minister of HOUSING AND URBAN AFFAIRS be pleased to state: 
(a) whether the Government is  aware of the concerns relating to 
inadequate pedestrian infrastructure, unsafe footpaths, traffic 
congestion and rising dependence on private vehicles affecting 
urban mobility and equitable access across cities in the country 
and if so, the details thereof; 
(b)  the steps taken by the Government to promote walkable cities 
through pedestrian-friendly roads, cycling infrastructure, integrated 
public transport systems and improved last -mile connectivity under 
urban development programmes; 
(c)  the progress made by the Government in expanding non- motorized 
transport facilities, accessible footpaths, street safety measures 
and inclusive mobility infrastructure for women, elderly citizens 
and differently able persons in urban areas; and  
(d)  whether the Government has assessed the implications of 
continued prioriti sation of motor vehicle infrastructure over 
pedestrian and public transport systems in densely populated cities 
and if so, the details thereof? 
 
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE 
MINISTRY OF HOUSING AND URBAN AFFAIRS 
(SHRI TOKHAN SAHU) 
 
(a): As per the Twelfth Schedule of the Constitution of India, urban 
planning, including planning and provision of roads, footpaths and urban 
transport infrastructure, is a function of Urban Local Bodies 
(ULBs)/Urban Development Authorities. The respective State 
Governments/Union Territories and ULBs are, therefore, responsible for 
assessing local mobility conditions and for planning, developing, 
maintaining and enforcing provisions relating to pedestrian pathways, 
cycling infrastructure, street safety, public transport and last -mile 
connectivity. The Government of India supplements their efforts 
through policies, advisories, technical guidelines, schematic 
interventions and financial assistance. 
…2/- 

-2- 
(b) to (d): The Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs has published the 
Urban and Regional Development Plans Formulation and 
Implementation (URDPFI) Guidelines, 2014, the National Urban 
Transport Policy, 2006 and the Metro Rail Policy, 2017, which 
encourage integrated land- use and transport planning, pedestrian-  and 
cycle-friendly development, prioritisation of public transport and 
provision of adequate non- motorised transport infrastructure. The 
URDPFI Guidelines specifically recognise last -mile connectivity as an 
integral element of the Chapter 4 Regional Planning A pproach under 
Section 4.5.1 and address non- motorised transport and accessibility to 
public transport as part of Chapter – 6 Sustainability Guidelines, 
sustainable urban transport planning under Section 6.1.3. 
Chapter -7 Simplified Planning Techniques -  Section 7.3.5 and Table 7.4 
of the URDPFI Guidelines provide for surveys of pedestrian facilities, 
non-motorised vehicle infrastructure, public transport and overall 
mobility patterns as part of the plan- preparation process. Chapter -8 
Infrastructure Planning, Sections 8.2.3 and 8.2.4 prescribe planning and 
design standards for footpaths and cycle/non- motorised vehicle tracks. 
Further, under the Atal Mission for Rejuvenation and Urban 
Transformation (AMRUT), non-motorised urban transport was one of the 
thrust areas. So far, 431 km of pedestrian pathways/walkways and 43 
km of dedicated cycle tracks have been created under the Mission.  
Under the PM -eBus Sewa Scheme, the Government has sanctioned 
10,000 electric buses across more than 100 cities to augment city bus 
services, improve public transport accessibility, strengthen first - and 
last-mile connectivity, encourage greater use of public transport, and 
promote sustainable, clean, energy -efficient urban mobility and reduce 
dependence on private vehicles.  
Chapter -8 Infrastructure Planning, Section 8.2.15 of the URDPFI 
Guidelines, relating to Transit -Oriented Development and mass transit, 
advocates an integrated public transport system combining different 
modes and services through interchanges and feeder services, 
rationalisation of existing services and improved passenger dispersal at 
transport terminals. The Ministry also supports States and cities 
through the Scheme for Special Assistance to States for Capital 
Investment for strengthening the urban planning ecosystem. Under its 
Transit-Oriented Development component, capital incentives have been 
provided for notification and implementation of TOD corridors. So far, 
39 TOD corridors have been draft /final notified in eight States, enabling 
higher Floor Area Ratio/floors, increased density within TOD zones and 
improved last-mile connectivity.

(b) Water being a State subject, responsibility for  groundwater management 
including improving groundwater quality and mitigat ing contamination such as 
nitrate contamination, primarily rests with the res pective State Governments. 
However, the Central Government supplements the eff orts of the States 
through technical guidance, scientific inputs and v arious schemes and 
programmes. 
CGWB regularly monitors groundwater quality and dis seminates the 
monitoring data through Ground Water Quality Report s, Ground Water Quality 
Bulletins and fortnightly Ground Water Quality Alerts. The data are shared with 
the concerned State Governments and other stakehold ers to facilitate 
identification of contaminated areas including nitr ate-affected areas and 
planning of appropriate mitigation and groundwater management measures. 
To minimise nitrate loading at source, Government i s implementing the 
Soil Health Management  and Soil Health Card Scheme s under the National 
Project on Soil Health and Fertility of the Nationa l Mission for Sustainable 
Agriculture, which promote soil test-based and bala nced application of 
fertilisers. In addition, Natural Farming is being promoted since 2019-20 
through the Bharatiya Prakritik Krishi Paddhati (BP KP) under the 
Paramparagat Krishi Vikas Yojana (PKVY), which emph asises exclusion of 
synthetic chemical inputs and promotes on-farm biom ass recycling, biomass 
mulching, and use of cow dung-urine formulations an d other plant-based 
preparations. 
Further, Government of India promotes groundwater r echarge and water 
conservation through initiatives such as the Jal Sh akti Abhiyan (JSA), Jal 
Sanchay Jan Bhagidari (JSJB), Mission Amrit Sarovar  and Atal Mission for 

3 
 
Rejuvenation and Urban Transformation (AMRUT) 2.0, etc. Enhanced 
groundwater recharge can facilitate dilution and at tenuation of nitrate 
contamination and together with measures such as aw areness generation on 
the environmental impacts of excessive fertiliser u se, soil test-based and 
need-based fertiliser application, precision farmin g, integrated nutrient 
management and adoption of organic farming and orga nic manure-based 
practices, wherever feasible, contributes to reduci ng nitrate contamination in 
groundwater. 
  
(c) Realizing the significance of having high frequency data on ground water on 
near real time basis, this Ministry has taken up th e process of installing Digital 
Water Level Recorders (DWLRs) with telemetry system s throughout the 
country under its various schemes and projects like  Ground Water 
Management & Regulation (GWM &R) Scheme, Atal Bhuja l Yojana etc. The 
state governments had also funded for carrying out the said activity under 
National Hydrology Project(NHP). So far, around 24, 000 DWLRs have been 
installed across the country under the above said s chemes which facilitate 
near real-time access to ground water related data. 
(d) Water being a State subject, sustainable develo pment and management of 
groundwater resources is primarily the responsibili ty of the State 
Governments. However, the Central Government facili tates the efforts of the 
State Governments by way of technical and financial  assistance through its 
various schemes and projects. In this direction, th e important steps taken by

entries.t: Inadequate Air Connectivity from Sri Guru Ram Dass Jee International Airport
entries.head:
GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF CIVIL AVIATION 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. : 3042 
 ( TO BE ANSWERED ON THE  6th August 2026 )  
INADEQUATE AIR CONNECTIVITY FROM SRI GURU RAM DASS 
JEE INTERNATIONAL AIRPORT 
3042.    SHRI GURJEET SINGH AUJLA  
                
Will the Minister of CIVIL AVIATION 
be pleased to state:- 
(a) whether the Government is aware of the severe hardships faced by 
passengers, particularly the large Punjabi diaspora, due to the lack of suffici ent 
direct international flights from Sri Guru Ram Dass Jee International Airport, 
Amritsar, especially to Canada and if so, the details thereof; 
 
(b) whether any concrete steps are proposed to establish direct flight 
connectivity between Amritsar and Cana da to eliminate the financial and 
operational inconvenience of transit travel via Delhi or foreign hubs, if so, the 
details thereof; 
 
(c) whether the Government has taken note of the inadequate direct domestic air 
connectivity from Amritsar to key strategi c and religious destinations, 
specifically the Northeast region, Patna Sahib, Nanded Sahib, Chennai and 
Jaipur; 
 
(d) if so, the details of the measures being taken to introduce direct domestic 
flights from Amritsar to these destinations for the convenience  of defence 
personnel stationed at the border, pilgrims, tourists, students and business 
travellers; and 
 
(e) the timeline by which the Government intends to enhance both international 
and domestic air connectivity at this major border, religious and econo mic hub 
to match its strategic importance? 
ANSWER 
Minister of State in the Ministry of CIVIL AVIATION       
(Shri Murlidhar Mohol) 

(a) to (e): International flight operations are governed by bilateral Air Services 
Agreement (ASA) between India and the respective country. In accordance with 
ASA, Indian designated carriers are free to mount operations to/from any 
international airport including Amritsar to foreign destinations such as Canada 
as per mutually agreed capacity limits, while any designated foreign airline can 
operate to/from a point in India if it is designated as a point of call in the ASA. 
At present, direct international connectivity to Sharjah, Birmingham, London, 
Kuala Lumpur, Dubai, Doha and Singapore is available from Amritsar Airport. 
 
Ministry of Civil Aviation has launched Hub & Spoke operations to provide 
seamless international connectivity to passengers from Tier-II and Tier-III cities 
through Indian hub airports. As part of the phased expansion of the initiative, 
Hub & Spoke operations  from Amritsar Airport were launched on 28 July, 
2026. Under this initiative, international passengers complete check -in, 
immigration and customs formalities at the originating spoke airport, such as 
Amritsar, and thereafter travel seamlessly through the d esignated hub airport to 
their international destinations including Canada. 
 
The start of domestic or international flights from any point in India is purely a 
commercial decision of scheduled airlines on the basis of passenger demand, 
availability of slots, economic viability of the route and other associated factors. 
The Government provides an enabling environment for growth of civil aviation 
sector but does not interfere in the operational plans of the airlines. 
******

(iv)  Pradhan Mantri Mudra Yojana (PMMY) facilit ates collateral-free institutional credit of up to

entrepreneurs from aspirational, hilly, border and other lesser developed regions, including those in

(ii) Women-owned enterprises are eligible  for 90% guarantee coverage and a 10% concession in

at least 3% of their annual pr ocurement from women-owned MSEs under Public Procurement

MINISTRY OF FOOD PROCESSING INDUSTRIES

 Schemes relating to Cold-chain Development  
  
 3044. Shri Sanjay Dina Patil:  
  
 Will the Minister of FOOD PROCESSING INDUSTRIES be pleased to state: 
  
(a) whether the Government has reviewed the implementation of schemes relating to cold-chain 
development, food preservation, warehousing and integrated food parks serving in Mumbai 
during the last three years and if so, the details thereof; 
(b) the details of projects sanctioned, funds allocated and infrastructure created to improve 
handling, storage, transportation and processing of perishable agricultural and marine 
products supplied to Mumbai; 
(c) whether the Government has assessed the impact of these initiatives on reducing food 
wastage, improving farmer income and ensuring availability of quality food products in 
Mumbai; if so, the details thereof; and  
(d) the measures taken or proposed to be taken to further strengthen food supply chains, food 
safety standards and modern processing infrastructure serving Mumbai?  
 
  ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF FOOD PROCESSING INDUSTRIES 
(SHRI CHIRAG PASWAN) 
  
(a)  The Ministry of Food Processing Industries (MoFPI) has reviewed the implementation 
of the component schemes under the Pradhan Mantri Kisan SAMPADA Yojana (PMKSY), 
which support the establishment of integrated cold chain and value addition infrastructure, 
Mega Food Parks, Agro Processing Clusters and food processing units, thereby facilitating the 
creation of cold storage, warehousing, food processing and food preservation infrastructure at 
various levels during the last three years. The implementation of projects approved under the 
component schemes of PMKSY has been closely monitored by the Programme Management 
Agencies (PMAs) engaged by the Ministry. Further, the Technical Committee (TC) and the 
Project Approval Committee (PAC) constituted under the respective schemes have periodically 
reviewed the implementation of ongoing projects approved across the country, including those 
in the State of Maharashtra, which serve the Mumbai region, during the last three years. 
(b)   As of 30.06.2026, a total of 204 food processing projects has been sanctioned in the 
State of Maharashtra under the component schemes of the Pradhan Mantri Kisan SAMPADA 
Yojana (PMKSY) with a total approved grant-in-aid of ₹1,241.54 crore. These projects 
facilitate the creation of cold storage capacity of 2.98 lakh MT for preservation of perishable 
agricultural raw materials and processed products and the procurement of 403 reefer vehicles/ 
agri-logistics for preservation and transportation of perishable agricultural raw materials and 

finished processed products. The implementation of these 204 projects may lead to creation of 
food preservation capacity of 10.04 lakh MT per annum and food processing capacity of 89.08 
lakh MT per annum in the State of Maharashtra. The infrastructure created under these projects 
may facilitate in strengthening the supply chain for perishable agricultural and marine products 
across the State, including the Mumbai region. 
(c)  MoFPI has conducted various assessments from time to time to identify the level of 
food processing and to estimate post-harvest losses for various agricultural produces in India. 
These assessments are based on primary data collection nationwide including Mumbai and 
provides crop-wise estimates of the level of food processing and post-harvest losses. However, 
so far, this Ministry has not undertaken any assessment specifically to identify the impact of 
these initiatives on reducing food wastage, improving farmer income and ensuring availability 
of quality food products. 
  
(d)  MoFPI provides financial assistance for setting up food processing projects under three 
Schemes, namely: (i) Pradhan Mantri Kisan SAMPADA Yojana (PMKSY), (ii) PM 
Formalisation of Micro Food Processing Enterprises (PMFME) Scheme, and (iii) Production 
Linked Incentive Scheme for Food Processing Industry (PLISFPI). These schemes aim to 
strengthen food supply chains, enhance food safety standards, and promote the development of 
modern food processing infrastructure nationwide, including the Mumbai region.

3049. SHRI ABHISHEK BANERJEE: 
 
पेĚोͧलयम और Ĥाकृ Ǔतक गैस मंğी 
Will the Minister of PETROLEUM AND NATURAL GAS be pleased to state: 
(a) the details of the number of complaints received by the Government, Oil Marketing 
Companies or Public Sector retail outlets regarding mileage loss, fuel system issues, engine 
damage, component replacement or warranty denial allegedly linked to E20 petrol, State-
wise, vehicle category-wise and year-wise; 
(b)  whether any mechanism exists for testing fuel samples in such complaints, if so, the details 
thereof; 
(c) the details of the number of complaints found valid, rejected or pending; and 
(d) whether any compensation, repair liability or consumer grievance mechanism has been 
prescribed for vehicles not originally certified for E20 use, if so, the details thereof? 
ANSWER 
पेĚोͧलयम और Ĥाकृ Ǔतक गैस मंğालय मɅ राÏय मंğी 
(Įी सुरेश गोपी) 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF PETROLEUM & NATURAL GAS  
 (SHRI SURESH GOPI) 
(a) to (d): The Ethanol Blended Petrol (EBP) Programme has been implemented through a 
phased, scientifically validated and consultative process involving NITI Aayog, automobile 
manufacturers, Oil Marketing Companies (OMCs), Automotive Research Association of India 
(ARAI), Society of Indian Automobile Manufacturers (SIAM), Indian Institute of Petroleum (IIP) 
and other technical institutions. 
 
Since ESY 2014–15, the programme has generated foreign exchange savings of over ₹1.97 lakh 
crore, substituted nearly 316 lakh metric tonnes of crude oil, avoided approximately 952 lakh metric 
tonnes of CO₂ emissions and generated more than ₹1.66 lakh crore in additional income for Indian 
farmers. 
 
Government has not received any widespread or substantiated complaints from vehicle 
manufacturers, automobile associations or consumer organisations regarding engine failure, fuel 
pump issues, corrosion, water contamination or other performance issues attributable to E20 fuel. 
Government has, however, taken note of certain concerns raised in media and social media, which 
have been scientifically examined. 
 
Extensive laboratory studies and field trials conducted by ARAI, SIAM, IOCL, IIP and automobile 
manufacturers covering parameters such as engine durability, drivability, startability, corrosion 
resistance, material compatibility, emissions and fuel efficiency have confirmed that E20 is safe for 
use under prescribed standards. 
These studies also established that legacy vehicles do not exhibit any significant variation in 
performance or abnormal wear and tear due to E20. 
 
These extensive laboratory studies, field validation and real-world operating experience have not 
established any widespread adverse impact on vehicle performance due to E20 fuel. 
  

 
 E15+ blended petrol has been in widespread use across the country for over three-and-a-half years 
and E19–E20 fuel for over two-and-a-half years. More than 20 crore two-wheelers and over 3 crore 
petrol cars have been operating on these blends without any verified evidence of widespread engine 
failure or abnormal wear attributable to E20 fuel. Manufacturer service data confirm that there is no 
abnormal corrosion, wear or reduction in vehicle life due to E20 fuel. Manufacturers continue to 
honour warranty obligations for vehicles using E20 fuel, providing further confidence in its safety 
and reliability. 
 
Accordingly, year-wise and State-wise details of such complaints are Nil. 
 
Ethanol Blended Motor Spirit (EBMS) supplied and sold through Retail Outlets (ROs) is ensured to 
conform to the applicable BIS specifications. Oil Marketing Companies (OMCs) have issued 
detailed Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) to dealerships covering the receipt, inspection, 
sampling, decantation and sale of EBMS at retail outlets. 
 
Further, to prevent any quality issues arising from water contamination, especially during the 
monsoon season, OMC officials conduct periodic water-ingress audits of Motor Spirit (MS) tanks at 
retail outlets. Dealers are also required to monitor water levels in MS tanks at regular intervals. In 
addition, Automated Tank Gauging (ATG) systems installed at retail outlets continuously monitor 
water levels in MS tanks. In the event water is detected beyond the prescribed limits, the automation 
system triggers an interlock mechanism, resulting in the automatic suspension of sales from the 
affected tank until corrective action is taken.  
 
These measures ensure that only quality-compliant fuel is dispensed to consumers. However, in case 
of any specific complaint regarding quality of fuel delivered from the retail outlet, sampling/ testing 
of the product samples drawn from the retail outlet is done and further necessary action on the 
established cases where samples are not meeting the norms is taken, as per the Marketing Discipline 
Guidelines.
