entries.t: Rehabilitation of Tribals affected by Ken-Betwa Link Project
entries.head:
GOVERNMENT OF INDIA  
MINISTRY OF TRIBAL AFFAIRS 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO-3052  
TO BE ANSWERED ON- 06/08/2026 
  
REHABILITATION OF TRIBALS AFFECTED BY KEN-BETWA LINK PROJECT  
  
3052. SHRI RAHUL GANDHI:  
          SHRI AJENDRA SINGH LODHI:  
  
Will the Minister of TRIBAL AFFAIRS be pleased to state: 
  
(a) the number of tribal families affected by the Ken-Betwa Link Project, the number fully and 
partially compensated and these declared ineligible for rehabilitation along with the reasons 
therefor, village-wise; 
  
(b) whether the Government has received or been referred any complaints of amounts recorded 
as disbursed but not having reached beneficiaries, if so, the number thereof and the action taken 
thereon; 
  
(c) the date-wise details of Gram Sabha meetings under the Forest Rights Act, including 
participation, signatures obtained and grievances received regarding consent, compensation 
and displacement and their disposal status; 
  
(d) the reasons for evicting tribal families without complying with the Stage-II Forest Clearance 
conditions; 
  
(e) whether the Government is considering including common resources in compensation, 
enhancing compensation and extending the rehabilitation cut-off date; and 
  
(f) whether the Government has taken cognisance of protesting tribal communities being 
evicted without dialogue, if so, the action taken thereon? 
  
ANSWER 
MINISTER OF STATE FOR TRIBAL AFFAIRS 
(SHRI DURGADAS UIKEY)  
                  
(a):  Ken Betwa Link Project Authority under Department of Water Resources, River 
Development and Ganga Rejuvenation, Ministry of Jal Shakti has informed that Land 
Acquisition and Rehabilitation and Resettlement activities are being undertaken by the State 
Governments.  
  

However, Ministry of Tribal Affairs (MoTA) is member of Steering and Monitoring 
committees of Ken-Betwa Link Project, which inter alia monitors the progress of implementation 
of Action plan of R&R of Project Affected Families (PAFs). Further, MoTA had given a clearance 
for R&R plan for Scheduled Tribes Project Affected Families (ST-PAF) of Ken-Betwa Link 
Project, Phase –I, wherein the proposal provided by the National Water Development Agency, 
(NWDA) in 2016, mentioned that the Ken-Betwa Link Project, Phase-I involves displacement of a 
total of 1,913 Project Affected Families (PAFs) (population 8,339) out of which a total of 648 
PAFs belong to Scheduled Tribes (ST).  
  
(b) & (f): MoTA has not received any complaint explicitly stating the issues of amounts recorded 
as disbursed but not having reached beneficiaries. However, Ministry of Tribal Affairs has received 
the various representations raising issues of displacement due to the Ken-Betwa River Link Project, 
which were examined and as the implementation of the FRA lies with the State Governments and 
UT Administration, these have been forwarded to the State Government of Madhya Pradesh and 
respective District Administrations for examination and necessary action. 
  
(c):  As implementation of Scheduled Tribes and Other Traditional Forest Dwellers (Recognition 
of Forest Rights) Act, 2006 (in short, FRA) lies with State Governments and UT Administrations, 
this data is not centrally maintained by MoTA. 
  
(d):   Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEFCC) has informed that they have 
accorded the Stage-II approvals to two proposals pertaining to Ken- Betwa link project in Madhya 
Pradesh on 03.10.2023 and 06.05.2021 inter-alia stipulating the following conditions: 
  
i. The State Government to ensure that the user agency implements the R&R Plan as per the 
R&R Policy of State Government in consonance with National R&R Policy, Government 
of India before the commencement of the project work. The said R&R Plan is monitored 
by the State Government / Regional Office of MoEF&CC along with indicators for 
monitoring and expected observable milestones; 
ii. The State Government to ensure that compliance of Scheduled Tribes and Other Traditional 
Forest Dwellers (Recognition of Forest Rights) Act, 2006 has been completed in 
accordance with the relevant Rules and Guidelines issued by the MoEF&CC in this regard, 
before handing over of forest land to the user agency 
  
Further, provisions of Rule No. 11 (7) of the Van (Sanrakshan evam Samvardhan) Rules, 2023 
provides that the State Government or Union territory Administration can issue order for diversion, 
assignment of lease or de-reservation, as the case may be, only after  receiving the ‘Final’ approval 
of the Central Government under sub-section (1) of section 2 of the Adhiniyam, and after fulfilment 
and compliance of the provisions of all other Acts and rules made thereunder, as applicable 
including ensuring settlement of rights under the Scheduled Tribes and Other Traditional Forest 
Dwellers (Recognition of Forest Rights) Act, 2006 (2 of 2007). 
 
Moreover, MoTA has been exhorting the State Governments and UT Administrations to

entries.head:
GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF CIVIL AVIATION 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. : 3054 
 ( TO BE ANSWERED ON THE  6th August 2026 )  
EXPANSION OF AIRPORT INFRASTRUCTURE IN TAMIL NADU  
3054.    SHRI SELVAM G                            
             DR. RANI SRIKUMAR                       
             SHRI C N ANNADURAI      
                  
Will the Minister of CIVIL AVIATION 
be pleased to state:- 
(a) whether the Government has undertaken or proposes to undertake 
expansion, modernization and capacity enhancement of airports in Tamil Nadu 
and if so, the details thereof, airport-wise; 
(b) the details of the projects approved or under consideration including new 
terminals, runway expansion, passenger amenities, cargo infrastructure and 
improved air connectivity along with the expected timeline fixed for 
completion; 
(c) the likely impact of these airport expansion projects on regional 
connectivity, tourism, trade, investment and employment in Tamil Nadu; and 
(d) the further measures proposed t o strengthen aviation infrastructure and 
enhance air connectivity across the State? 
ANSWER 
Minister of State in the Ministry of CIVIL AVIATION       
(Shri Murlidhar Mohol) 
(a) & (b): Upgradation, modernization and capacity enhancement of existing 
airports is a continuous process and is undertaken by the Airports Authority of 
India (AAI) and other airport operators from time to time based on passenger 
demand forecasts, operational requirements, demand from airlines, availability 
of land, financial viability, statutory and regulatory clearances, and other site -
specific factors. 
 
Major expansion and development works at airports in Tamil Nadu include: 
 
Chennai Airport: Phase -II modernization at a cost of 2,467 crore to enhance 
passenger handling capacity from 30 Million Passengers Per Annum (MPPA) to 
35 MPPA, along with storm water drain modification (209.01 crore), 

refurbishment of Terminal -1 (81.80 crore) and development of airside  
infrastructure (480.06 crore). 
 
Tiruchirappalli Airport: Construction of a Ne w ATC Tower -cum-Technical 
Block at a cost of 80.17 crore. 
 
Coimbatore Airport: Construction of the boundary wall on newly acquired land 
at a cost of 51.31 crore and addition and alteration to the existing terminal 
building at a cost of 13.71 crore. 
 
The timeline for completion of the airport projects depends upon many factors 
such as land acquisition, availability of mandatory clearances, financial closure 
etc. 
 
(c) & (d): International Civil Aviation Organisation (ICAO) study titled 
'Economic Benefits of Civil Aviation: Ripples of Prosperity', shows that the air 
connectivity has an economic multiplier of 3.25 an d employment multiplier of 
6.1. 
 
In the state of Tamil Nadu, Salem Airport has been developed and 
operationalised whereas Vellore and Neyveli are being developed under the 
UDAN Scheme. The next phase of the scheme includes development of 100 
airports, connecting 120 destinations across the country including Tamil Nadu.

MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF PETROLEUM AND NATURAL GAS 
(SHRI SURESH GOPI) 
 
(a) to (e): India has surplus production of petroleum products to cater to the domestic needs. 
During 2025-26, 284.9 MMT of Petroleum Products were produced against the domestic 
consumption of 241.6 MMT.  The distribution of petroleum products like MS, HSD, ATF, 
LPG, CNG, PNG etc. is continuously monitored to ensure uninterrupted supplies through a 
robust supply chain management system across the country including Maharashtra.  
The strengthening of depot and terminal infrastructure, storage augmentation and 
enhancement of transportation facilities, augmenting the Retail Outlets, LPG distributorships, 
CNG stations and alternate fuel infrastructure to improve availability and distribution of 
petroleum products is a continuous process. 
The retail outlets are set up by OMCs at identified locations based on feasibility studies.   
Locations found to be having sufficient potential are included in the roster of state marketing 

plan for setting up of Retail Outlets. For appointment of LPG distributorships also, feasibility 
study is carried out based on available refill sales potential that can sustain economically 
viable operation. Viable locations are advertised accordingly.  
 
Further, establishment of Compressed Natural Gas (CNG) stations and the provision of Piped 
Natural Gas (PNG) connections to households are undertaken as part of the development of 
the City Gas Distribution (CGD) network. These activities are carried out by entities 
authorized by the Petroleum and Natural Gas Regulatory Board (PNGRB). 
PSU OMCs have commissioned 1143 new Retail Outlets and 18 new LPG distributorships 
during last 3 financial years in Maharashtra. CGD entities have released 17.18 lakh DPNG 
(Domestic) connections, installed 507 new CNG stations and laid 8,736 Inch-KM pipeline 
during last 3 financial years in Maharashtra. 
In the State of Maharashtra, the Petroleum and Natural Gas Regulatory Board (PNGRB) has 
authorized 22 Geographical Areas (GAs), including one GA spanning Madhya Pradesh and 
Maharashtra and one GA spanning Gujarat and Maharashtra, for the development of the City 
Gas Distribution (CGD) network. Collectively, these authorized GAs cover all districts of the 
State. 
Details of important infrastructure projects commissioned in the state of Maharashtra during 
last three years are given at Annexure. 
Further, the Government has notified a comprehensive control order dated 24.03.2026 under 
the Essential Commodities Act, 1955 to facilitate time-bound expansion of pipeline 
infrastructure across the country, especially CGD. The Order provides a uniform framework 
for grant of right of way (RoW) and permissions by mandating strict timelines, enabling 
deemed approvals in case of delays, and prohibiting imposition of unauthorized charges by 
public authorities.  
To strengthen energy security and minimise supply risks, India has significantly diversified its 
crude oil sourcing portfolio from 27 countries to 41 countries and expanded LNG and LPG 
sourcing to 15 countries thereby reducing the dependence on any particular country, region or 
transit route and enhanced India's ability to manage supply disruptions and market volatility. 
Government, in consultation with Public Sector Oil and Gas Companies and other 
stakeholders, continuously assesses global supply conditions and acts appropriately to ensure 
uninterrupted availability of crude oil, LNG and petroleum products.

electricity peak demand was around 12 % as compared to corresponding period 
last year. As on date, the all -time high All -India peak demand of 270.8 GW was 
successfully met in the month of May 2026, and in July, 2026.  The State-wise and 
month-wise ‘Power Supply Position’ from January, 2026 to June, 2026 including 
Chhattisgarh in terms of Energy is given at Annexure-I. The ‘energy supplied’ has 
been commensurate with the ‘energy requirement’ with only a marginal gap which 
is generally on a ccount of constraints in the State transmission / distribution 
network. 

The Government has taken following measures to strengthen power 
infrastructure in view of the increasing duration, frequency and intensity of 
heatwaves due to climate change:    
 
1. Generation and Storage Planning: 
 
(i) As per National Electricity Plan (Generation), installed generation capacity in 
2031-32 is likely to be 874 GW. With a view to ensure generation capacity 
remains ahead of projected demand, all the States, in  consultation with CEA, 
have prepared their “Resource Adequacy Plans (RAPs)”, which are dynamic 10-
year rolling plans and includes power generation as well as power procurement 
planning. 
 
(ii) All the States were advised to initiate process for creating/ contra cting 
generation capacities; from all generation sources, as per their Resource 
Adequacy Plans. 
 
(iii) In order to augment the power generation capacity, the Government of 
India has initiated following capacity addition programme:  
 
a.  Thermal Capacity Addition: The projected thermal (coal and lignite) 
capacity requirement by the year 2035 –36 is estimated at approximately 
3,15,000 MW as against the 2,11,855 MW installed capacity as on 
31.03.2023. To meet this requirement, Ministry of Power has envisaged to 
set up an additional minimum 1,05,000 MW coal and lignite based thermal 
capacity. 
 
  Accordingly, Thermal capacities of around 21,080 MW have been 
commissioned since April 2023 till 30.06.2026. In addition, 47,545 MW of 
thermal capacity (including 4,845 MW of stressed thermal power projects) 
is currently under construction. The contracts of 16,000 MW have been 
awarded and are due for construction.  
 
 b.  Central Electricity Authority (CEA) has projected hydro power 
capacity addition of about 16,448 MW during the  period 2026–27 to 2031–
32. Of this, 400 MW has been commissioned as on 30.06.2026 and 12,973 
MW are presently under construction. 
  
 c.  Nuclear Capacity Addition: 8,000 MW of Nuclear Capacity is under 
construction and targeted to be completed by 2031-32. 5,600 MW of Nuclear 
Capacity is under various stages of planning and approval. 
 
 d.  Renewables Capacity Addition: 1,47,720 MW Renewable Capacity 
including 119,580 MW of Solar (including Hybrid -Solar) and 27,720 MW of 
Wind (including Hybrid -wind) is under  construction while 47,830 MW of 
Renewable Capacity including 44,440 MW of Solar is at various stages of 
planning and targeted to be completed by 2029-30.   
 

    e.  Addition of Energy Storage Systems:  As on 30.06.2026, 15,870 
MW/95,220 MWh Pumped Storage  Projects (PSPs) are under construction. 
Further, a total of 6,580 MW/39,480 MWh capacity of Pumped Storage 
Projects (PSPs) are concurred and yet to be taken up for construction. As 
on 30.06.2026, 15,754 MW / 42,530 MWh Battery Energy Storage System 
(BESS) capacity are under construction, 11,747 MW / 38,425 MWh has been 
awarded and 19,192 MW / 67,574 MWh BESS capacity are under tendering 
stage. 
 
2. Promotion of Renewable Energy (RE) Generation:  
 
(i) 100% Inter State Transmission System (ISTS) charges have been waived 
for inter -state sale of solar and wind power

DOMESTIC FOOD MARKET IN TAMIL NADU 
 
3061. MS. S JOTHIMANI: 
 
Will the Minister of FOOD PROCESSING INDUSTRIES be pleased to state: 
 
(a)  the specific initiatives being implemented by the Union Government to assist the State 
of Tamil Nadu in capitalizing on the projected forty-seven per cent growth of India's 
domestic food market, which is expected to reach 1,274 billion US Dollars by 2027; 
 
(b)  the details of the measures being taken by the Union Government to support 
innovative startups in Tamil Nadu’s food processing sector to enhance technological 
advancements and economic growth; and 
 
(c)  whether there are any specific financial assistance schemes or incentives designated 
for Tamil Nadu’s food processing industries to boost exports and infrastructure 
development and if so, the details thereof? 
 
ANSWER 
 
THE MINISTER OF FOOD PROCESSING INDUSTRIES 
(SHRI CHIRAG PASWAN) 
 
(a): In order to ensure overall development of food processing sector, Ministry of Food 
Processing Industries (MoFPI) has been incentivizing setting up/expansion of related 
infrastructure through its Central Sector Umbrella Scheme - Pradhan Mantri Kisan SAMPADA 
Yojana (PMKSY); Central Sector Scheme - Production Linked Incentive Scheme for Food 
Processing Industry (PLISFPI) and Centrally Sponsored Scheme - PM Formalization of Micro 
Food Processing Enterprises (PMFME). These schemes are demand driven and are 
implemented across the country including the State of Tamil Nadu.   
(b): Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT), Government of India, 
launched the Startup India initiative on 16th January 2016 to build a strong ecosystem for 
nurturing innovation, supporting startups and encouraging investments in the startup ecosystem 
of the country. As on 30th June 2026, a total of 9,949 entities have been recognized as startups 
by DPIIT in the Food Processing sector across the country. Of these, 709 entities have been 
recognized as startups in the Food Processing sector in the State of Tamil Nadu. 
Under the Startup India initiative, the Government constantly undertakes various efforts 
to support startups across industries and sectors. The flagship Schemes namely, Fund of Funds 

for Startups (FFS), Startup India Seed Fund Scheme (SISFS) and Credit Guarantee Scheme for 
Startups (CGSS) support startups across sectors at various stages of their business cycle. 
Under FFS, a total number of 65 startups from Tamil Nadu have been supported with a 
cumulative investment of Rs.1,420.85 crore (as on June 30, 2026), out of which 4 startups from 
food & beverages sector have been supported with an aggregate amount of Rs. 224.38 crore. 
SISFS provides financial assistance to seed stage startups through incubators. SISFS is 
implemented from 1st April 2021. Under the SISFS, supported incubators have approved Rs. 
69.16 crore to 450 startups from Tamil Nadu. Out of this, specifically in the Food Processing 
sector, 21 startups have been supported and a total of Rs.  21.2 crore has been approved to these 
startups under SISFS as on 30th June 2026. CGSS is implemented to enable credit access 
through debt funding to startups through eligible financial institutions [Member Institutes 
(MIs)]. CGSS is operationalized by the National Credit Guarantee Trustee Company (NCGTC) 
Limited and has been operationalized from 1st April 2023. 48 loans amounting to Rs. 187.60 
crore have been guaranteed in Tamil Nadu as on June 30, 2026 under CGSS. Of this, a loan 
has been guaranteed amounting to Rs. 1.5 crore in food processing sector as on June 30, 2026 
in the State of Tamil Nadu. 
In addition to the above, MoFPI also extends support to innovative startups across the 
country, including those in Tamil Nadu, through its schemes. Under the PMFME Scheme, a 
total of 80 Incubation Centres have been approved and established across the country, out of 
which 04 Incubation Centres are operational in Tamil Nadu, for providing training in food

3062.  SMT. SUPRIYA SULE: 
DR. AMOL RAMSING KOLHE:

Will the Minister of MICRO, SMALL AND MEDIUM ENTERPRISES be pleased to state: 
 
(a)  whether the Khadi and Village Industries Commission (KVIC) has been organizing 'Khadi

details thereof; 
(b)  whether the Government proposes to organize similar programmes in Maharashtra and if so, 
the details thereof; 
(c)  the number of artisans, weavers and  other beneficiaries in Maharashtra who have been 
provided machines, toolkits and other assistance under the schemes of KVIC during the last three

ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE FOR MICRO, SMALL AND MEDIUM ENTERPRISES  
(SUSHRI SHOBHA KARANDLAJE) 
 
(a) & (b):  Under the Gramodyog Vikas Yojana (GVY), the Khadi  and Village Industries 
Commission (KVIC) imparts skill training to rural and traditional artisans in various village 
industries and also provides toolkits to enhance their productivity. As part of these initiatives, Khadi 
Rojgar Utsav Programmes has been organized by KVIC at Nasik and Wardha during FY 2025-2026 
to distribute toolkits to rural artisans. 
 
 
(c):  KVIC implements various KVI schemes and programmes for the development of Khadi and 
Village Industries across the country including in the State of Maharashtra. 
 
 Under the Khadi Vikas Yojana (KVY), the Modified Market Development Assistance 
(MMDA) component provides financial assistance to eligible Khadi artisans, while the 
Workshed Scheme for Khadi  Artisans provides financial assistance for the construction of 
individual and group worksheds. Under the MMDA component, 400 artisans were benefited 
in 2023 –24, 519 artisans in 2024 –25, and 360 artisans in 2025 –26. Further, under the 
Workshed Scheme for Khadi Artisans, 40 artisans were benefited in 2024 –25 and 30 artisans 
in 2025–26. 

 
 
: 2 : 
 
 Under Gramodyog Vikas Yojana (GVY), the district-wise number of artisans benefitted in 
Maharashtra State during the last three years and current year are given at Annexure-I. 
 
 
(d): The Ministry of MSME implements various schemes across the country, including Vidarbha, 
Marathwada and the tribal areas of Maharashtra, to promote employment and entrepreneurship 
among traditional artisans, women and youth. These schemes provide skill training, financial 
assistance, modern tools and equipment, marketing support and handholding support to facilitate 
self-employment and sustainable livelihood opportunities. 
 
 Skill  training is provided to artisans and unemployed youth under various trades, including 
Khadi spinning and weaving, bee -keeping, food processing, tailoring, embroidery, pottery, 
agarbatti and candle making , and other village industries as well as to the artisans and 
craftspeople engaged in 18 traditional trades, including carpentry, bl acksmithy, goldsmithy, 
masonry, barbering and fishing net making etc. 
 
 Financial support is also provided through PMEGP and PM Vishwakarma to promote self -
employment and entrepreneurship. Under PMEGP, Margin Money subsidy of up to 35% of 
the project cost is provided for eligible beneficiaries, with higher subsidy for Special 
Categories as per Scheme g uidelines. Under PM Vishwakarma, collateral -free Enterprise 
Development Loans of up to ₹3 lakh are provided in two tranches at a concessional interest 
rate of 5%. 
 
 Marketing support, including quality certification, branding, onboarding on e -commerce 
platforms such as GeM, advertising, publicity, exhibitions and buyer-seller meets, is provided 
to enhance market access and business opportunities for artisans and entrepreneurs. 
 
 
 
(e):  State-wise funds are not allocated under KVIC programmes, however, a fund of Rs.2402.99 
lakh was utilized in the State of Maharashtra during the last three years and current year under 
various KVI activities.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS 
  
 LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION No. 3063

NATIONAL HIGHWAYS PROJECTS IN TAMIL NADU 
  
3063.    SHRI RAJA A. 
  
Will the Minister of ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS  
सड़क परिवहन औि िाजमार्ग मंत्री 
(a) the total number and the details of National Highway projects 
currently under construction in the State of Tamil Nadu and the 
number of these projects that are delayed beyond the stipulated 
timelines, project-wise;  
(b) the de tails regarding causes of delays in National Highway 
projects in Tamil Nadu, such as cost escalation, environmental 
clearances, negligence of contractors, etc.; and  
(c) the concrete and time -bound steps taken by the Government so 
far to ensure timely comp letion of the delayed projects in the State 
with details thereof? 
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS 
  
(SHRI NITIN JAIRAM GADKARI) 
(a) & (b) At present, 50 National Highway projects are under 
construction in the State of Tamil Nadu. Of these, 33 projects are 
under execution beyond their originally stipulated completion 
timelines. The delays are attributable to one or more of the 
following factors, depending upon the project: 
 
i. land acquisition and Right of Way (RoW) related issues; 
 

ii. utility shifting and statutory/ railway/ forest/ environmental  
clearances; 
 
iii. contractor-related issues such as inadequate resource 
mobilisation, slow progress and financial constraints; 
 
iv. delay in procurement of construction materials such as borrow 
earth/fly ash; 
 
v. change in project scope/design and other technical  
requirements; 
 
vi. adverse weather conditions and other force majeure events;  
and 
 
vii. local/site-speciﬁc issues including law and order, public 
demands and other implementation constraints. 
 
(c) The Government has taken various measures to facilitate 
timely completion of National Highway projects and to minimise 
delays in projects, including: 
 
i. Continuous coordination with the State Government and other 
concerned agencies for e xpeditious resolution of issues relating to 
land acquisition, utility shifting and statutory clearances. 
 
ii. Regular review of project progress with all stakeholders at 
various levels, for timely resolution of implementation bottlenecks. 
 
iii. Escalation of unresolved issues to appropriate forums such as 
the Project Monitoring Group (PMG) and PRAGATI for expeditious  
resolution. 
 
Based on experience gained from execution of NH projects, 
the Government has taken several measures to minimise the delay 
in future projects like: 
 
i. Award of works only after ensuring availability of at least 90% 
encumbrance-free Right of Way (RoW). 
ii. Ensuring that major statutory clearances, approvals and 
permissions are obtained before award of works, to the extent  
feasible.

3066.   Shri SRIBHARAT MATHUKUMILLI: 
Will the Minister of JAL SHAKTI be pleased to state: 
(a) the number of dams and reservoirs for which saf ety assessments have been 
completed under the Dam Safety Act, 2021, State-wis e against the total number of 
specified dams in each State including the status o f MeghadriGedda, Raiwada, 
Tatipudi and Mudasarlova reservoirs in Andhra Pradesh; 
(b) whether the Government has undertaken any spillway repair, structural audit or 
rehabilitation work at MeghadriGedda, Raiwada, Tati pudi and Mudasarlova 
reservoirs and if so, the details thereof; 
(c) the estimated annual water loss including losse s due to evaporation and 
reduced storage capacity, attributable to the absen ce of such repairs at each of 
these reservoirs; and 
(d) the timeline by which the remaining safety assessments and spillway audits are 
proposed to be completed across the country and spe cifically for Visakhapatnam 
in view of the Government’s December 2026 target fo r pending dam safety 
evaluations? 
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR JAL SHAKTI  
(SHRI RAJ BHUSHAN CHOUDHARY) 
(a)  The responsibility for ensuring the safety of d ams, including their operation, 
maintenance and surveillance, rests primarily with the respective dam owners, 
which are predominantly the State Governments and C entral/State Public Sector 
Undertakings. 
Further, in accordance with Section 31 of the Dam S afety Act, 2021, every 
owner of a specified dam is required to carry out a nnual pre-monsoon and post-

2 
 
monsoon inspections through its Dam Safety Unit and  submit the inspection 
reports to the concerned State Dam Safety Organisat ion (SDSO). The SDSO 
examines these reports and communicates its observa tions regarding the safety 
status of the dam, deficiencies noticed and remedia l measures required, if any, to 
the concerned dam owner. 
As per the information furnished by the National Da m Safety Authority 
(NDSA), pre-monsoon inspections for the year 2026 h ave been completed in 
respect of 6,566 out of 6,598 completed and operati onal specified dams across the 
country. The State/UT-wise details are given at Annexure.  
In Andhra Pradesh, pre-monsoon inspections have bee n carried out for all 
150 specified dams, including MeghadriGedda, Raiwad a and Tatipudi 
reservoirs. Further, Mudasarlova does not fall under the category of specified dams 
under the Dam Safety Act, 2021. The Greater Visakha patnam Municipal 
Corporation is responsible for its upkeep and the r eservoir serves primarily as a 
source of drinking water. 
Moreover, under Section 38 of the Dam Safety Act, 2 021, every specified 
dam is required to undergo a Comprehensive Dam Safe ty Evaluation (CDSE) 
through an Independent Panel of Experts. As informe d by the NDSA, Independent 
Panels of Experts have so far inspected 1,090 speci fied dams, and CDSE reports 
have been completed for 468 dams.

structural rehabilitation or rehabilitation works have been undertaken in respect of

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF HOUSING AND URBAN AFFAIRS

UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 3069 
TO BE ANSWERED ON AUGUST 06, 2026 
 
APPROVAL OF NORMS FOR HIGH RISE BUILDINGS 
 
NO. 3069 SHRI VARUN CHAUDHRY: 
Will the Minister of HOUSING AND URBAN AFFAIRS be pleased to state: 
(a) whether the Government has taken note of complaints from various 
parts of the country  alleging grant of statutory approvals to high- rise 
projects despite deficiencies in fire safety and environmental 
compliance and if so, the details thereof; 
(b) whether the Government has received representation in respect of 
any housing projects in Sector-50, Gurugram, Haryana, raising similar 
concerns regarding the grant of Fire No Objection Certificate (NOC), 
Occupation Certificate and Completion Certificate, if so, the details 
thereof and the responsibility fixed therein along with the action 
taken to resolve the issue project-wise and society-wise; 
(c) whether the Government has undertaken or proposes to undertake a 
review of the process  followed by the State authorities in granting 
such approvals in cases where serious  safety deficiencies  are 
subsequently noticed and if so, the details thereof; and 
(d) the details of the corrective measures taken/proposed to be taken to 
improve transparency, accountability and public safety in the 
approval process for high- rise projects  particularly in sector 50, 
Gurugram? 
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE 
MINISTRY OF HOUSING AND URBAN AFFAIRS 
(SHRI TOKHAN SAHU) 
(a) and (b): ‘Land’ and ‘Colonisation’ are State subjects. Further, as per the 
Twelfth Schedule of the Constitution of India, urban planning, regulation of 
land use and construction of buildings are functions of Urban Local 
Bodies/Urban Development Authorities. Accordingly, approval of building 
plans, issuance and renewal of Fire No Objection Certificates, grant of 
Occupation/Completion Certificates, inspection of buildings and 
enforcement against violations are undertaken by the concerned State 
Governments, Urban Local Bodies, Development Authorities and Fire 
Services in accordance with the applicable State Acts, rules, building bye-
laws and development control regulations. 
…2/- 

-2- 
Complaints relating to alleged deficiencies in fire safety, environmental 
compliance or grant of statutory approvals to individual high- rise projects 
are, therefore, examined and acted upon by the respective statutory 
authorities. No centralised project -wise data regarding such complaints 
and approvals is maintained by the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs. 
(c) and (d): The Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs has issued the Model 
Building Bye- Laws (MBBL), 2016  for guidance of States /Union Territories  
(UTs). The Chapter 11- Fire Protection and Fire Safety Requirements,  of 
the Model Building Bye-Laws contains provisions relating to fire protection 
and fire- safety requirements  and Chapter - 5 Provisions for High Rise 
Development, provides for Safety of High -rise developments .  These 
provisions are advisory in nature and become legally enforceable upon 
their adoption and notification by the respective State or local authority. 
The norms and standards for fire safety and their implementation are 
prescribed under the relevant State building bye- laws and development 
control regulations. Further, Part F - ‘Fire and Life Safety’ of the National 
Building Construction Standards 2026 (NBCS 2026) published by the 
Bureau of India Standards  contains provisions regarding fire prevention, 
life safety in relation to fire, and fire protection of buildings; apart from 
specific occupancy-wise requirements. Also, Part F provides the additional 
requirements for high- rise buildings with respect to fire and safety 
particularly with regards to planning, design, execution, maintenance and 
training.  
Further, the MBBL 2016 provides a model framework covering building-plan 
scrutiny, fire and life safety, structural safety, disaster resilience, 
environmental safeguards and grant of occupancy -related approvals.  
States/UTs have also been encouraged to implement O nline Building 
Permission System (OBPS) for transparent, time -bound and technology -
enabled processing of applications, integration of departmental 
clearances, digital scrutiny of building plans and maintenance of 
electronic approval records.  Under Atal Mission for Rejuvenation and 
Urban Transformation (AMRUT), OBPS has been made operational in 3, 774 
towns including 452  AMRUT cities to facilitate online issuance of 
construction permits. 
However, adoption of the Model Building Bye- Laws, modification of State 
building regulations, conduct of inspections, periodic fire- safety audits, 
disclosure of approvals, enforcement against violations and fixation of 
accountability for officials and project proponents remain within the 
jurisdiction of the respective State/UT  Governments and competent local 
authorities.

entries.t: Reduction in Frequency of Flights from Prayagraj to Mumbai
entries.head:
GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF CIVIL AVIATION 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. : 3076 
 ( TO BE ANSWERED ON THE  6th August 2026 )  
REDUCTION IN FREQUENCY OF FLIGHTS FROM PRAYAGRAJ TO 
MUMBAI  
3076.    SHRI PRAVEEN PATEL                       
Will the Minister of CIVIL AVIATION 
be pleased to state:- 
(a) whether the Government is aware that various airlines have recently reduced 
the frequency of flights from Prayagraj to Mumbai wherein the flight operated by 
Akasa Air on all seven days of the week has be en reduced to only one day a week 
from July and the flight operated by IndiGo on six days a week has been reduced 
to only four days a week and if so, the reasons therefor; 
(b) whether the Government proposes to issue directions to the airlines to increase 
the frequency of flights in view of increasing inconvenience faced by passengers 
and if so, the details thereof; and 
(c) whether it is a fact that currently no air service is being operated from Prayagraj 
under Viability Gap Funding (VGF) as the period of the Regional Connectivity 
Scheme has expired and if so, the details thereof? 
ANSWER 
Minister of State in the Ministry of CIVIL AVIATION      (Shri Murlidhar Mohol) 
(a) to (c): With the repeal of the Air Corporations Act in March 1994, the Indian 
domestic aviation sector was deregulated. Airlines provide air services to specific 
destinations based on traffic demand and commercial viability, subject to 
compliance with the extant guidelines. As air traffic demand is seasonal in nature, 
airlines periodically op timise their route networks and plan route expansion after 
considering the prevailing operating costs during the relevant period. 
 
Accordingly, M/s Indigo and M/s Akasa Airlines have informed their plans to 
restore flights from Prayagraj to Mumbai from October 2026. 
 

Currently, no RCS flights are in operation from Prayagraj under the Viability Gap 
Funding (VGF) support period of the UDAN Scheme. 
******

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS 
  
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 3077 
ANSWERED ON 06th AUGUST, 2026 
  
IMPLEMENTATION OF CASHLESS TREATMENT SCHEME 
  
3077. MS. IQRA CHOUDHARY: 
  
Will the Minister of ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS  
  
सड़क परिवहन औि िाजमार्ग मंत्री 
be pleased to state: 
  
(a) the details of road accident victims on Expressways, National 
Highways (NHs) and State Highways (SHs) who received free 
treatment up to Rs. 1.5 lakh under the Cashless Treatment Scheme 
during the financial years 2023-24, 2024-25 and 2025-26, State-wise 
and year-wise;  
(b) whether instances have been reported of private hospitals 
delaying treatment during the Golden Hour on the grounds of police 
formalities or advance payment requirements, if so, the details 
thereof and the action taken against such hospitals during the last 
three years; 
(c) the number of citizens awarded an incentive of Rs. 5,000 along 
with a citation for transporting road accident victims to hospitals 
under the Good Samaritan Scheme, State -wise and year -wise; 
 
(d) whether any centralized digital dashboard or helpline has been 
made available at the district level for real -time tracking of 
hospitals and redressal of public grievances relating to the Cashless 
Treatment Scheme, if so, the details thereof; and 
 
(e) the number of persons provided treatment under the Cashless 
Treatment Scheme during the last two years in Shamli and 
Saharanpur districts of Uttar Pradesh? 

 ANSWER 
  
THE MINISTER OF ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS 
(SHRI NITIN JAIRAM GADKARI) 
  
(a) In accordance with the legal mandate under Section 162 of the 
Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, the Cashless Treatment for Road 
Accident Victims Scheme, 2025 was launched for nationwide 
implementation on 13.02.2026. The scheme provides treatm ent 
cover upto ₹1.5 lakh per victim, subject to a maximum cap of 7 days 
from date of accident on any category of road. Further, the 
treatment cover will be available to all those victims who are 
involved in road accidents caused by use of motor vehicles. 
As on 31.07.2026 since the launch of the scheme for nation -wide 
implementation, a total of 22,481 victims have received free 
treatment as per scheme guidelines across 34 States/UTs. The 
State/UT-wise details are attached as Annexure-I. 
  
(b)  Time-bound pro cedures and clearly defined responsibilities 
have been prescribed under PM -RAHAT scheme to minimise delays 
in the provision of treatment, processing of claims and 
disbursement of payments to hospitals. Treatment under the 
Scheme is provided through the following categories of hospitals:- 
(i) Hospitals empanelled under Ayushman Bharat Pradhan Mantri 
Jan Arogya Yojana ( AB PM-JAY) and compliant with the guidelines 
issued by the National Health Authority (NHA) are automatically 
deemed designated hospitals under the Scheme.  
(ii) The States/UTs may onboard additional designated hospitals  
with the required infrastructure, skilled personnel and trauma -care 
capability, in accordance with the guidelines issued by NHA vide 
O.M. No. S-12018/81/2024 dated 20.05.2025.  
(iii) Hospitals other than designated hospitals are required to 
provide immediate stabilisation treatment and may thereafter 
transfer the victim to an appropriate designated hospital within 
stipulated timelines. 

Denial of admission or treatment under the S cheme amounts to non-
compliance with the applicable Scheme provisions. States/UTs are 
empowered to take action under laws regulating clinical 
establishments, including the Clinical Establishments (Registration 
and Regulation) Act, 2010, or the corresponding State-specific laws. 
Further, the hospital empanelment guidelines provide for 
disciplinary proceedings, suspension and de -empanelment in cases 
of non-compliance. 
(c)   The Government has instituted the Rah -Veer Scheme to 
encourage citizens to assist vict ims of serious road accidents 
during the Golden Hour. As per the information received from 
States/UTs, the number of citizens awarded  incentive under the 
Good Samaritan Scheme are attached as Annexure-II. 
(d)   As per the scheme guidelines, a dedicated Grievance 
Redressal Officer (GRO) is to be appointed by the District Road 
Safety Committee in every district to address grievances arising 
from implementation of the Scheme. If the applicant is dissatisfied 
with t he resolution, or if there is a delay, the grievance may be 
escalated to the District Collector, and thereafter to the State Road 
Safety Council, which acts as the appellate authority.  
  
The NHA helpline 14588 is also available to hospitals for grievances  
relating to hospitalisation, treatment and settlement of hospital 
claims. 
  
Further, a citizen-centric PM-RAHAT module has been developed as 
part of the m-Parivahan mobile application . The module enables 
citizens to access information relating to the Sche me, obtain 
details of the nearest designated hospital, check the s

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS 
  
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. - 3078 
ANSWERED ON 06th AUGUST, 2026 
  
STRENGTHENING ROAD SAFETY 
  
3078. SHRI SURESH KUMAR SHETKAR: 
   
Will the Minister of ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS  
  
सड़क परिवहन औि िाजमार्ग मंत्री 
be pleased to state: 
  
(a) the steps taken to strengthen emergency trauma care, ambulance 
services and the Golden Hour response mechanism for road accident 
victims across the country;  
(b) whether the Government has undertaken any assessment of the 
implementation of the Motor Vehicles (Amendment) Act, 2019 with 
regard to improvement in road safety and reduction in traffic 
violations, if so, the findings thereof;  
(c) the details of initiatives under taken to improve road safety 
awareness among school students, young drivers and commercial 
vehicle operators along with the outcomes achieved thereof;  
(d) whether the Government has issued guidelines for mandatory 
road safety audits at various stages of Na tional Highway (NH) 
projects, if so, the details thereof and the extent of compliance by 
implementing agencies; and  
(e) whether the Government proposes to launch any new scheme or 
mission to achieve the target of substantially reducing road accident 
fatalities by 2030, if so, the details thereof including the financial 
outlay, implementation strategy and the expected outcomes?  
  

  
ANSWER 
  
THE MINISTER OF ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS 
                                                                                         
(SHRI NITIN JAIRAM GADKARI) 
  
(a) and (e) In accordance with the legal mandate under Section 162 of 
the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, the Cashless Treatment for Road 
Accident Victims Scheme, 2025 was launched for nationwide 
implementation on 13.0 2.2026. The scheme provides treatment cover 
upto ₹1.5 lakh per victim, subject to a maximum cap of 7 days from 
date of accident on any category of road. Further, the treatment cover 
will be available to all those victims who are involved in road 
accidents caused by use of motor vehicles. 
The following measures have been taken to strengthen the Golden 
Hour response mechanism: 
  
(i). Through convergence with the 112 Emergency Response Support 
System (ERSS), a victim or Good Samaritan may obtain details of the 
nearest designated hospital and seek ambulance support. The 
jurisdictional police are also intimated to facilitate timely response 
and authentication.  
  
(ii). Hospitals empanelled under AB PM -JAY and compliant with the 
guidelines issued by the National Health Authority are automatically 
listed as designated hospitals under the Scheme. States and Union 
Territories have also been enabled b y NHA vide O.M. No. S -
12018/81/2024 dated 20 May 2025, to onboard additional hospitals with 
the requisite trauma -care infrastructure and skilled personnel, 
particularly near accident hotspots and in areas with limited treatment 
facilities. 
  

(iii). Where a victim reaches a non -designated hospital, the hospital is 
required to provide immediate stabilisation treatment, thereby 
ensuring treatment even where a designated facility is not located at 
the first point of care. 
  
(iv). The Government has instituted t he Rah -Veer Scheme to 
encourage citizens to assist victims of serious road accidents during 
the Golden Hour. The Scheme operates along with the protections 
provided to Good Samaritans under Section 134A of the Motor 
Vehicles Act, 1988 and the Good Samarita n Rules notified vide G.S.R. 
594(E) dated 29.09.2020. Any individual who has assisted a victim of a 
serious accident involving a motor vehicle by administering immediate 
assistance and rushing the victim to a Hospital/Trauma Care Centre 
within the Golden H our of the accident for medical treatment is 
eligible for a cash reward of Rs. 25,000 per incident, along with a 
Certificate of Appreciation, subject to the provisions of the Scheme. 
  
(b) The Motor Vehicles (Amendment) Act, 2019 as stands implemented 
provides for strict penalties for ensuring compliance and enhancing 
deterrence for violation of traffic rules and strict enforcement through 
use of technology. Traffic management and enforcement is essentially 
in the domain of State Governments/UT  Administrations. While Central 
Government formulates rules under the Motor Vehicle Act, 1988, the 
enforcement of these rules comes under the sole jurisdiction of State 
Governments/UT Administrations. 
  
(c) A media outreach activity namely 'Sadak Suraksha Abhiyaan' hs 
been undertaken during the Financial Year 2025 –26, under which, 
awareness activities on road safety issue, including safety of school 
going children, etc., have been undertaken. As part of the Abhiyaan, a 
total of 150 Nukkad Natak (street plays) were organ ized in schools 
across the country with the objective of creating behavioural change 
and enhancing road safety awareness among students. 
  
Further, the pilot phase of P

 Will the Minister of POWER 
be pleased to state: 
 
(a)  whether due to overloaded transformers, dilapidated power lines and 
excess load capacity, frequent transformer breakdowns, power outages and risk 
of accidents persist in several villages and urban colonies of Sonipat and Hisar 
Lok Sabha Constituencies;  
 
(b)  if so, the details of the sanctioned projects and funds allocated for the 
replacement and capacity enhancement of such transformers and dilapidated 
power lines in the said constituencies during the last three years;  
 
(c)  whether the Government is implementing any special scheme for working 
on the expansion of separate agricultural feeders, modernization and 
implementation of smart distribution systems to ensure uninterrupted power 
supply to farmers for irrigation within stipulated timelines;  
 
(d)  if so, the details of the proposed works, timelines thereof and the expected 
benefits therefrom in Sonipat Lok Sabha Constituency; and  
 
(e)  the details of the proposed agricultural feeders, the present progress of the 
works and the likely timeframe for the completion thereof in the Hisar Lok Sabha 
Constituency? 
A N S W E R 
 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF POWER  
 
(SHRI SHRIPAD NAIK)  
 
(a) Electricity is a concurrent subject and power distribution is handled by 
distribution utilities that  function under the guidance of the respective State 
Electricity Regulatory Commissions (SERCs) and State Governments. As per the 
Electricity Act, 2003, distribution of electricity is a licensed activity and it is the 
duty of the respective distribution li censee to develop and maintain an efficient 
and safe distribution system in its area of supply. Hence, the responsibility for 
taking necessary measures for the upgradation and maintenance of the 

distribution system to ensure quality power supply, including  transformers and 
distribution lines, rests with the respective distribution utilities.  
As reported by the distribution utilities of Haryana, details regarding overloaded 
Distribution Transformers (DTRs), dilapidated/overloaded power lines identified, 
transformer breakdown cases during the last three years; major reasons for such 
breakdowns and the action taken in respect of Hisar and Sonipat Lok Sabha 
Constituencies are given at Annexure-I. 
 
(b) to (e): The Government of India launched Revamped Distributi on Sector 
Scheme (RDSS) in the year 2021 to supplement the efforts of States to help them 
provide quality supply of power to consumers through a financially sustainable 
and operationally efficient distribution sector. Loss reduction infrastructure and 
smart metering works worth Rs 1.53 lakh crores and Rs 1.31 lakhs crores, 
respectively, have been sanctioned under RDSS. The loss reduction and smart 
distribution works sanctioned under RDSS include: 
 
i. Works for creation of new/upgradation of substations includi ng Gas 
Insulated Switchgear (GIS) Substations 
 
ii. Installation of new Distribution Transformers (DT) and augmentation of 
existing DTs 
 
iii. Replacement of old conductors 
iv. Underground of HT/LT lines 
v. Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition (SCADA) works 
vi. Smart metering works covering 19.79 crore consumers and smart system 
metering works for 2.11 lakh feeders and 52.53 lakh DTs have been 
sanctioned. Till date, 5.83 crore smart meters have been installed under 
RDSS, and overall, 7.34 crore smart meters have been installed across the 
country under various schemes. 
 
The above sanction includes works for loss reduction infrastructure 
amounting to Rs 6,693.15 crores under RDSS for the state of Haryana. Further, as 
reported by the State, all agricultural feeders have already been segregated since 
2021. The smart metering works were undertaken by the State under its own plan 
in the districts of Gurugram, Panchkula, Karnal, Panipat and Faridabad for 8.74 
lakh consumers. 
 
The details regarding works undertaken under RDSS in Hisar  and Sonipat 
Lok Sabha constituencies are given at Annexure -II. The sanctioned works are 
expected to complete with the scheme period i.e. March 2028. The works once 
executed would lead to improvement in quality of power supply and enhanced 
consumer services.

Will the Minister of ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS 
सड़क परिवहन औि िाजमार्ग मंत्री 
be pleased to state: 
(a) whether the Government has taken note of the recent changes in the 
toll policy adopted by  the Government of Bihar exempting private non -
commercial four-wheelers from payment of toll on State Highways; 
(b) whether the Ministry has issued any model guidelines or policy 
framework for levy of user  charges on State Highways by State 
Governments and if so, the details thereof; 
(c) whether the Government has examined the fiscal implications of 
exempting private vehicles from toll on State Highways in certain States 
and if so, the details thereof; and 
(d) whether the Government proposes to evolve a uniform framework in 
consultation with  State Governments for balancing user convenience, 
revenue generation and maintenance of  State Highway infrastructure 
and if so, the details thereof?

ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS 
(SHRI NITIN JAIRAM GADKARI) 
(a) to (d) The collection of user fees/Toll, if any, on State Highways/ 
Expressways falls under the constitutional  jurisdiction of the respective 
State Governments and is governed in accordance with the User Fee/Toll

Accordingly, matters relating to exemption of private non -commercial 
four-wheelers from payment of toll on State Highways, issuance of policy 
guidelines for levy of user charges on State Highways, assessment of the

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF CIVIL AVIATION 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. : 3081 
 ( TO BE ANSWERED ON THE  6th August 2026 )  
CAP ON AIRFARES  
3081.    SHRI BRIJENDRA SINGH OLA                 
Will the Minister of CIVIL AVIATION 
be pleased to state:- 
(a) whether the airfares are increased arbitrarily and excessively during festivals and emergency 
situations in the country causing unnecessary financial burden on common passengers; 
(b) if so, whether the Government maintains data on such hikes in  airfare indicating the frequency, 
duration and extent of increase in airfares, if so, the details thereof during the last five years and the 
current year, year-wise and if not, the reasons therefor; 
(c) whether the Government is contemplating to regulate airfares, cap maximum fares or implement 
any effective regulatory mechanism to protect the interests of consumers and if so, the details thereof 
along with the action taken so far in this regard; and 
(d) whether small and large airports have been handed ov er or are proposed to be handed over to 
private entities under the Public Private Partnership (PPP) model and if so, the details of the 
provisions made to ensure transparency, competition, public interest and accountability in this 
process? 
ANSWER 
Minister of State in the Ministry of CIVIL AVIATION      (Shri Murlidhar Mohol)  
(a) to (c): The pricing of airfares is subject to dynamic fluctuations influenced by the forces of supply 
and demand. Various determinants such as current seat occupancy, fuel costs, a ircraft capacity, 
seasonal fluctuations and other relevant factors significantly impact airline ticket pricing.; 
; 
With the repeal of Air Corporation Act in March 1994, airfares are not subject to be regulated by the 
Government. Airlines have the autonomy to establish airfare based on their operational & economic 
viability on a particular route while adhering to Rule 135 of the Aircraft Rules, 1937.; 
; 
The Government generally refrains from regulating airfares to maintain market competitiveness, 
however, it retains vigilant oversight role, intervening in exceptional circumstances by redistributing 
capacity across various sectors and imposing temporary fare caps, such as during the Covid 
Pandemic, festivals like Maha kumb or other extraordinary instances like  Pahalgam incident & the 
Indigo flight disruptions.; 
; 
In order to enhance the transparency in airfare, Directorate General of Civil Aviation (DGCA) has set-
up Tariff Monitoring Unit (TMU) that monitors airfares on selected 78 routes on a random basis by 
using airlines websites on monthly basis to ensure that the airlines do not charge airfares outside the 
range declared by them.; 
; 
(d): As per the National Monetization Pipeline (NMP) 2.0 of Govt of India, airports are proposed for 
monetization. Selection o f the Public Private Partnership (PPP) is done through a transparent open 
competitive bidding process through online portal. 
******

ENVIRONMENTAL IMPACT OF COAL-BASED THERMAL POWER PLANTS 
 
3083. SHRI CHANDRA PRAKASH CHOUDHARY: 
 
 Will the Minister of POWER 
be pleased to state: 
 
(a) whether the Government ha s taken measures to reduce the environmental impact of 
the coal-based Bokaro Thermal Power Station (BTPS) and Chandrapura Thermal Power 
Station (CTPS) of the Damodar Valley Corporation (DVC) and if so, the details thereof;  
 
(b) the present status of insta llation and commissioning of Flue Gas Desulphurisation 
(FGD) systems at the said stations along with the reasons for any delay;  
 
(c) the details of fly ash generation, utilisation and scientific ash management and the 
measures taken to promote biomass and  Municipal Solid Waste (MSW)/Refuse Derived 
Fuel (RDF) co-firing at these plants;  
 
(d) the details of the outsourcing agencies/Engineering, Procurement and Construction 
(EPC) contractors engaged for these environmental compliance works and other works, 
their performance against contractual milestones and delays, penalties, if any, along with 
the corrective measures taken in the matter; and  
 
(e) the strategy adopted by the Government to ensure environmental sustainability while 
maintaining reliable thermal power generation at BTPS and CTPS? 
A N S W E R 
 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF POWER  
 
(SHRI SHRIPAD NAIK)  
 
(a) : Bokaro Thermal Power Station (BTPS) and Chandrapura Thermal Power Station 
(CTPS) operate under the control of the Damodar Valley C orporation (DVC). In order to 
comply with the environmental norms notified by the Ministry of Environment, Forest and 
Climate Change (MoEF&CC), DVC has implemented several measures. These initiatives 
include installation of Electrostatic Precipitators (ESPs) to control particulate matter, De-
NOx system to reduce nitrogen oxides, Continuous Emission Monitoring Systems (CEMS), 
Continuous Ambient Air Quality Monitoring System (CAAQMS), ash water recirculation, 
rainwater harvesting and wastewater recycling syst ems. Plantation has also been 
undertaken to mitigate the environmental impact of these power plants. Moreover, Flue 
Gas Desulphurisation (FGD) system has also been installed at BTPS.  
 
(b) : In BTPS, FGD system has been installed and was declared under com mercial 
operation on 22.06.2024.  
 
Vide Notification dated 11.07.2025 of MoEF&CC, Category -C thermal power plants 
are required to comply with the stack height criteria prescribed under G.S.R. 742(E) dated 
30.08.1990. Since CTPS is a category ‘C’ thermal power plant, FGD is not required. 
 
……….2.

(c) : Fly ash generated at BTPS and CTPS is managed in accordance with the provisions 
of MoEF&CC Ash Notifications and the Ministry of Power guidelines. Details of ash 
generation and utilisation for the last three years is given below:

The fly ash is utilized in cement manufacturing, brick and block production. For 
better ash management, DVC has undertake n several measures including evacuat ion of 
ash through Rail -cum-Road (RCR) mode, filling/ disposal of ash in abandoned mines and 
low-lying areas, execution of Memorandum of Understanding (MoUs) with NHAI and other 
Government agencies for road construction projects, and regular e-auction of dry fly ash 
through the Expression of Interest (EOI) process. 
 
At BTPS, co-firing of non-torrefied biomass pellets has already been implemented 
and around 1,286 Metric Ton (MT) of biomass was co -fired during FY 2025 -26. CTPS is 
equipped with Ball and Tube type grinding mills for coal pulverisation, which are not 
suitable for pulverisation of non-torrefied biomass pellets with coal due to high Volatile 
Matter (VM) content and other technical and operational limitations. 
 
At present, there is no sourcing of MSW/ RDF at either of these plants. 
 
(d) : The details of the outsourcing agencies/contractors engaged for environmental 
compliance works and other works are at Annexure. 
 
(e) : In order to ensure environmental sustainabil ity while maintaining reliable thermal 
power generation at BTPS and CTPS, DVC has adopted a comprehensive compliance 
strategy in line with the MoEF&CC Notification dated 07.12.2015 which inter alia includes 
installation of ESPs, De -NOx, FGD systems, CEMS a nd CAAQMS to track air quality 
parameters continuously, improved ash handling/ transportation mechanism and 
plantation drives etc.

an approximately eight kms freight corridor with about 800 metres under the

IMPACT OF BHARATMALA PARIYOJANA PROJECTS 
  
3088.  SHRI THARANIVENTHAN M S:   
  
Will the Minister of ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS 
सड़क परिवहन औि िाजमार्ग मंत्री  
be pleased to state:  
  
(a) the total number of projects sanctioned and completed under Bharatmala 
Pariyojana, State-wise particularly in Arani Lok Sabha Constituency of Tamil 
Nadu; 
  
(b) the  total length of roads constructed or upgraded under Bharatmala 
Pariyojana during the last three years along with the estimated cost and 
timelines thereof; 
  
(c) whether the Government has assessed the impact of Bharatmala 
Pariyojana on freight efficiency,  regional connectivity and local economic 
development and if so, the details thereof; 
  
(d) the steps taken to ensure timely completion of pending projects and 
resolution of issues relating to land acquisition and environmental 
clearances; and 
  
(e) the measures adopted to ensure that local employment, small contractors 
and Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) benefit from Bharatmala 
Pariyojana projects? 
  
ANSWER 
  
THE MINISTER OF ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS 
(SHRI NITIN JAIRAM GADKARI) 
  
(a) & (b) Bharatmala Pariyojana Phase -I was approved in 2017 covering a 
length of 34,800 km across the country at an estimated outlay of Rs. 

5,35,000 Crore. Under the program, projects covering a total length of 26,425 
km have been awarded and out of this, 22,755 km  has already been 
constructed upto June, 2026. State -wise details are annexed. Further, during 
last 3 years, about 6,600 km of National Highways (NHs) under Bharatmala 
Pariyojana have been constructed. The details of works sanctioned / 
completed in Arani Lok Sabha Constituency are annexed. 
(c) The study conducted by Indian Institute of Management (IIM), Bangalore 
to evaluate the impact of Bharatmala Pariyojana indicates positive effects 
across multiple sectors. Economically, household income and expenditure  
has increased. Logistics efficiency has improved with reduced costs. 
Businesses have benefited from better access to markets and factories. 
Socially, travel time to schools and healthcare facilities has decreased, 
enhancing accessibility. Overall, the stu dy suggests that Bharatmala 
Pariyojana has significantly contributed to socio -economic growth. As per 
the study conducted by IIM Bangalore, Bharatmala Pariyojana has 
demonstrated significant socio-economic benefits. 
(d) The primary reasons for delay in Nat ional Highway (NH) projects are 
issues / bottlenecks relating to land acquisition, delay in getting statutory 
clearances / permissions, utility shifting, encroachment removal, law & 
order, non-availability of construction material / minerals, poor performa nce 
of Contractor / Concessionaire, and Force Majeure events like Covid -19 
pandemic etc. To expedite project execution, various initiatives have been 
undertaken. These include streamlining and expediting the land acquisition 
process through Bhoomi Rashi po rtal, revamping the Parivesh Portal through 
Ministry of Environment, Forests and Climate Change to expedite forest and 
environmental clearances, enabling online approval of General Arrangement 
Drawings (GAD) for Road over Bridges (ROBs) and Road under Bridges (RUBs) 
from the Railways, and conducting review meetings at various  levels with all 
stakeholders, including State Governments. The Government is taking all 
necessary steps for timely completion of these projects. 
(e) For NH works, bids are invited on e-procurement portal of the Central 
Government, wherein bidders can compete based on their technical and 
financial capacity. Further, Government has made it mandatory to meet the 
provision of local content requirement, in its bidding process to help local 
suppliers/ manufacturers including Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises.

(a) whether the Ministry has developed any monitoring mechanism 
in coordination with the  State Governments for compliance with 
statutory traffic rul es by vehicles registered on the Vahan portal, if 
so, the details thereof; 
  
(b) whether the Government has conducted any study regarding the 
compliance with statutory traffic rules by vehicles registered on the 
Vahan portal; 
  
(c) if so, whether the Gover nment has taken cognizance of the fact 
that some of the vehicles  registered on the Vahan portal does not 
meet the compliance standards of statutory rules; 
  
(d) if so, the number of such vehicles, State and Union Territory -
wise; and 
  
(e) the steps being taken by the Government to ensure compliance 
with statutory rules by registered vehicles in the country? 
 
 
 
 
 
  

ANSWER 
 
THE MINISTER OF ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS 
 
(SHRI NITIN JAIRAM GADKARI) 
  
(a) to (e). The Central Government has enacted the Motor Vehicles 
Act, 1988 under Entry 35 of the Concurrent List (List III) of the 
Seventh Schedule to the Constitution of India. In exercise of the 
powers conferred under the Act, the Central Government has also 
framed the Central Motor Vehicles Rules, 1989 (CMVR). Accordingly, 
the role of the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways is primarily 
confined to the formulation of the statutory framework under the 
Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 and the rules framed thereunder, while the 
implementation and enforcement of the provisions of the Act and 
the Rules are undertaken by the respective State Governments and 
Union Territory Administrations. 
In furtherance of its statutory mandate, various technology -enabled 
platforms have been developed and implemented to facilitate 
uniform implementation of the provisions of the Motor Vehicles Act, 
1988 across the country. The National Register of Motor Vehicles 
under Section 62B of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 and the National 
Register of Driving Licences under Section 25A of the Act ar e 
maintained through the VAHAN and SARATHI platforms, 
respectively. These platforms provide a common digital 
infrastructure to the States and Union Territories for registration of 
motor vehicles, issuance of driving licences, associated services 
and maintenance of related statutory records. The aforesaid portals 
are being customised by the respective State Governments and 
Union Territory Administrations to cater to their specific operational 
and administrative requirements. 
Further, Chapter XIII of the Moto r Vehicles Act, 1988 pertains to 
offences, penalties and procedures prescribing offences including 
offence relating to non-compliance of traffic rules.  
Moreover, Section 136A of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 provides for 
electronic monitoring and enforceme nt of road safety on National 
Highways, State Highways, roads and urban areas having such 

population as may be prescribed by the Central Government. In 
furtherance of the same, Rule 167A of the CMVR pertaining to 
Electronic Monitoring and Enforcement of Ro ad Safety has been 
formulated. Additionally, Standing Operating Procedure (SOP) dated 
28.10.2025 has been circulated to States/UTs for Electronic 
Monitoring & Enforcement of Road Safety.  
Further, Rule 167, prescribes a comprehensive uniform procedure 
for issuance, contesting and payment of electronic challans issued 
to a person acting in violation of provisions of the Act. The said Rule 
mandates that every challan issued shall be uploaded on the 
designated portal (e -Challan portal) and shall be served upon  the 
registered owner or driving licence holder or such other person as 
may be liable. Rule 167 also provides that where a person fails to 
comply with the prescribed timelines for payment or contesting of 
the challan, transport related services excluding p ayment of tax, 
shall be withheld, until the outstanding challan is disposed of in 
accordance with the provisions of the Rules. The implementation of 
the aforesaid procedure, including adjudication of challans is 
undertaken by the respective States/UTs thro ugh their designated 
authorities. 
In addition to the above, Section 53 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 
empowers the registering authority to suspend the Certificate of 
Registration of a vehicle if such vehicle fails to comply with the 
requirements of the A ct or the rules made thereunder. Where such 
suspension of the Certificate of Registration continues without 
interruption for a period of not less than six months, the registering 
authority is further empowered to cancel the registration under 
Section 54 of the Act.

entries.t: DBT in Implementation of Scholarship Schemes for Tribals
entries.head:
GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF TRIBAL AFFAIRS 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION No. 3091 
TO BE ANSWERED ON 06.08.2026 
  
“DBT in Implementation of Scholarship Schemes for Tribals” 
  
3091. Shri PP Chaudhary: 
Dr. K Sudhakar: 
Shri Jugal Kishore: 
Smt. Mahima Kumari Mewar: 
Smt. Himadri Singh: 
Shri Nalin Soren: 
Shri Manish Jaiswal: 
  
Will the Minister of TRIBAL AFFAIRS be pleased to state: 
(a) whether the Ministry has undertaken any assessment of the Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) Tribal Portal 
for implementation of scholarship schemes in the country: 
(b) if so, the details thereof, State-wise and district-wise; 
(c) the progress achieved in improving transparency and timely disbursement of scholarships through the 
portal; 
(d) whether any measures have been undertaken to strengthen real-time monitoring, authentication of 
Aadhaar/bank account, beneficiary verification and prevention of fake or duplicate claims under the 
scholarship ecosystem, if so, the details thereof; and 
(e) the observed impact of digitalisation on improving access to scholarships for Scheduled Tribe (ST) 
students, reducing processing delays and lowering dropout rates across the country, State-wise?  
ANSWER 
MINISTER OF STATE FOR TRIBAL AFFAIRS 
(SHRI DURGADAS UIKEY)  
(a)  Currently, the Ministry is already leveraging the benefit of DBT Tribal Portal by accessing the data 
of beneficiaries submitted by the respective State/UT for monitoring and generating MIS reports for the 
implementation of pre-matric and post-matric scholarship schemes. The States/UTs have also been given 
facilities to upload queries, documents, utilization certificates, statement of expenditure etc. which has 
reduced processing time and reduced grievances. 
(b)       The details of the number of beneficiaries reported by the States/UTs on the DBT Tribal Portal for 
the pre-matric and post-matric scholarship schemes during the last three financial years are given at 
Annexure-I. 
(c)       The Pre-Matric and Post-Matric Scholarship Schemes are the Centrally Sponsored Schemes and 
implemented through respective States/UTs. The disbursement of scholarships is carried out by the 
concerned State/UT through their own portal or NSP portal. The progress made through the Portal are 
given as under: -     
i.End-to-End Digitization: Transition from paper-based processing to scheme-specific digital portals. 
ii.Common Data Standard: Implementation of standard data format for seamless web-service API based 
data sharing between States/UT portals/ National Scholarship Portal (NSP) and the DBT Tribal Portal of 
the Ministry 

iii.Faster Communication and Online Processing: Online upload of Utilization Certificates (UCs), 
Statements of Expenditure (SoE), and queries by States, significantly reducing processing time and 
administrative delays. 
iv.Public Transparency & Outcome Dashboards: Integration of beneficiary and transaction data with the 
Performance Dashboard of the Ministry, DBT Mission, Prayas Dashboard, and NITI Aayog for outcome 
tracking. 
(d)       The data of beneficiaries reported by the State/UTs in the DBT Tribal Portal have been useful for 
monitoring and generating MIS reports. Integration of National Scholarship Portal with States/UTs 
scholarship portal enables data validation and automated deduplication checks across schemes and 
databases.  
Under Pre-Matric and Post-Matric Scholarship Schemes for ST students, to eliminate float at State level, 
minimize delays in release of scholarship, and ensure transparency of fund flow, the Ministry has adopted 
the SNA SPARSH Model for release of central share under Pre-Matric and Post-Matric Scholarship 
Scheme.  This serves as a Just-in-Time Disbursement Framework under which the Central Share funds 
are release in "Just-in-time" as and when the bills are raised by respective State Govt for payment of 
scholarship. Once the bills for scholarship payment is approved, both Central Share as well as State 
Share fund is directly transferred from RBI account to Student beneficiary account on through DBT. This 
eliminates the parking of central share funds at state level and minimize delay in disbursement of 
scholarship. 
Under Central Sector Schemes of Scholarship implemented directly by the Ministry, a robust digital 
mechanism is established through the National Scholarship Portal (NSP), Ministry’s Scholarship Portal 
and the Public Financial Management System (PFMS) to facilitate Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT). 
(e)       Removal of physical application process and manual verification by Institute/District/State 
authorities has streamlined approval workflows and reduced the overall application processing time. 
Transfer of Scholarship amount through Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) into the beneficiary student bank 
accounts ensures that financial benefit reaches targeted ST students in time and without involvement of 
intermediaries.

EXPANSION OF BAGDOGRA AIRPORT 
3092.    SHRI RAJU BISTA                       
    
Will the Minister of CIVIL AVIATION 
be pleased to state:- 
(a) the current status of the Bagdogra Airport expansion project including the 
expected timeline for its completion; 
(b) the steps taken to improve direct air and helicopter connectivity at Bagdogra 
Airport under the UDAN Scheme; 
(c) whether the Government has evaluated the development of minor airstrips 
and helipads in the districts of North Bengal; and 
(d) if so, the details thereof and if not, the reasons therefor? 
ANSWER 
Minister of State in the Ministry of CIVIL AVIATION       
(Shri Murlidhar Mohol) 
(a): The Airports Authority of India (AAI) has undertaken the development of 
New Civil Enclave at Bagdogra Airport at an estimated cost of Rs.1549 crore. 
The projected date of completion for the project is March, 2027. However, the 
timeline for completion of the airport projects depends upon many factors such 
as land acquisition, availability of mandatory clearances, financial closures etc. 
 
(b) to (d): The objective of the UDAN Scheme is to develop and operationalise 
unserved or underserv ed airstrips including heliports in North Eastern region, 
hilly states, and island territories to improve regional air connectivity and make 
air travel accessible in remote areas. 
 
The next phase of the UDAN Scheme, launched on 04.07.2026, expands air and 
helicopter connectivity by envisaging the development of 100 airports and 200 
modern helipads in Aspirational Districts and Priority Area districts where no 
heliport or airport is operational or under development, which will facilitate 
improved access for  passenger connectivity as well as support emergency 
medical evacuation, disaster response and relief operations i n remote and 
underserved areas. 
 

The modified UDAN scheme introduces a Challenge Mode framework under 
which the State Government of West Ben gal may identify and nominate 
suitable locations for development of airport and heliport infrastructure, subject 
to operational feasibility and availability of suitable sites.

THE MINISTER OF ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS 
 
(SHRI NITIN JAIRAM GADKARI) 
(a) to (d) Government in Ministry of Road Transport and 
Highways allocates and releases funds under the Central Road & 
Infrastructure Fund (CRIF) Scheme as per the provisions of the 
amended CRIF Act, 2000, based on the criteria duly approved by the 
Government in Ministry of Finance to the State Governments / Union

development and maintenance of State Roads.   Government in 
2022-23 has also taken up specific programme for replacement of 
existing Railways level crossings and construction of standalone 
Bridges on State Roads known as “Setu Bandhan” under CRIF

State Roads projects, including proposals of Road Under Bridge 
(RUB) / Road Over Bridge (R OB) / Bridge p rojects under Setu 
Bandhan, duly prioritized and recommended by State/UT 
Governments, including the State of Telangana, based on the 
current year accrual and outstanding committed liabilities of

inception in FY 2022 -23.  State / Union Territory (UT) – wise details 
of the projects are at Annexure. Out of this, 14 projects costing 
₹544 Crore have been completed. 
(e)     In a major step towards enhancing efficiency, transparency, 
and inter -agency coordination in infrastructure development, 
Government has inter -alia launched the PRISM -SG (Portal for Rail -
Road Inspection & Stages Management – Steel Gi rders) Portal  to 
digitise key approval and inspection processes related to the 
construction of ROBs. The portal enables end -to-end online 
submission of documents, scrutiny, raising and resolution of 

queries, approvals, scheduling of inspections, and upload ing of 
inspection reports, photographs, test results, supported by a 
complete audit trail and real-time monitoring capabilities. 
However, Administrative Approval, Technical Approval and 
Financial Sanction of the individual projects of the approved list 
under CRIF Scheme along with their implementation, monitoring & 
quality control vests with respective State/UT Governments.
