3094. SHRI YADUVEER WADIYAR: 
 
पेटŌोिलयम और Ůाक ृ ितक गैस मंũी 
 
Will the Minister of PETROLEUM AND NATURAL GAS be pleased to state: 
(a) whether the Government has undertaken any assessment of feedstock availability,aggregation and 
supply-chain constraints affecting Compressed Biogas (CBG) plants establishedunder the Sustainable 
Alternative Towards Affordable Transportation (SATAT) initiative and theGalvanizing Organic Bio-
Agro Resources Dhan (GOBARdhan) initiative, if so, the details thereof; 
(b) the details of CBG plants sanctioned, commissioned and operational under the aforesaidinitiatives, 
along with those facing feedstock or pipeline connectivity constraints, State-wise; 
(c) whether the Government maintains the data on biomass aggregation mechanisms andlong-term 
feedstock supply arrangements for such plants, if so, the details thereof; and 
(d) the corrective measures taken to strengthen feedstock aggregation, pipeline connectivityand the 
sustained operation of CBG plants? 
 
ANSWER 
 
पेटŌोिलयम और Ůाक ृ ितक गैस मंũालय मŐ राǛमंũी 
(ŵी सुरेश गोपी  )  
 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF PETROLEUM AND NATURAL GAS 
(SHRI SURESH GOPI) 
 
(a) to (d) The selection of feedstock and its aggregation arrangements are the responsibility of the 
respective CBG project developers based on local availability and techno-commercial viability. The 
Government periodically reviews the progress of CBG projects through consultations with State 
Governments, Oil & Gas Marketing Companies (OGMCs), CBG developers and other stakeholders. 
During these consultations, issues relating to feedstock availability, biomass aggregation and supply-
chain logistics, including seasonal availability of biomass, collection and transportation of dispersed 
feedstock, storage and competing uses of biomass, have been identified and are addressed through 
appropriate policy and facilitation measures. 
As reported by entrepreneurs on the GOBARdhan Portal, as on 31stJuly, 2026, 217 CBG plants have 
been commissioned.The State/UT-wise details of commissioned CBGprojects are at Annexure.  

CBG project developers adopt biomass aggregation models based on local availability and techno-
commercial feasibility, including long-term feedstock supply arrangements with farmers, Farmer 
Producer Organizations (FPOs), cooperatives, local vendors, or through their own aggregation 
mechanisms.  
To strengthen biomass aggregation, pipeline connectivity and the sustained operation of CBG plants, 
Government have taken various measures, inter-alia including:  
(i) Biomass Aggregation Machinery (BAM) Scheme: Financial assistance of up to ₹9 crore per CBG 
plant is provided to eligible CBG producers for procurement of biomass aggregation machinery at 50% 
of the procurement cost of eligible machinery, subject to a maximum of ₹90 lakh per set. 
(ii) Crop Residue Management (CRM) Scheme: Under this scheme financial assistance of 50% is 
provided to farmers for purchase of crop residue management machinery, 80% for establishment of 
Custom Hiring Centres, and 65% (up to ₹1.50 crore) for paddy supply chain projects to support 
collection, aggregation and utilization of crop residue. 
(iii) Development of Pipeline Infrastructure (DPI) Scheme: Financial assistance is provided to eligible 
entities for development of dedicated pipeline connectivity between CBG plants/clusters and the CGD 
or Natural Gas Pipeline network to facilitate CBG evacuation. 
(iv) Model State CBG Policy: A Model State CBG Policy has been circulated to States/(Union 
Territories) UTs to facilitate investments, streamline approvals, improve feedstockavailability and 
promote sustainable CBG production. 
(v) Special Assistance to States for Capital Investment (SASCI): A CBG Sector Reforms component 
has been introduced under the SASCI Scheme to incentivize States/UTs to create an enabling 
ecosystem for the development of CBG projects.

entries.head:
GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF CIVIL AVIATION 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. : 3095 
 ( TO BE ANSWERED ON THE  6th August 2026 )  
STRENGTHENING OF AIR CONNECTIVITY IN AKOLA  
3095.    SHRI ANUP SANJAY DHOTRE                  
Will the Minister of CIVIL AVIATION 
be pleased to state:- 
(a) whether Akola Airport has been considered for operationalisation or expansion 
under the Modified UDAN Scheme and if so, the details and the present status 
thereof along with the details of the assistance provided therefor; and 
(b) the measures taken/proposed to be taken to strengthen operational viability, 
enhance passenger traffic and improve regional air connectivity under the said 
scheme, particularly in Maharashtra including Akola? 
ANSWER 
Minister of State in the Ministry of CIVIL AVIATION      (Shri Murlidhar Mohol) 
(a) & (b): The Government has launched the next phase of the UDAN Scheme on 
04.07.2026 for a period of ten years, from FY 2026 -27 to FY 2035-36, with a total 
outlay of Rs. 28,840 crore. This includes budget ary support of Rs. 12,159 crore 
from the Government of India for the development of 100 airports. 
The Scheme provides a Challenge Mode framework under which State 
Governments may nominate aerodromes and helipads for development. Proposals 
are evaluated bas ed on availability of encumbrance -free land, infrastructure 
readiness, technical and operational feasibility, traffic potential, statutory 
clearances and support of the State Governments. 
To enhance operational viability and passenger traffic, the Scheme i ncorporates 
longer VGF mechanism extending up to five years, progressively tapered to enable 
airlines to transition towards commercially sustainable operations. The Scheme 
also supports the development and upgradation of airport infrastructure and 
encourages State Governments to provide facilitative measures. These measures 
are applicable across the country, including Maharashtra.

(d) whether the Ministry has explored the use of substitute materials 
or recycling technologies to reduce dependence on imported 
bitumen, if so, the details thereof?  
ANSWER 
 THE MINISTER OF ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS 
  
(SHRI NITIN JAIRAM GADKARI) 
 
 
(a) to (c)  No shorta ge of bitumen was reported during the Financial 
Year (FY) 2025 -26, accordingly, the pace of construction of National 
Highways (NHs) was not affected for any such causes. 
However, during the current FY 2026-27, pace of construction of 
NHs has been marginally affected  due to short supply of bitumen 
arising out of West Asia crisis. 

NH contracts generally contain provisions for price adjustment 
to address fluctuations in price rise of materials including Bitumen 
during the implementation period. Moreover, in order to mitigate the 
impact of significant increase in price of bitumen and as a special 
relief measure to ensure uninterrupted construction and maintenance 
of NH projects, the Government has issued Cost Escalation 
Compensation Mechanism for bitumen effective upto 30.09.2026. 
For addressing the supply constraints, a Joint Core Committee 
was established including representatives of all stakeholders 
including Oil Manufacturing Companies (OMCs) for day -to-day 
monitoring of bitumen supply. OMCs we re also requested to arrange 
the import of bitumen to avoid supply constraints. 
(d)  The Government has established a framework to reduce the 
demand for bitumen in the construction and maintenance of NH 
projects. The strategy adopted inter -alia includes us e of high -
strength stabilized materials in the underlying pavement layers, 
which reduces the design thickness of bituminous layers and 
consequently the requirement of fresh bitumen. The Government also 
promotes reuse of reclaimed bitumen recovered from exi sting 
bituminous pavements through recycling techniques. 
Further, the Government has issued guidelines from time to 
time for the use of substitute materials and recycling technologies to 
reduce dependence on imported bitumen by way of: 
i. Use of Reclaimed Asphalt Pavement (RAP) with Foamed 
Bitumen   or Bitumen Emulsion in pavement construction and 
rehabilitation; and 
ii. Implementation of Hot In -place Recycling Technology for 
Periodic Renewal (PR) works. 
iii. Promoting use of modified bitumen e.g. C rumb Rubber Modified   
Bitumen (CRMB), Polymer Modified Bitumen (PMB) 
iv. Focus on promoting bio-bitumen  
These measures help in reducing consumption of fresh bitumen, 
conserving natural resources and promoting sustainable construction 
and maintenance of NHs.

IMPROVEMENT IN GROUNDWATER LEVELS 
†3097.  Shri VIVEK THAKUR: 
Will the Minister of JAL SHAKTI be pleased to state: 
(a) whether any improvement has been recorded in th e groundwater levels 
across the identified development blocks in the cou ntry, particularly in Nawada 
and Sheikhpura districts; and 
(b) if so, the details thereof? 
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR JAL SHAKTI  
(SHRI RAJ BHUSHAN CHOUDHARY) 
(a) & (b)  Dynamic Ground Water Resources of the co untry, including Nawada 
and Sheikhpura districts of Bihar are assessed annu ally by the Central Ground 
Water Board (CGWB) jointly with the concerned State  Governments/UT 
Administrations. The assessment estimates the Annua l Ground Water Recharge, 
Annual Extractable Ground Water Resource, Annual Gr ound Water Extraction 
and the Stage of Ground Water Extraction at the ass essment-unit level 
(Block/Mandal/Taluk/Tehsil/District, as applicable) , based on which the 
assessment units are categorised as Safe, Semi-Crit ical, Critical or Over-
exploited. 
A comparison of the Dynamic Ground Water Resources Assessments of 
2020 and 2025 indicates an overall improvement in t he groundwater resource of 
the country. During this period, total Annual Groun d Water Recharge increased 
from 436.15 Billion Cubic Metres (BCM) to 448.52 BC M, while the Annual 
Extractable Ground Water Resource increased from 39 7.62 BCM to 407.75 BCM. 

2 
 
The total Annual Ground Water Extraction for all us es increased marginally from 
244.92 BCM to 247.22 BCM. Consequently, the Stage of Ground Water Extraction 
declined from 61.60 per cent in 2020 to 60.63 per c ent in 2025. Further, the 
proportion of assessment units categorised as Safe increased from 63.56 per 
cent in 2020 to 73.14 per cent in 2025, while the p roportion of Over-exploited 
assessment units declined from 16 per cent to 10.80  per cent,indicating an 
overall improvement in groundwater availability across the country. 
A comparison of the Dynamic Ground Water Resources Assessments of 
2020 and 2025 indicates an improvement in the overa ll groundwater-resource 
position of Nawada district. During this period, th e Annual Ground Water 
Recharge increased from 618.91 Million Cubic Metres  (MCM) to 730.94 MCM, 
while the Annual Extractable Ground Water Resource increased from 558.85 
MCM to 659.61 MCM. Although the Annual Ground Water  Extraction increased 
marginally from 315.21 MCM to 328.46 MCM, the Stage  of Ground Water 
Extraction declined from 56.40 per cent to 49.80 pe r cent. Consequently, the 
overall Stage of Ground Water Extraction remained w ell below 70 per cent and 
the district continued to remain in the Safe catego ry. As per the Dynamic 
Ground Water Resources Assessment, 2025, out of the  14 assessment units in 
the district, 10 are categorised as Safe, 2 as Semi -Critical and 2 as Critical with 
no Over-exploited assessment units. 
In Sheikhpura district, the Annual Ground Water Rec harge increased from 
182.14 MCM in 2020 to 187.04 MCM in 2025, while the  Annual Extractable 
Ground Water Resource increased from 163.93 MCM to 169.73 MCM. However, 
the Annual Ground Water Extraction also increased f rom 87.53 MCM to 99.85 
MCM, resulting in the Stage of Ground Water Extract ion increasing from 53.40 
per cent to 58.83 per cent. Nevertheless, the overa ll Stage of Ground Water 
Extraction remained below 70 per cent and the distr ict continued to remain in 
the Safe category. As per the Dynamic Ground Water Resources Assessment, 
2025, five out of the six assessment units in the d istrict are categorised as Safe 
and one as Critical with no Semi-Critical or Over-exploited assessment units.

through localised action and institutional convergence. The JSA: CTR campaign

The JSA: CTR 2025 was launched with the theme “Jal Sanchay Jan Bhagidari:

convergence and innovative financing mechanisms wit h special focus on 148

To further strengthen the momentum of Jal Shakti Ab hiyan: Catch the

commenced on 1 June 2025 and concluded on 31 May 2026.

Jal Sanchay Jan Bhagidari: Catch the Rain (JSJB: CT R) – 2026 was

Bhagidari (JSJB) initiative and simultaneously inte grating it with the Jal Shakti 
Abhiyan: Catch the Rain (JSA: CTR) campaign. The in itiative focuses on 
intensifying community action and mobilization to b uild low-cost rainwater 
harvesting structures in low cost and saturation mode.  
The objective is to ensure that every drop of water  is conserved through 
collective efforts, following a whole-of-society an d whole-of-government 
approach. By fostering community ownership, the ini tiative seeks to develop 
cost-effective, local solutions at the micro level for water conservation and 
ground water recharge. The initiative is guided by the 3Cs principle—

outcomes. The Government promotes the initiative in  partnership with State

broader community effectively. The progress of the campaign is monitored

UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 3102 
TO BE ANSWERED ON AUGUST 06, 2026 
 
INCENTIVES TO ULBS 
 
NO. 3102 SHRI TRIVENDRA SINGH RAWAT: 
Will the Minister of HOUSING AND URBAN AFFAIRS be pleased to state: 
(a) whether there is any provision to provide additional financial 
assistance, special grants or other resources as incentives to Urban 
Local Bodies (ULBs) securing excellent or high grades in cleanliness 
audits and if so, the details thereof along with the details of the process, 
criteria and the frequency of the said audit; 
(b) if not, whether there is any such proposal under consideration for the 
same and if so, the details thereof; 
(c) whether the drone technology is being used under the Swachh Bharat 
Mission – Urban (SBM-U) for monitoring cleanliness, inspecting waste 
management sites and assessing the cleanliness arrangements in 
public places and if so, the details thereof, State and U LB-wise along 
with the outcomes achieved therefrom; and  
(d) if not, the Government's perspective on using drone technology to make 
cleanliness monitoring more effective and technology-based? 
 
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE  
MINISTRY OF HOUSING AND URBAN AFFAIRS 
(SHRI TOKHAN SAHU) 
 
(a)  and (b):  Swachh Bharat Mission–Urban (SBM-U) 2.0 was launched on 
1 October 2021 for a period of five years, introducing a new component, 
Used Water Management (UWM), with the vision of achieving Garbage Free 
Status for all cities through source segregation, door-to-door collection,  
…2/- 

-2- 
scientific management of all fractions of waste, safe disposal of residual 
waste in scientific landfills, and remediation of all legacy dumpsites in the 
urban areas of the country. 
Under SBM – U 2.0, the total financial outlay of the States and UTs for the 
entire Mission Period is ₹1,41,600 Cr, including committed Central 
Assistance of ₹36,465 Cr.  
Under Solid Waste Management component of SBM-U 2.0 Central Financial 
Assistance (CFA) of fund is provided for setting up various type of municipal 
waste processing facilities such as Material Recovery Facilities (MRFs), 
Waste to Compost (WtC ) plants, Bio -methanation plants, Refused Derived 
Fuel (RDF) processing facilities, Waste to Electricity (WtE) plants, 
Construction and Demolition (C&D) waste plants, sanitary landfill including 
CBG plant. 
Under UWM component, financial assistance is provided to the Urban Local 
Bodies (ULBs) with population less than 1 Lakh for setting up of Sewage 
Treatment Plants ( STPs)/ STP- cum-FSTP and laying Interception and 
Diversion (I&D) structures including provision of pumping stations and 
pumping main/gravity main upto STP etc. 
Further, MoHUA has been conducting an annual cleanliness survey – 
Swachh Survekshan since the year 2016, which has over the years played 
a key role in triggering positive competition amongst cities towards 
achieving the objectives of the Mission. This annual survey ranks cities on 
various cleanliness parameters, conducted through a significantly rigorous 
process, has enthused cities and States/UTs to compete positively with 
each other to be ranked as the cleanest city/ State. Best Ranking cities are 
awarded for their performance. No other incentives are provided to cities 
selected under Swachhta Survekshan.  
(c) and (d): Sanitation is a State subject. State/ULBs are responsible for 
planning, designing, executing, operating and reviewing sanitation and 
solid waste management works in the urban areas of the country, including 
decisions on deployment of technology such as drone- based aerial survey 
for monitoring cleanliness, inspecting waste management sites and 
assessing cleanliness arrangements in public places.

FHTCs UNDER JJM IN THANE DISTRICT 
 
†3105. SHRI BALYA MAMA SURESH GOPINATH MHATRE: 
Will the Minister of JAL SHAKTI be pleased to state: 
(a) the current status of Functional Household Tap Connections (FHTCs) provided under the 
Jal Jeevan Mission (JJM) in Thane district of Maharashtra; 
(b) the manner in which the quality of drinking water and regularity of water supply are being 
monitored; 
(c) the special measures taken by the Government to ensure drinking water supply in areas 
facing water scarcity during the summer season; and 
(d) the timeline fixed by the Government for completion of the pending projects? 
  
  
ANSWER 
  
THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR JAL SHAKTI 
(SHRI V. SOMANNA)  
(a) to (d) Drinking Water is a ‘State’ subject, and hence, under Jal Jeevan Mission (JJM), 
the responsibility of planning, approval, implementation, operation & maintenance of 
drinking water supply schemes lies with State/UT Governments. The Government of India 
supports the States by providing technical and financial assistance. Under JJM, as per 
existing guidelines,  Bureau of Indian Standards’ BIS:10500 standards are adopted as 
benchmark for quality of water being supplied through the piped water supply schemes. 
Significant progress has been made in Thane district of Maharashtra since the launch of Jal 
Jeevan Mission, towards enhancing access to tap water to rural households. At the start of Jal 
Jeevan Mission in August 2019, only 66,075 (25.29%) rural households were reported to 
have tap water connections. As on date, as reported by State, out of 2.61 lakh rural 
households in the district, more than 1.98 lakh (75.93%) households are reported to have tap 
water connections in their homes (Source: JJM-IMIS). 
The following corrective actions have been taken to address and overcome implementation 
deficiencies and ensure qu ality works under JJM in various parts of the country including 
Maharashtra: 
i. Celebration of  Jal Arpan Diwas – for transparent handing over of scheme to 
community where the Local MPs and MLAs are to be invited. 

Page 2 of 2 
 
ii. District Technical Unit (DTU) to be constitute d to monitor and provide support to 
assure the water supply in the Panchayats and villages. 
iii. Jal Sewa Ankalan to be carried out by Panchayat for all the villages. The issues to be 
reviewed by District Technical Unit (DTU) and action to be taken by DWSM. 
iv. Sujalam Bharat database to be used for reporting all the water supply assets of rural 
areas on digital platforms such as JJM IMIS, PM Gati Shakti. 
v. O&M Policy Finalization - Expedite the notification of the State O&M Policy in 
accordance with the national framework. 
vi. Third-Party Inspection Agency (TPIA) of all the works under JJM with 
involvement of district administrative authorities. 
vii. Source and Asset Protection Advisory to be issued by district-level for protection of 
water sources and JJM assets, including pipelines, reservoirs, and pump houses. 
State has informed that water quality testing is carried out regularly during the pre -
monsoon and post -monsoon seasons to ensure that potable water supplied to rural 
households conforms to the prescribed quality standards. The functioning of water supply 
schemes is monitored periodically by the implementing agencies and field functionaries to 
ensure regular and adequate supply of safe drinking water. 
Further, Water being a State subject, steps for augmentation, co nservation and efficient 
management of water resources are primarily undertaken by the respective State 
Governments. To ensure long -term sustainability of drinking water supply, the Mission 
provides for development, strengthening and augmentation of drinki ng water sources, along 
with creation of bulk water transfer, treatment and distribution infrastructure, particularly in 
water-scarce, drought -prone and desert areas. States/UTs have been advised to undertake 
source sustainability measures such as rainwate r harvesting, recharge structures, rejuvenation 
of water bodies and reuse of greywater through convergence with programmes such as VB G 
RAM G erstwhile MGNREGA, Finance Commission tied grants, State schemes and CSR 
initiatives. These efforts are complement ed by national initiatives including Jal Shakti 
Abhiyan: Catch the Rain, Jal Sanchay Jan Bhagidari, the National Aquifer Mapping 
Programme and Atal Bhujal Yojana. 
States/UTs have been advised  to review the status of preparedness at all levels and take all 
possible measures required to keep the piped water supply infrastructure operational and take 
expeditious action to address any gaps to avoid any disruption in drinking water supply 
during the summer period. 
State has planned to complete all pending projects in Thane district by June 2028.

Bhavani Project Canal System, Kodiveri Anicut Irrig ation System and 
Kalingarayan Anicut Canal System taken up under the  Extension, Renovation & 
Modernisation (ERM) Scheme with assistance from NAB ARD.  Further, the 
irrigation situation in the Bhavanisagar Dam comman d area, is reviewed 
continuously by them.  Water releases are scheduled  to maximize irrigation 
benefits while ensuring equitable distribution. 
Government of India has launched a pilot scheme viz . Modernisation of

entries.t: Monitoring of LPG Refills under PMUY
entries.head:
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 3110 
TO BE ANSWERED ON 06th August, 2026 
 
Monitoring of LPG Refills under PMUY 
 
3110. Shri Sasikanth Senthil:  
 
पेĚोͧलयम एवं Ĥाकृ Ǔतक गैस मंğी 
 
 Will the Minister of PETROLEUM AND NATURAL GAS be pleased to state: 
 
(a) whether the Government monitors the average number of LPG refills under Pradhan 
Mantri Ujjwala Yojana (PMUY) availed per Ujjwala beneficiary and if so, the details thereof, 
State/UT-wise along with the average number of refills during each of the last three years; 
 
(b) whether the refill frequency among Ujjwala beneficiaries is affected by affordability, 
subsidy support or the price of the cylinders; and 
 
(c) if so, the details thereof along with the subsidy provided and the steps taken to ensure 
sustained use of LPG usage by beneficiaries? 
 
ANSWER 
 
पेĚोͧलयम एवं Ĥाकृ Ǔतक गैस मंğालय मɅ राÏयमंğी 
(Įी सुरेश गोपी) 
 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF PETROLEUM AND NATURAL GAS 
(SHRI SURESH GOPI) 
 
(a) to (c): Yes. Government regularly monitors the LPG consumption of PMUY beneficiaries 
through Petroleum Planning and Analysis Cell (PPAC’s) Consumption reports, Common 
LPG Database Platform (CLDP) & reviews with PSU OMCs. Consumption of domestic LPG 
by households depends on several factors like food habits, household size, cooking habits, 
tradition, flavor, taste, preferences, price, availability of alternate fuels etc.  
 
State/UT-wise details of Per Connection Consumption during the last three years are given at 
Annexure-A. 
 
In order to encourage sustained usage and address the issue of low refill consumption among 
PMUY beneficiaries, various steps have been taken inter alia, including organizing 
campaigns for improving awareness about PMUY , promotion through Out of Home (OOH) 
hoardings, radio jingles, Information, Education and Communication (IEC) Vans etc. In 
addition, PMUY beneficiaries have been given option to swap from 14.2 kg to 5 Kg to reduce 
upfront cash outgo and option of 5 Kg Double Bottle Connection. 

As a result of various steps taken by Government to improve access and affordability of 
domestic LPG for PMUY consumers, per connection consumption of PMUY beneficiaries (in 
terms of no. of 14.2 kg LPG cylinders taken per year) has increased from 3.68 in FY 2021-22 
to 4.71 in FY 2025-26.  
 
India imports majority of its LPG requirement & LPG prices in the country are based on 
Saudi CP. The average Saudi CP (the international benchmark for LPG pricing) rose upto 
US$ 780/MT in April and May 2026. In June 2026, as the Saudi CP rose further to US$ 
796/MT (excluding premium), the Market Determined Price (MDP) of a 14.2 kg domestic 
LPG cylinder went upto Rs. 1,695 per 14.2 Kg cylinder.  
 
The Retail Selling Price of domestic LPG is being maintained at Rs. 942 per 14.2 Kg cylinder 
since June 2026, which carried an implicit subsidy (under-recovery) of more than Rs 700 per 
14.2 Kg cylinder in June 2026 and Rs 500 per cylinder during July 2026. Even for the month 
of August 2026, the RSP carries an implicit subsidy of Rs. 188 per cylinder. For more than 
10.5 crore PMUY consumers, the effective price is only Rs. 642 per cylinder (Delhi), after a 
targeted subsidy of Rs. 300 per cylinder.

entries.t: Status of Chardham Mahamarg Vikas Pariyojana
entries.head:
GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS 
  
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 3111 
ANSWERED ON 06th AUGUST, 2026 
  
Status of Chardham Mahamarg Vikas Pariyojana 
  
3111. Shri Rao Rajendra Singh: 
Will the Minister of ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS  
  
सड़क परिवहन औि िाजमार्ग मंत्री 
be pleased to state: 
(a)  the current status of the Chardham Mahamarg Vikas Pariyojana, 
including the extent of road development completed so far; 
(b) the progress made under  the Chardham Mahamarg Vikas 
Pariyojana in providing All -weather road connectivity to the 
Chardham pilgrimage sites; and 
(c) the challenges encountered in the implementation of the 
Chardham Mahamarg Vikas Pariyojana and the measures taken by 
the Goverment to ensure its timely completion? 
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS 
(SHRI NITIN JAIRAM GADKARI) 
(a) to (c)     Chardham Mahamarg Vikas Pariyojana comprises 
improvement of 5 existing National Highways (NHs) connecting 
Chardham viz., Yamunotri , Gangotri, Kedarnath and Badrinath 
including Tanakpur to Pithoragarh section of Kailas -Mansarovar 
yatra, aggregating a length of about 825 km. Out of 825 km length, 
640 km length has been completed.  
          Under the directions of Hon’ble Supreme Court , in August 
2019, a High Powered Committee (HPC) was constituted comprising 

representatives from various reputed institutes such as Physical 
Research Laboratory, Wildlife Institute of India, Wadia Institute of 
Himalayan Geology, Central Soil Conservation R esearch Institute, 
National Institute of Disaster Management, Forest Research 
Institute etc. with mandate to consider the cumulative and 
independent impact of Chardham Projects on the entire Himalayan 
Valleys and give directions in respect of environmental  impacts. In 
addition, Hon'ble Supreme Court also directed to set up an 
"Oversight Committee" to ensure the implementation of the 
recommendations given in the report of aforesaid HPC especially 
the strategic roads viz. Rishikesh – Mana, Rishikesh – Gangotri and 
Tanakpur - Pithoragarh. The Committees meet on regular basis and 
their recommendations are implemented during the execution of 
works.  
The implementation of these projects has encountered several 
challenges, including environmental and ecological con cerns, 
delays in Land Acquisitions (LA) & obtaining forest clearances, 
difficult Himalayan terrain, frequent landslides and adverse weather 
conditions.  
The Government has taken various steps to address these 
challenges such as: 
i. Coordination with local adm inistration & concerned 
departments for Land Acquisition (LA) & Forest Clearance (FC) 
ii.  Regular review meetings with contractors and State 
Authorities at various levels to resolve bottlenecks. 
iii. Rapid Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA) in compliance 
of Hon’ble Court order. 
iv. Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) signed with Tehri Hydro 
Development Corporation India Ltd. (THDCIL) for specialized 
landslide treatment measures for the State of Uttarakhand. 
v. Decision taken in November, 2024 for implementation of 
“Cost-effective Long -term Remedial Measures of Landslide 
Prone areas in Hilly region” as per Expert Committee Report. 

vi. Decision taken in November, 2025 through policy initiative on 
"Additional Augmented and Systematic Remedial Measures to 
Address concerns regardi ng Construction of National 
Highways in Hilly Regions and Amendments to the Request For 
Proposal (RFP) for Detailed Project Report/Engineering, 
Procurement and Construction (DPR/EPC) Document thereof” 
in order to: 
a. improve the quality of DPRs; 
b. ensure adequa te provisions of hill slope protection 
measures; 
c. improvement in construction practice in hilly terrain;  
d. ensure implementation of slope cutting and stabilization 
works in the first instance to be followed up by road 
construction works for NHs in Hilly/Mountainous terrain; 
e. monitoring and early warning system for potential 
landslides. 
vii. Decision taken in July, 2026 through policy initiatives on 
“Specification including mandatory Certification and Quality 
Assurance for Rockfall Mitigation Measures for National 
Highways Projects” elaborating comprehensively on necessary 
checks and balances regarding ensuring adherence to quality 
standards and obligations of contractors and field offices. 
viii. MoU signed with Defence Geo -informatics Research 
Establishment (DGRE) for Te chnological collaboration of Geo -
hazard mitigation measures on NHs. 
ix. MoU signed with Geological Survey of India (GSI) on 
Geological investigation for tunnels and sharing of data for 
Geohazard Studies.  
x. Research scheme taken up through Indian Institute of 
Technology (IIT) Roorkee for Development of Guidelines for 
the Assessment of Hillslope Instability using Instrumentation 
& Real Time Monitoring. 
*****

entries.t: Villages Certified as "ODF Plus Model" in Odisha
entries.head:
Page 1 of 2 
 
GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF JAL SHAKTI 
DEPARTMENT OF DRINKING WATER AND SANITATION 
  
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 3112 
ANSWERED ON 06.08.2026 
  
VILLAGES CERTIFIED AS "ODF PLUS MODEL" IN ODISHA 
  
3112. SMT. APARAJITA SARANGI: 
  
Will the Minister of JAL SHAKTI be pleased to state: 
  
(a) the percentage of villages in Odisha certified as “ODF Plus Model” through independent  
verification as against those self-declared on the national portal; 
(b) the steps taken to bridge the operational gaps preventing ODF Plus villages from achieving 
Model status; 
(c) whether the Government proposes to provide dedicated Operation and Maintenance funding 
for peri-urban Gram Panchayats facing high-density waste generation near urban centres such 
as Bhubaneswar and if so, the details thereof; and 
(d) the mechanisms established to sustain daily solid and liquid waste management operations 
including collection machinery and payment of workers' wages in rural Gram Panchayats 
lacking adequate local revenue sources? 
  
ANSWER 
  
THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR JAL SHAKTI 
(SHRI V. SOMANNA) 
 
(a) Sanitation is a State subject. Swachh Bharat Mission (Grameen) Phase II [SBM(G) -Phase 
II], is a Centrally Sponsored Scheme, implemented by the State and Union Territory 
Governments, including Odisha, in rural areas within their respective jurisdictions. SBM(G) -
Phase II is being implemented during the period from 2020-21 to 2026-27, with focus on Open 
Defecation Free (ODF) sustainability and to cover all the villages with solid and liquid waste 
management (SLWM) arrangements with visual cleanliness i.e. converting villages from ODF 
to ODF Plus (Model).  The operational guidelines provide for system for self -declaration of 
villages followed by verification to be conducted as per prescribed timelines.  As per data 
reported by the State on the SBM(G) Integrated Management Informatio n System (IMIS) 
45,052 villages of Odisha have been declared as ODF Plus (Model) as on 31 st July, 2026. Out 
of these, 44,921(99.7%) villages are reported to have been 1 st verified and 37,271(82.3%) 
villages are reported to have been 2nd verified, as on 31st July 2026. 

Page 2 of 2 
 
  
(b) Under Swachh Bharat Mission (Grameen) [SBM(G)] Phase -II, Department of Drinking 
Water and Sanitation (DDWS), Ministry of Jal Shakti, Government of India has been providing 
financial and technical support to the States/UTs, including Odisha, for implementation of the 
programme. 
SBM(G) Phase II operational guidelines promote decentralized planning where people 
collectively analyze their current situation, decide the improvement that they intend to achieve 
and accordingly identify interventi on for achieving the desired levels of service and 
improvements. Planning under SBM(G) Phase II will be done at three levels i.e. each Gram 
Panchayat (GP) will prepare Village Action Plan which would act as a resource for input into 
the Gram Panchayat Deve lopment Plan (GPDP) as well as for the subsequent formulation of 
the respective District Swachhata Plans; District will prepare  a District Swachhata Plan after 
consolidating  Village Action Plans of its GPs and incorporating the interventions to be taken 
up at Block and District levels for the implementation of SBM(G) Phase II; States/UTs 
Governments would develop a Project Implementation Plan and Annual Implementation Plans 
(AIPs) every year consolidating the Distrct Swachhata Plans to achieve the objecti ves of 
SBM(G) Phase II in a comprehensive and participatory manner. Through this decentralized 
planning States/ UTs are  also expected to undertake gap assessment and plan for way ahead 
and steps to be taken to bridge the operational gaps for achieving ODF Plus status for villages. 
(c) & (d) SBM(G) Phase II is a Centrally Sponsored Scheme. As per SBM(G) Phase II 
guidelines, there is no provision for financial incentive for the Operation and Maintenance 
(O&M) of sanitation assets and infrastructure. The O&M r equirements can be met by the 
respective  States/UTs and their Rural Local Bodies (RLBs) through Finance Commission 
Grants, local revenues, CSR funds, revenue generation models or other available funding 
sources based on their needs and   local preferences, including for sustaining daily solid and 
liquid waste management operations and payment of workers' wages in rural Gram Panchayats. 
  
*****

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF POWER 
 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO.3113 
ANSWERED ON 06.08.2026 
 
ELECTRIFICATION OF TRIBAL HOUSEHOLDS 
 
3113. SHRI K RADHAKRISHNAN:  
ADV DEAN KURIAKOSE: 
 
 Will the Minister of POWER 
be pleased to state: 
 
(a) the details of tribal households electrified under various Government schemes 
since 2019, State/UT-wise and year-wise;  
 
(b) the details of average daily hours of electricity supplied in Scheduled Areas 
and Tribal majority districts since 2024, State/UT -wise, year -wise and feeder -
wise;  
 
(c) the details of villages in Scheduled Areas experiencing power supply of less 
than twelve hours per day on average since 2024, State/UT -wise and year-wise; 
and  
 
(d) the steps taken to strengthen transmission and distribution infrastructure in 
tribal and remote areas? 
A N S W E R 
 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF POWER  
 
(SHRI SHRIPAD NAIK)  
 
(a) to (d): Electricity being a concurrent subject, supply and distribut ion of 
electricity to all consumers, including tribal households, is within the purview of 
the respective distribution utility which functions under the guidance of the 
respective State Government and State Electricity Regulatory Commission. 
Further, as per the Electricity (Rights of Consumers) Rules, 2020, the distribution 
licensee shall supply 24x7 power to all consumers. However, the State 
Commission may specify lower hours of supply for some categories of 
consumers. The Rules are applicable for all Stat es and for all areas, including 
Scheduled Areas and tribal majority districts.  
 
On the transmission side, Government of India (GoI) engages with the State 
for developing the transmission plan and for executing the inter -state 
transmission network. The intra-state transmission network is developed by the 
state. A total of 2,18,267 ckm of transmission lines, 9,47,405 MVA of 
transformation capacity and 84,390 MW of inter -regional transmission capacity 
have been added since 2014, strengthening the ability to t ransfer power across 
the country, including to tribal and remote areas. 
 
On the distribution side, GoI supplements the efforts of the States through 
various schemes to help them achieve the objective of providing quality supply 
of power. 

Works amounting to  Rs. 1.85 lakh crore were executed under the earlier 
schemes of DDUGJY, Integrated Power Development Scheme (IPDS) and 
SAUBHAGYA. Presently, under Revamped Distribution Sector Scheme (RDSS), 
works amounting Rs. 1.53 lakh crore for loss reduction infrastructure and Rs. 1.31 
lakh crore for smart metering have been sanctioned. 
 
Further, under Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Gram Jyoti Yojana (DDUGJY) 
launched in 2014, and thereafter under Pradhan Mantri Sahaj Bijli Har Ghar Yojana 
(SAUBHAGYA) launched in October, 2017, electrification of all willing households, 
including tribal households, was completed by 31st March, 2019 as reported by 
the States/ UTs. A total of 2.86 crore households were electrified during the 
SAUBHAGYA period including tribal households. Both the schemes stand closed 
as on 31.03.2022.  
 
Under the ongoing RDSS, launched in July 2021, based on the surveys 
conducted by the States, electrification works have been sanctioned for 
households left out earlier. Since most of the left -out households are in remo te, 
hilly and forest areas, the norms for household electrification under RDSS were 
relaxed and the ceiling limit for cost of electrification was enhanced. Grid based 
electrification works have been sanctioned under RDSS, wherever found feasible, 
as per the revised norms, and off-grid solar based electrification has been taken 
up under the New Solar Power Scheme, where grid supply is not feasible.  
 
Works amounting to Rs. 6,522 crore for 13.65 lakh households have been 
sanctioned under RDSS, including for p ublic places. This includes sanction for 
1,27,987 households belonging to Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Groups (PVTGs) 
identified under Pradhan Mantri Janjati Adivasi Nyaya Maha Abhiyan (PM -
JANMAN) and 2,83,558 households belonging to Scheduled Tribes ide ntified 
under Dharti Aaba Janjatiya Gram Utkarsh Abhiyan (DA-JGUA). In addition, 52,439 
households in the States of Gujarat, Odisha and West Bengal have been taken up 
under the respective State Plans. Till date, 4.88 lakh households have been 
electrified, including 2,77,256 PVTG and tribal households. Under the New Solar 
Power Scheme, works have been sanctioned for off -grid solar based 
electrification of 8,823 PVTG households under PM -JANMAN and 4,099 tribal 
households under DA -JGUA. Till date, 11,838 PVTG and tribal households have 
been electrified under the said scheme. ( State/UT wise details of household 
electrification for PVTG and Tribal households is enclosed as Annexure-I). 
 
Further, for remote and border areas of the country, works amounting to 
Rs.1,164 crores have been sanctioned for strengthening of electricity 
infrastructure in Nor

entries.t: Rectification of Black Spots on NHs in Andhra Pradesh
entries.head:
GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS 
  
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO- 3115 
ANSWERED ON- 06TH AUGUST, 2026 
RECTIFICATION OF BLACK SPOTS ON NHs IN ANDHRA PRADESH 
  
3115. SHRI PRABHAKAR REDDY VEMIREDDY: 
 
Will the Minister of ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS 
  
सड़क परिवहन औि िाजमार्ग मंत्री 
be pleased to state: 
  
(a) the status of short -term and long -term rectification of identified 
black spots on National Highways in Andhra Pradesh, district -wise; 
and  
(b) the steps taken to conduct periodic road safety audits and 
identify new accident -prone locations on National Highways in 
Andhra Pradesh? 
 
ANSWER 
  
THE MINISTER OF ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS 
  
(SHRI NITIN JAIRAM GADKARI) 
  
(a) & (b) Certain continuous stretches on National Highways (NHs) 
have been identified qualifying the criteria of black spots i.e. 
locations with occurrence of certain number of accidents involving 
fatalities and grievous injuries. These stretches have been 
identified on real -time basis through AI based tools developed by 
Indian Institute of Technology (IIT), Kanpur. Based on the available 
accident data from Electronic Detailed Accident Report (e -DAR) for 
the period 2023 –2025, 6,358 Black spot corridors have been 

identified. The district-wise list of the black corridors in the State of 
Andhra Pradesh is annexed. 
Rectification of black spots is a continuous process. Short -term 
measures for immediate rectification of black corridors include road 
markings, signages, cras h barriers, road studs, delineators, closure 
of unauthorized median openings, traffic calming measures, 
highway lighting etc. Long -term measures for rectification of black 
corridors like improvement of road geometrics, junction 
improvements, spot widening of carriageway, construction of 
underpasses/overpasses, etc. are also taken as permanent 
rectification measures as per site requirement. Long term 
rectification works involve pre -construction activities such as land 
acquisition, forest clearance & utility shifting which takes 
significant time. 
Road Safety Audit is carried out for the independent assessment of 
newly constructed National Highways before opening them to 
public. All identified road safety issues, including those related to 
road signage and markings, are addressed before the road is opened 
to the public. Subsequently, during the operation of the project 
highway, assessment is carried out at regular intervals to identify 
safety issues that may have emerged during operation stage and 
any necessary remedial measures are taken in a time -bound 
manner. Besides this, accident data on all existing and new 
National Highways is monitored on a pan -India basis through 
the eDAR portal (electronic Detailed Accident Report), and accident 
spots are identified. Fu rther, all field officers have been delegated 
powers to take advance remedial action on these identified 
accident spots, preventing them from converting to blackspots.

BLACK SPOTS ON RAJGANJ-GOVINDPUR NH STRETCH IN 
DHANBAD 
  
3116.    SHRI DULU MAHATO:  
  
Will the Minister of ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS 
सड़क परिवहन औि िाजमार्ग मंत्री 
be pleased to state:  
  
(a) whether the Ministry is aware of the reported 91 deaths and 15 
black spots on the Rajganj –Govindpur stretch of National Highway 
(NH) in Dhanbad district during the period from January t o April, 
2026, if so, the details thereof;  
(b) the immediate engineering measures being undertaken to rectify 
road design deficiencies, unauthorized openings and high -risk black 
spots on the said National Highway (NH) stretch;  
(c) the timeline fixed for repair and restoration of non -functional 
streetlights on the corridor to address poor visibility and fatal night -
time accidents;  
(d) whether safety infrastructure such as foot overbridges, zebra 
crossings, rumble strips and Closed -Circuit Television (CCTV ) 
cameras are being installed for enhancement of road safety and 
traffic monitoring on the said stretch, if so, the details thereof; and  
(e) the enforcement measures being undertaken to curb wrong -side 
driving, over -speeding and drunken driving for protec tion of 
pedestrians and two -wheeler riders on the said National Highway 
(NH) stretch?   
ANSWER 
  
THE MINISTER OF ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS 
(SHRI NITIN JAIRAM GADKARI)  

(a) to (c) Total 8 numbers of black spots were identified as per 
the  Black Spot series 2021-23 issued by the Government in Ministry 
of Road Transport &  Highways between the stretch from Rajganj to 
Govindpur. Out of this, 5 black spots have already been rectified by 
providing underpass, foot overbridge, service road, & other saf ety 
measures during 6-lane widening of NH -19. The remaining 3 number 
of black spots at Chainages 407+500, 408+120, and 410+180 fall 
within the 6 -lane Govindpur Elevated project stretch and will be 
rectified  upon completion of the elevated corridor. The sc heduled 
completion date of the project is March 2028. Further, unauthorized 
openings are regularly being closed with the help of District 
Administration. 
  
Moreover, all the streetlights along the project corridor are currently 
functional, and defects, if any, during the operation period are being 
rectified. 
(d) & (e) 03 numbers of Foot Over Bridge (FOB), rumble marking 
and other safety measures have been provided and Closed -Circuit 
Television (CCTV) cameras at 2 km intervals have been installed for 
traffic monitoring. Further, road safety campaigns/awareness 
programmes are being conducted in coordination with State 
Government/District Administration on regular basis to curb wrong -
side driving, over-speeding and drunken driving etc.

DEPARTMENT OF WATER RESOURCES, RIVER DEVELOPMENT & GANGA 
REJUVENATION 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 3120 
ANSWERED ON 06.08.2026 
FLOODING IN PUNJAB 
3120.   Smt. HARSIMRAT KAUR BADAL: 
Will the Minister of JAL SHAKTI be pleased to state: 
(a) whether the Government is aware that half of Pu njab faces floods and 
thousands of villages are submerged causing loss of  human lives, cattle and 
crops every year and if so, the details thereof; 
(b) whether the Government is aware that at the tim e of scarcity, water from 
Punjab is diverted to other States and during the m onsoon season, excess 
water is released into Punjab causing unprecedented  floods and if so, the 
details thereof; 
(c) whether the Government acknowledges that the ab sence of adequate 
representation of Punjab officers and reduced decis ion-making powers have 
contributed to recurring water flooding situations in the State during the last 
few years and if so, the details thereof; and 
(d) whether the Government has taken note that Punj ab itself suffers record 
inundation because there is no responsible authorit y from Punjab in Bhakra 
Beas Management Board (BBMB) to regulate, anticipat e or control such 
situations, if so, the details thereof and the reac tion of the Government 
thereto? 
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR JAL SHAKTI  
(SHRI RAJ BHUSHAN CHOUDHARY) 
 

2 
 
(a)  The country including Punjab experiences flood s of varying degree in 
different  years. As per the report of the Central Water Commission 
“Assessment of Area Affected Due to Floods in India ”, based on satellite 
imagery data for the period from 1986 to 2022, the total flood-affected area in 
Punjab has been assessed as 0.121 million hectares (Mha) and the area 
protected through various steps taken towards flood  management by the 
Central/State Government has been assessed as 3.19 Mha. The data regarding 
loss of human lives, cattle, and crops due to flood s are not maintained 
centrally.  
  
(b) to (d)  As informed by the Bhakra Beas Manageme nt Board (BBMB), the 
release of water throughout the year is regulated b y an Inter-State Technical 
Committee comprising stakeholders, in accordance wi th the water 
requirements, after obtaining consensus among the p artner states. While 
determining reservoir releases, BBMB takes into con sideration several key 
factors, including reservoir storage availability, the States' allocated 
shares/quotas, prevailing and forecast catchment co nditions, reservoir rule 
curves, dam safety considerations, and any specific  operational issues raised 
by the partner States.  
BBMB regulates the distribution of waters of the Ra vi, Beas and Sutlej 
rivers among partner States in accordance with the applicable inter-State 
agreements of 1959 on construction of Bhakra Nangal  Project between Punjab 
& Rajasthan and of 1981 between the States of Punjab, Haryana & Rajasthan. 
As per the Punjab Reorganization Act, 1966, the BBMB consists of: 
i. a whole-time Chairman and two whole-time members to  be 
appointed by the Central Government;  
ii. a representative each of Governments of the States of Punjab, 
Haryana,  Rajasthan & Himachal Pradesh,  
iii. two representatives of Central Government.  

3 
 
As per past precedence, one Whole Time Member, name ly Member 
(Power) in BBMB, is appointed from the State of Pun jab. Further, the State of 
Punjab has been represented by the Principal Secret ary, Water Resources 
Department, Government of Punjab in the Board. 
Accordingly, adequate representation of the State o f Punjab exists in 
both the decision-making process of the Board and t he Technical Committee 
responsible for regulating reservoir operations and  water releases from the 
dam. 
The partner States project their irrigation and dom estic water 
requirements during the monthly meetings of the Tec hnical Committee of the 
BBMB. Based on the decisions taken in these meeting s, BBMB regulates water 
releases from the reservoirs. The Technical Committ ee comprises Chief 
Engineers of the partner States (Punjab, Haryana an d Rajasthan), 
representatives of the Central Water Commission, and Special Invitees from the 
Indian Meteorological Department, Agriculture Depar tment and senior officers 
from BBMB, among others.

entries.t: Tribal Land Rights and Consent in Projects
entries.head:
GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF TRIBAL AFFAIRS 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION No. 3121  
To Be Answered On- 06/08/2026 
  
Tribal Land Rights and Consent in Projects   
3121. Shri Vijay Kumar Hansdak:   
Will the Minister of TRIBAL AFFAIRS be pleased to state:  
(a) the details of tribal land diversion proposals approved since 2019 under the Forest Rights Act, 2006 and 
the Panchayats (Extension to Scheduled Areas) Act, 1996 indicating area diverted and the number of 
affected tribal households, State-wise; 
(b) whether compliance with Gram Sabha consent and recognition of Forest Rights prior to diversion of 
tribal land has been assessed since 2019 and if so, the year-wise details of assessments conducted, cases of 
non compliance identified and action taken thereon; 
(c) the details of disputes relating to land acquisition, rehabilitation and implementation of Gram Sabha 
consent provisions in mining and other diversion projects in Scheduled Areas since 2019 including number 
of cases and stage of resolution, State-wise and year-wise; and 
(d) the status since 2021 of rehabilitation measures and pending legal or administrative disputes in projects 
involving diversion of tribal land in Scheduled Areas, project-wise? 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE FOR TRIBAL AFFAIRS 
(SHRI DURGA DAS UIKEY)  
(a):      Department of Land Resources (DoLR), Ministry of Rural Development is Nodal Ministry at the 
Centre for land related matters and has informed that Land and its management fall under the exclusive 
legislative and administrative jurisdiction of States as provided under the Constitution of India (Seventh 
Schedule- List II (State List)- Entry No. (18). Further, land acquisition and associated rehabilitation is 
undertaken by the Central and State Governments under various Central and State Acts. 
Ministry of Environment, Forest & Climate Change (MoEF&CC) has informed that proposals for 
use of forest land for non-forestry purposes are processed online through PARIVESH portal 
(https://parivesh.nic.in). Information relating to forest land proposed for diversion, category of proposal, 
details of the User Agency, current status of proposals, project affected trees, etc. is available on the 
PARIVESH Portal. 
Section 3(2) of the Scheduled Tribes and Other Traditional Forest Dwellers (Recognition of Forest 
Rights) Act, 2006 provides for minimal diversion of forest land for specific development facilities managed 
by the Government, subject to the condition that the extent of such diversion shall not exceed one hectare 
in each case and shall require the recommendation of the concerned Gram Sabha. The details to diversion 
of tribal land are not centrally maintained by Ministry of Tribal Affairs (MoTA). 
Further, Ministry of Panchayati Raj (MoPR), being administrative Ministry of implementation of 
Panchayats (Extension to Scheduled Areas) Act, 1996 has informed that all matters relating to Panchayats, 
including land related matters of rural areas, fall within the purview of concerned State Governments and 
neither the State Governments have furnished details of such cases to MoPR nor does the MoPR maintain 
such details. 
  
(b): As informed by MoEF&CC, provisions of Rule No. 11 (7) of the Van (Sanrakshan evam Samvardhan) 
Rules, 2023 provides that the State Government or Union territory Administration can issue order for 
diversion, assignment of lease or de-reservation, as the case may be, only after  receiving the ‘Final’ 
approval of the Central Government under sub-section (1) of section 2 of the Adhiniyam, and after 

fulfilment and compliance of the provisions of all other Acts and rules made thereunder, as applicable 
including ensuring settlement of rights under the Scheduled Tribes and Other Traditional Forest Dwellers 
(Recognition of Forest Rights) Act, 2006 (2 of 2007). Further, MoTA has been exhorting the State 
Governments and UT Administrations to ensure that no rightful beneficiary is deprived of their forest rights 
including compliance of Section 4 (5) of FRA which stipulates that the claimants cannot be evicted or 
removed from forest land under his occupation till the recognition and verification procedure is complete. 
(c) & (d):  Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement (R&R) of Project Affected Families, 
including its implementation and disbursement of compensation, is being dealt with by the respective State 
Government/Project Authority. Therefore, details of disputes relating to land acquisition, rehabilitation and 
implementation of Gram Sabha consent provisions in mining and other diversion projects is not centrally 
maintained by MoTA.  
MoEF&CC has informed that the proposals for diversion of forest land received from the States/UTs 
are examined in accordance with the provisions of the Van (Sanrakshan Evam Samvardhan) Adhiniyam, 
1980, and the Rules and Guidelines made thereunder. 
Grievances/ representations when received in the Ministry regarding violation of provisions

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF CIVIL AVIATION 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. : 3124 
 ( TO BE ANSWERED ON THE  6th August 2026 )  
EXPANSION OF MANGALURU INTERNATIONAL AIRPORT  
3124.    SHRI CAPTAIN BRIJESH CHOWTA              
Will the Minister of CIVIL AVIATION 
be pleased to state:- 
(a) whether the Government has reviewed the aviation skilling and maintenance ecosystem 
and the current operational, traffic, facility and proposal status of Mangaluru International 
Airport and if so, the details thereof; 
(b) the details of the passenger and cargo traffic data, capacity, approvals, investments and 
service indicators of Mangaluru International Airport; 
(c) the details of the infrastructure, regulatory, airline, land, skill and coordination constraints 
affecting the expansion of aviation ecosystem and airport capacity; and 
(d) the time -bound facilitation and capacity enhancement plan for Mangaluru International 
Airport? 
ANSWER 
Minister of State in the Ministry of CIVIL AVIATION      (Shri Murlidhar 
Mohol) 
(a): The Government has undertaken various measures to strengthen the aviation skilling and 
aircraft Maintenance, Repair and Overhaul (MRO) ecosystem in the country.  
 
As part of the Union Budget 2026 -27, 'nil' Basic Customs Duty (BCD) has been provided on 
components or parts, including engines, for the manufacture of aircraft and the manufacture 
of parts required for such aircraft. Further, the BCD exemption on parts, testing equipment, 
tools and tool -kits required for aircraft MRO has been extended till 31st M arch, 2028. As a 
result of these initiatives, the number of domestic MROs in India has increased from 96 in 
2014 to 164 as of March 2026.;; 
 
The Government has also taken measures to strengthen pilot training capacity and 
infrastructure in the country. The  Civil Aviation Requirements (CAR) Section 7, Series D, 
Part I prescribe an Aircraft:Instructor:Cadet ratio of 1:1:10, corresponding to a training 
capacity of approximately 3500 cadets at the approved FTOs at any given time. The measures 
taken also include: 
(i) Simplifying and streamlining the approval and oversight process for Flying Training 
Organisations. 
(ii) Revising training regulations to improve efficiency and optimise utilisation of training 
resources. 
(iii) Introducing a ranking framework for FTO s to promote quality and safety in pilot 
training.; 

(iv) To enhance flying hours availability, the inflight visibility criteria has been conditionally 
revised to 3 Kms from earlier 5 Kms under the Flight Training Circular 01 of 2025. 
(v) DGCA has revised CAR Section 7, Series I, Part V and Designated Examiner's Manual by 
delinking the examiner function from the Certified Flight Instructor (CFI)/Dy. CFI role, 
delegating Flight Instructor Rating checks to FTOs, expanding qualified examiner pool, 
reducing cool-off period to 30 days for appearing in second attempt of Oral exam for CFI, 
Dy. CFI & Designated Examiner. 
(vi) The frequency of oral examinations/boards for Assistant Flight Instructors (AFIs) and 
Flight Instructors (FIs) has been increased to a monthly basis.;; 
 
Training programmes for aviation manpower are aligned with the DGCA -approved training 
and procedures manual, emerging skill requirements of the aviation sector through active 
collaboration with industry stakeholders, including periodic curriculu m revision. 
Requirements are periodically reviewed by DGCA and are kept in line with International 
Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO) framework. 
 
(b) Mangaluru International Airport handled 2.56 million passengers, 18917 Air Traffic 
Movements (ATMs) and 58 51.74 tonnes of cargo for FY 2025 -26. The airport has a 
passenger handling capacity of 3.2 Million Passengers Per Annum (MPPA). The airport has 
been awarded the ACI Level 5 Customer Experience Accreditation and has also been 
recognized as the World's Best Airport for Arrivals based on Airport Service Quality (ASQ) 
survey ratings. 
 
(c)Mangaluru International Airport has a runway (06 -24) measuring 2330 m * 45 m, a new 
integrated terminal building with an area of 48572 sq. m. and an integrated cargo terminal 
with a capacity of 9000 metric tonnes per annum. The airport is presently served by Air India 
Express and IndiGo. The airport currently has 583.77 acres of land.; 
 
(d) The expansion and modernization of airports is a continuous process undertaken by 
Airport Operators based on land availability, commercial viability, socio -economic 
considerations and traffic demand or the willingness of airlines to commence or enhance 
operations.

†3125. SHRI SANATAN PANDEY: 
 
 Will the Minister of POWER 
be pleased to state: 
 
(a) whether funds have been allocated under various Central Government 
schemes, such as Smart Grid Distribution System Strengthening, Sub-Station and 
Transmission Infrastructure, etc. for strengthening the energy sector in Uttar 
Pradesh, particularly in Ballia Parliamentary Constituency;  
 
(b) the details of funds allocated and actually utilized for each district of Uttar 
Pradesh and particularly for Ballia district during the last three years, scheme -
wise;  
 
(c) the number of consumers, farmers, institutions and other beneficiaries who 
have received direct benefits under these schemes in Ballia Parliamentary 
Constituency; and  
 
(d) wheth er the Government has prepared any new action plan to expedite 
completion of pending projects and further strengthen energy infrastructure and 
if so, the details thereof? 
A N S W E R 
 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF POWER  
 
(SHRI SHRIPAD NAIK)  
 
(a) to (c):  Government of India launched the Revamped Distribution Sector 
Scheme (RDSS) in July 2021 with the objective of improving the quality of power 
supply through a financially sustainable and operationally efficient distribution 
sector.  
 
Under the s cheme, financial assistance is being provided to the 
distribution utilities for loss reduction infrastructure works and smart metering 
works. For the State of Uttar Pradesh, based on proposal submitted by the State, 
projects worth Rs. 21,782 crore for loss reduction infrastructure and Rs. 18,956 
crore for smart metering works have been sanctioned. 
 

For Ballia Lok Sabha Constituency, projects worth Rs. 202.62 crore for loss 
reduction infrastructure and Rs. 176.56 crore for smart metering works have 
been sanctioned under RDSS. 
 
The district-wise details of funds allocated for the State of Uttar Pradesh 
under RDSS are at Annexure. 
 
As per the guidelines, the funds are released at the DISCOM level and 
therefore the district-wise utilisation is provided at the time of project closure. 
The works sanctioned under RDSS in the Ballia Parliamentary Constituency and 
their physical progress are as follows:

Under the Green Energy Corridor (GEC) scheme, the intra -state 
transmission system in Uttar Pradesh is being strengthened to facili tate 
evacuation of power from renewable energy (RE)-rich areas. The transmission 
system under GEC -II is currently under implementation and envisages the 
development of 2,567 ckm of transmission lines along with 10,440 MVA of 
transformation capacity. As of June 2026, all 28 projects under GEC -II in Uttar 
Pradesh have been awarded.  
 
Through above Schemes, all consumers, farmers, institutions, and other 
beneficiaries will get benefit from improved reliability and quality of power 
supply. 
 

 
 
 
(d):  Monitoring and review of works sanctioned under RDSS is being done by 
the Nodal Agencies, namely, PFC Ltd and REC Ltd on a regular basis. Further, an 
institutional mechanism at the State level i.e., Distribution Reforms Committee 
headed by Chief Secretary of the Stat e concerned, and at the Central level i.e., 
Inter-Ministerial Monitoring Committee headed by Secretary (Power), has been 
put in place to review and monitor the implementation of the works sanctioned 
and expedite the completion of pending projects under the Scheme. 
 
Additionally, through PRAGATI (Pro -Active Governance and Timely 
implementation), an IT based multipurpose and multi-modal interactive platform, 
review of important schemes/programmes, and projects of the Government of 
India as well as the project s flagged by State Governments for timely 
implementation, is undertaken. Stakeholders like Secretaries of 
Ministries/Departments of Govt. of India, and Chief Secretaries/Administrators of 
States/UTs are onboarded onto the PRAGATI portal to provide inputs o n the 
implementation and progress of Projects, Programmes, Schemes, and Grievance 
Resolution, among other areas.

entries.head:
GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF HOUSING AND URBAN AFFAIRS 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 3126 
TO BE ANSWERED ON AUGUST 06, 2026 
 
 
URBAN HOUSING PROJECTS UNDER PMAY-U IN PUNJAB 
 
 
NO. 3126 DR. RAJ KUMAR CHABBEWAL:   
 
Will the Minister of HOUSING AND URBAN AFFAIRS be pleased to state: 
(a) whether the Government has reviewed the status of urban housing 
projects under Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana -  Urban (PMAY-U) and 
Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana - Urban 2.0 (PMAY-U 2.0) in Punjab and 
if so, the details thereof; 
(b) the details of the houses sanctioned, under construction and 
completed under PMAY -U and PMAY -U 2.0 during the last three 
years, city and district-wise; 
(c) whether any proposals from Punjab have been approved under 
PMAY-U 2.0 and if so, the details including the number of 
beneficiaries and the financial assistance sanctioned thereof; 
(d) the status of projects in Smart Cities of Punjab namely Amritsar, 
Jalandhar and Ludhiana after closure of the Smart Cities Mission 
(SCM) on 31 March 2025 indicating completed, ongoing and pending 
projects along with reasons for delay, if any; and 
(e) the steps taken by the Government to ensure continued financial and 
technical support for urban infrastructure, affordable housing and 
climate-resilient urban development in Punjab after SCM? 
 
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE  
MINISTRY OF HOUSING AND URBAN AFFAIRS 
(SHRI TOKHAN SAHU) 
 
(a) to ( c): Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs (MoHUA) has been 
implementing Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana -  Urban (PMAY -U) since  
25.06.2015 to provide all weather pucca houses with basic civic amenities 
to eligible urban beneficiaries across the country. Based on the learnings 
from the experiences of implementation of PMAY -U, MoHUA has revamped 
the scheme and launched PMAY -U 2.0 ‘Housing for All’ Mission with effect 
from 01.09.2024 for implementation in urban areas across the country to 
support 1 crore additional eligible beneficiaries. PMAY-U 2.0 is implemented 
through four verticals i.e., Beneficiary Led Construction (BLC), Affordable 
Housing in Partnership (AHP), Affordable Rental Housing (ARH) and Interest  
…2/- 

-2- 
Subsidy Scheme (ISS). The Scheme Guidelines may be accessed at 
https://pmay-urban.gov.in/uploads/guidelines/Operational-Guidelines-of-
PMAY-U-2.pdf.  
 
Based on the project proposal submitted by the State of Punjab,  a total of 
1.21 lakh houses under PMAY -U have been sanctioned by the Ministry, so 
far. Out of which, 1.14 lakh houses have been grounded, 1.03 lakh are 
completed/delivered to the beneficiaries as on 13.07.2026. Further, a total 
of 37,778 houses have been sanctioned by the Ministry in Punjab under 
PMAY-U 2.0 as on 13.07.2026.  Out o f which 16,897 houses  have been 
grounded and 2,700 have been completed/delivered to the beneficiaries as 
on 13.07.2026.   
 
Under PMAY-U 2.0, a total of ₹537.06 crores of Central Assistance has been 
approved for the State of Punjab, of which ₹254.66 crore have been released 
to the State, based on the compliances submitted by them.  The city and 
district-wise details of houses sanctioned, grounded and completed under 
PMAY-U and PMAY -U 2.0  in Punjab during the last three years  is at 
https://pmay-urban.gov.in/PHQ/LSUQ-3126.pdf. 
 
The Ministry regularly conducts review of the progress of these schemes 
with States/UTs including State of Punjab through video conferences, field 
visits and other monitoring mechanisms to ensure effective implementation 
of PMAY-U & PMAY-U 2.0 across the country including Punjab. 
 
(d) & (e): In the State of Punjab, 3 cities viz. Amritsar, Jalandhar and 
Ludhiana were selected under Smart Cities Mission (SCM). As reported by 
the State as on 31.3.2026, out of a total 204 projects amounting to ₹4,485 
crores, 190 projects amounting to ₹4,148 crores have been completed. With 
the closure of SCM on 31.03.2025, there is no budgetary provision under the 
Mission. The Government remains committed to supporting urban 
infrastructure, affordable housing and climate- resilient urban development 
in the State of Punjab through various ongoing flagship schemes and 
institutional initiatives.  
 
After the completion of the Smart Cities Mission (SCM), financial and 
technical support continues to be extended under schemes such as PMAY -
U 2.0, Atal Mission for Rejuvenation and Urban Transformation (AMRUT) 2.0, 
Swachh Bharat Mission–Urban (SBM -U) 2.0, and other urban development 
programmes, based on the prescribed scheme guidelines and proposals 
received from the State Government.

particularly in metropolitan and coastal cities; and 
(e)  the steps taken to promote recycling and reuse of treated 
wastewater, strengthen sewage infrastructure and support States 
including Tamil Nadu in achieving sustainable urban water 
management? 
 
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE 
MINISTRY OF HOUSING AND URBAN AFFAIRS 
(SHRI TOKHAN SAHU) 
(a) and (b):  Water and Sanitation is State subject. Government of India 
supplements the efforts of the States through schematic interventions/ 
advisories. It provides financial and technical support to the States 
through various schemes/ Missions such as Atal Mission for 
Rejuvenation and Urban Transformation 2.0 (AMRUT 2.0). Under AMRUT/ 
AMRUT 2.0, the States/ Union Territories are empowered to select, 
appraise, prioritise and implement the projects. 
Under AMRUT, a total of 888 sewerage and septage management 
projects amounting to ₹34,471.71 crore have been taken up by the  
…2/- 
 

-2- 
States/ UTs for augmentation of about 6,299 Million Litres per Day (MLD) 
of sewage treatment capacity. A total of 5,575 MLD sewage treatment 
capacity have been created, of which 1,437 MLD capacity has been 
developed for recycle/reuse.  Under AMRUT 2.0, the State Water Action 
Plans (SWAPs) comprising of 605 sewerage/septage projects worth 
₹71,133.01 crore have been approved, which includes development of 
7,098 MLD sewage treatment capacity (new/augmentation) of which 
1,900 MLD sewage treatment capacity is for recycle/reuse. The details 
of AMRUT/ AMRUT 2.0 projects State-wise and City-wise is available at 
the website https://amrut.mohua.gov.in/approvedProjects/state. 
As reported by the States/ UTs, a total of around 6000 MLD of treated 
used water is reused for non potable purposes.  
 
(c): Under AMRUT/ AMRUT 2.0, funds are released to the States/ UTs 
and not project -wise. States/UTs further release funds to the ULBs/ 
Implementing Agencies as per progress of the projects. Total Central 
share of ₹16,181.28 crore has been released/ Sanctioned under AMRUT 
and AMRUT 2.0 to the States/ UTs for the projects including waste 
water treatment and reuse projects in the last three financial years 
(2023-24 to 2025-26) of which an amount of ₹14,361.17 crore has been 
utilised/ expenditure incurred by the States/ UTs. State/UT-wise details 
including Tamil Nadu are given in Annexure.  
 
(d): As per the information provided by the States/ UTs to National Green 
Tribunal (NGT), the total sewage generation in the country is 52,644 
MLD and the existing STP capacity is 31,885.13 MLD.  
Through various Missions/ Schemes such as AMRUT 2.0, Swachh Bharat 
Mission-Urban (SBM-U 2.0) and Namami Gange, States/UTs are 
supported to fill the gaps in sewage treatment capacity. Under AMRUT 
2.0, 7,098 MLD of sewage treatment capacity has been approved in 500 
AMRUT Cities. Further, under SBM-U, more than 10,000 MLD sewerage/ 
septage treatment capacity has been approved for the towns having 
less than 1 lakh population and around 6,600 MLD of STP capacity has 
been sanctioned under Namami Gange Programme. 
 
(e): Under AMRUT and AMRUT 2.0, reuse and recycling of treated used 
water is promoted as a key component of sustainable urban water 
management and water security. States/Union Territories (UTs) have 
been encouraged to develop reuse infrastructure including tertiary 
treatment facilities, distribution networks and storage systems as part 
of sewerage and used water management projects. Reuse is an 
admissible project component under AMRUT 2.0 and States are

sewerage projects.

treatment plants for recyclable treated water meeting environmental 
standards on sustained basis. The focus of this initiative is building 
capacity and incentivizing qualitative improvements in the treated

PROPOSALS FOR APC FROM KOLHAPUR 
  
3129. SHRI SHAHU SHAHAJI CHHATRAPATI: 
             
Will the Minister of FOOD PROCESSING INDUSTRIES be pleased to state: 
    
(a) the details of the number of Agro-Processing Cluster (APC) proposals received from 
Kolhapur tehsils/areas remain stuck in appraisal under Pradhan Mantri Kisan Sampada 
Yojana (PMKSY) and the time since these have been pending; 
(b) the specific deficiencies or objections that have held up approval despite acute post-harvest 
losses in Kolhapur's sugarcane/jaggery economy; 
(c) the details of the project including investment proposed, processing capacity, jobs 
promised and appraisal committee's last observations; and 
(d) the details of immediate steps taken to address these inexplicable delays including fast-
track timelines and officers accountability for farmer distress caused by processing gaps? 
  
ANSWER 
 
THE MINISTER OF FOOD PROCESSING INDUSTRIES 
(SHRI CHIRAG PASWAN) 
  
(a) to (d): The Ministry of Food Processing Industries (MoFPI) has been implementing the 
Scheme for Creation of Infrastructure for Agro Processing Clusters (APC) since 2017 as a 
component Scheme of the Pradhan Mantri Kisan Sampada Yojana (PMKSY). The APC Scheme 
aims to create modern infrastructure for food processing based on a cluster approach, reduce post-
harvest losses, add value to agricultural produce, increase farmers' income and generate 
employment. The Scheme is demand driven and is not District/ State/ Product/ Sector specific. 
  
The proposals are invited from prospective investors / entrepreneurs through Expressions of 
Interest (EoIs) issued by the Ministry from time to time, subject to availability of funds. At present, 
no EoI is open under the APC Scheme. Further, no proposal from Kolhapur is pending or remains 
under appraisal in the Ministry against the last EoI dated 14.05.2025.

3130. विरु ियावनवि मारनः 
 
क्या नागर विमानन मंत्री यह बताने की क ृ पा करेंगे दकः 
(क) क्या क ें द्र सरकार को मई, 2026 के बाि परंिूर में प्रस्तावित ग्रीनफील्ड हिाईअड्डे को 
बनाए रिने, उसमें बिलाि करने या उसे िापस लेने के संबंि में तवमलनाडु राज्य सरकार से 
कोई पत्र/सूचना प्राप्त हुई है और यदि हां, तो तत्संबंिी ब्यौरा क्या है; 
(ि) क्या क ें द्र सरकार ने उक्त राज्य सरकार से उसकी िततमान नीवतगत वस्िवत के संबंि में 
कोई स्पष्टीकरण मांगा है और यदि हां, तो तत्संबंिी ब्यौरा क्या है; 
(ग) क्या पररयोजना को लेकर लंबे समय से बनी अवनवितता के कारण पविमी चेन्नई में 
विमानन योजना, अिसंरचना विकास, वनिेश और स्िानीय अितव्यिस्िा पर प्रवतक ू ल प्रभाि पडा 
है और यदि हां, तो तत्संबंिी ब्यौरा क्या है; 
(घ) क्या क ें द्र सरकार का कोई ऐसी समय-सीमा वनिातररत करने का विचार है वजसक े भीतर 
तवमलनाडु राज्य सरकार के वलए पररयोजना पर अपने अंवतम वनणतय की सूचना िेना आिश्यक 
हो और यदि हां, तो तत्संबंिी ब्यौरा क्या है; और 
(ङ) वनिावसयों, वनिेशकों और अिसंरचना वनयोजन को प्रभावित करने िाली लंबी नीवतगत 
अवनवितता के वबना चेन्नई की भविष्य की हिाईअड्डा क्षमता आिश्यकताओं को पूरा करना 
सुवनवित करने के वलए क्या किम उठाए जा रहे हैं?  
 
उत्तर 
 
नागर विमानन मंत्रालय में राज्य मंत्री (श्री मुरलीिर मोहोल) 
(क): जी नहीं।  
(ि) से (ङ): सरकार ने ग्रीनफील्ड हिाईअड्डा (जीएफए) नीवत, 2008 के तहत दिनांक 
07.04.2025 को तवमलनाडु सरकार के उद्यम, तवमलनाडु इंडवस्ियल डेिलपमेंट कॉपोरेशन 
वलवमटेड (टीआईडीसीओ), को परंिूर में एक अंतरराष्ट्रीय ग्रीनफील्ड हिाईअड्डे की स्िापना के 
वलए 'सैद्ांवतक' अनुमोिन प्रिान दकया है। 
जीएफए नीवत के अनुसार, हिाईअड्डा पररयोजनाओं के कायातन्ियन की वजम्मेिारी संबंवित राज्य 
सरकार (यदि राज्य सरकार पररयोजना प्रस्तािक है) सवहत संबंवित हिाईअड्डा विकासकतात की 
होती है। हिाईअड्डे के वनमातण की समय-सीमा भूवम अविग्रहण, अवनिायत मंजूररयों की उपलब्िता, 
वित्तीय समापन आदि जैसे कई कारकों पर वनभतर करती है।

ANSWERED ON 6TH AUGUST, 2026 
  
PARVATMALA PARIYOJANA AND ROPEWAY PROJECTS 
  
†3133. Shri Chintamani Maharaj: 
Dr. Manna Lal Rawat: 
Shri Arvind Dharmapuri: 
Smt. Mala Rajya Laxmi Shah: 
Shri Vishweshwar Hegde Kageri: 
Shri Dilip Saikia: 
Shri Nalin Soren: 
Smt. Anita Nagarsingh Chouhan: 
Shri Trivendra Singh Rawat: 
Shri Chandra Prakash Choudhary: 
Shri Godam Nagesh: 
  
Will the Minister of ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS 
सड़क परिवहन औि िाजमार्ग मंत्री  
be pleased to state: 
(a) the details of ropeway projects identified, approved, reviewed, under  
implementation and completed under Parvatmala Pariyojana, State/UT -
wise and district-wise; 
(b) whether more ropeway projects have been proposed in the country 
and if  so, the details of the project -wise current status, estimated cost 
and time-frame, including religious or hill tourism sites, State/UT-wise; 
(c) the progress achieved in development of ropeway projects under the  
Pariyojana, Particularly in hilly and difficult terrain and Tribal  areas, 
State-wise; 
(d) whether the Government proposes to include the hilly and  tourism 
potential areas of Chhattisgarh, Madhya Pradesh and Jharkhand under 
the said project or to develop them in future, if so, the details of ropeway  
projects proposed or approved and the current status thereof; 

(e) the criteria adopted for approval of ropeway projects under Public 
Private Partnership (PPP) or other models and improve  regional 
connectivity; 
(f) t he expected impact of the Pariyojana on tourism, last -mile 
connectivity, local economic development, employment generation and 
comprehensive regional development in the hilly regions under the said 
projects; and 
(g) the measures being taken by the Governme nt to promote all -round 
economic development and tourism in the tribal and remote areas? 
 
ANSWER 
  
THE MINISTER OF ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS 
(SHRI NITIN JAIRAM GADKARI)  
(a), (b) and (c) The details are enclosed as Annexure. 
(d), (e), (f) and (g) Governm ent announced National Ropeway 
Development Programme – Parvatmala Pariyojana in Union Budget 2022 -
23 for development of Ropeways to improve last -mile connectivity in hilly 
regions. The ropeway infrastructure is an ecologically sustainable 
alternative to conventional infrastructure in difficult hilly areas. The idea 
is to improve connectivity and convenience for commuters, besides 
promoting tourism. This is also suitable for congested urban areas, where 
a conventional mass transit system is not feasible. 
The projects are implemented primarily under the Hybrid Annuity 
Mode (HAM), Design -Build-Finance-Operate-Transfer (DBFOT) mode and 
Engineering, Procurement and Construction (EPC) mode. The 
Concessionaire is responsible for construction, operation and 
maintenance during the Concession Period. Under HAM, the entire 
revenue is collected by the Authority; under DBFOT, revenue is collected 
by the Concessionaire,  as per the terms of the Concession Agreement.  
Development of ropeway and development of National Hi ghway 
infrastructure, including in tribal areas, is a continuous process. The 
ropeway projects under Parvatmala Pariyojana are taken up on the basis 
of the techno -financial outcome of the Detailed Project Report (DPR), 
fulfilment of prescribed technical an d financial criteria, requirement of 
connectivity, traffic density, ecological impact and synergy with the PM 
Gati Shakti National Master Plan.
