Kerala during the last three years, district-wise; 
 
(b) the key findings and recommendations of the high -level expert 
committees regarding the structural issues along the said NH; 
 
(c) whether the Government has accepted any such recommendations and if 
so, the details thereof; 
 
(d) the details of monetary penalties, debarments or criminal actions 
initiated against the contractors, independent engineers and officials for 
construction lapses; and 
 
(e) the revised timeline for the completion of the NH -66 widening project in 
Kerala considering the ongoing safety audits? 
  
ANSWER 
  
THE MINISTER OF ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS 
(SHRI NITIN JAIRAM GADKARI)  
  
(a) The structural failures are in the nature of failures of slope protection 
works, Reinforced Soil (RS) Walls during construction phase. The details are 
given in the Annexure-A; 
  
(b) & (c) The key findings of the Expert Committee are to conduct fresh 
geotechnical investigations including taking Boreholes and determination of 

subsoil properties, pull out tests on RE Wall, reverification of ground 
conditions after ground improvement & global stability analysis. Based on 
findings of the Expert Committee in their report dated 04.08.2025, these 
recommendations have been complied with by engaging the Experts from IIT 
and boreholes have been taken; 
  
(d) The details are given in the Annexure-A; and; 
  
(e) Out of 13 ongoing projects on NH -66, 11 projects will be completed in the 
year 2027 and 02 projects in the year 2028. The details are given in the 
Annexure-B.

सड़क परिवहन औि िाजमार्ग मंत्री 
  
be pleased to state: 
  
(a) the measures taken by the Government to reduce road fatalities 
and injuries across the country; 
(b) the details of third -party experts and agencies involved in 
evaluation of the safety of sanctioned road projects, State-wise; 
(c) the details of road safety audits conducted at various stages of 
road projects, State-wise and district-wise details thereof in Andhra 
Pradesh; and 
(d) the details of road safety awareness campaigns conducted, 
State-wise and district-wise details thereof in Andhra Pradesh? 
  
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS 
(SHRI NITIN JAIRAM GADKARI) 
  
(a) Government has formulated a multi -pronged strategy to address 
the issue of road safety based on 4E's i.e. Education, Engineering 
(both of roads and vehicles), Enforcement and Emergency Care. 
Accordingly, various initiatives have been taken for road safety in

(b) and (c) Government has issued guidelines for conducting regular

Essay writing/Poster making competition/Nukkad Natak and 
Mass awareness events.

wayside amenities, food stall points during the Safety Week. 
 Awareness drives for Road Safety through Flex banners, 
Workshop, and Discussion. 
 Retro reflective sheeting to avoid rear –end collision and 
installation of reflectors/retro -reflective tapes on truck, 
tractor-trolley, animal cart, etc. at toll plazas. 
 Motivation and road side safety awareness programme for 
school/college students through Quiz competitions, drawing 
competitions, Essay writing and speech competitions, etc. 
 Special drives to stop overloading along with checking of over-
speeding, unauthorized parking, drunk driving, etc. with the 
help of police department. 
 Health cum Eye Check -up Camp and distribution of eye 
glasses for truck/bus drivers operating on NHs. 
 Distribution of pamphlets, and the display of safety banners. 
 Checking fatigue of truck drivers and educating them about 
road safety. 

 Road safety awareness messages on social media, such as 
Twitter, Instagram and Facebook are being spread on regular 
basis.

UDAN SCHEME FOR KOLAR DISTRICT  
3138.    SHRI M MALLESH BABU                      
Will the Minister of CIVIL AVIATION 
be pleased to state:- 
(a) the progress achieved by the Government with regard to development of the 
Kolar airstrip under the Regional Connectivity Scheme (RCS) - UDAN and its 
integration into the regional aviation network; 
(b) the actions initiated by the Gov ernment for facilitating commencement of 
commercial flight operations, strengthening aviation infrastructure and improving 
air connectivity in Kolar district of Karnataka; 
(c) the developments witnessed in relation to technical assessments, route 
planning, airline participation and infrastructure requirements associated with 
operation of flights from the said district; 
(d) the measures implemented by the Government for enhancing regional 
connectivity, promoting economic activity, facilitating tourism and im proving 
travel convenience through aviation infrastructure in the region; and 
(e) whether the Government plans for operationalisation of air services from Kolar 
and for maximising the benefits of the UDAN Scheme for the said district and if 
so, the details thereof? 
ANSWER 
Minister of State in the Ministry of CIVIL AVIATION      (Shri Murlidhar Mohol) 
(a) to (e): Kolar airstrip is included in the list of unserved airports under the UDAN 
Scheme. As per the provisions of the Scheme, revival/upgradation of unse rved and 
underserved airports is undertaken only upon identification of the airport through a 
valid bid and award of a route to a Selected Airline Operator (SAO). 
No bids for routes connecting Kolar airstrip were received from any airline during 
the five rounds of bidding conducted under the UDAN Scheme. Consequently, the 
airstrip was not taken up for revival/upgradation under the Scheme. 

Further, the Government has launched the next phase of the UDAN Scheme on 
04.07.2026 for a period of ten years, from FY 2026-27 to FY 2035-36, with a total 
outlay of Rs 28,840 crore, including budgetary support of Rs 12,159 crore from the 
Government of India for the development of 100 airports. 
The Scheme provides a Challenge Mode framework under which State 
Governments may  nominate airstrips for development. Proposals are evaluated 
based on availability of land, infrastructure readiness, technical and operational 
feasibility, traffic potential, statutory clearances and support of the State 
Governments.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA

Schemes for the Development of STs in Alipurduar, West Bengal 
3139: Shri Manoj Tigga 
Will the Minister of TRIBAL AFFAIRS be pleased to state: 
(a) the major initiatives undertaken by the Government for the socio-economic development of 
Scheduled Tribe communities in Alipurduar district of West Bengal; 
(b) the number of beneficiaries covered under education, livelihood, skill development and 
scholarship schemes; 
(c) whether any additional tribal development projects are proposed for the district; and 
(d) if so, the details thereof? 
ANSWER 
 MINISTER OF STATE FOR TRIBAL AFFAIRS  
(SHRI DURGADAS UIKEY) 
(a)  The Government is committed to the socio-economic development of Scheduled Tribes across 
the country, including Alipurduar district of West Bengal, through various schemes and programmes 
implemented by the Ministry of Tribal Affairs: 
i. Pre-Matric Scholarships to ST students: The scheme is applicable to students who are studying 
in Classes IX –X. Parental income from all sources should not be more than Rs.2.50 lakhs per annum. 
Scholarship of Rs.225/-per month for day scholars and Rs.525/-per month for hostellers is given for 
a period of 10 months in a year. Scholarship is disbursed through the State Government/UT 
Administration. Funding ratio is 75:25 between Centre and States for all States except North East and 
Hills States/UT like Himachal Pradesh, Uttarakhand and Jammu and Kashmir where it is 90:10.For 
UTs without legislature sharing pattern is 100% Central share. 
 
ii. Post Matric Scholarship to ST students: The objective of the scheme is to provide financial 
assistance to the Scheduled Tribe students studying at post-matriculation or post-secondary levels to 
enable them to complete their education. Parental income from all sources should not be more than 
Rs.2.50 lakhs per annum. Compulsory fees charged by educational institutions are reimbursed subject 
to the limit fixed by the concerned State Fee fixation committee and scholarship amount of Rs.230 to 
Rs.1200 per month, depending upon the course of study is paid. The Scheme is implemented by the 
State Governments and Union Territory Administrations. Funding ratio is 75:25 between Centre and 
States for all States except NE and Hilly States/UT of Himachal Pradesh, Uttarakhand and Jammu 
and Kashmir where it is 90:10. For UTs without legislature sharing pattern is 100% Central share. 
National Fellowship and Scholarship for Higher Education for ST students: This a Central Sector 
Schemes implemented by the Ministry of Tribal Affairs. The scheme has two sub-Schemes, viz:  
 
iii.  
a National Scholarship Scheme for Higher Education of ST Students (earlier known as Top 
Class Scholarship Scheme): Under this Scheme, Scholarship is provided for pursuing Graduate/Post 
Graduate courses in the selected top-class Government and Non-Government Institutes in 
professional fields such as Management, Medicine, Engineering, Information Technology, Law etc. 
All the ST students, with annual parental income is not exceeding Rs.6.0 lakhs and studying in the 

265 notified institutes by the Ministry, are eligible to receive scholarship. This scheme is started from 
year 2007 - 08.  
b. National Fellowship Scheme for Higher Education of ST Students: It is a Central Sector 
Scheme, fully 
funded by Ministry of Tribal Affairs to grant scholarship to meritorious ST students for pursuing 
Ph.D in India after completion of Master degree. This scheme is started from year 2005-06. The total 
number of fresh fellowships for Ph.D every year will be 750. ST students with a minimum of 55% 
marks in Master Degree up to the age of 36 years are eligible to apply for fellowship under the 
Scheme. The value of fellowship is at par with UGC rates. 
 
iv. National Overseas Scholarship for ST students: It is a Central Sector Scheme of Ministry of 
Tribal Affairs under which scholarships are given to the meritorious Schedule Tribe (ST) students for 
pursuing higher education in top 1000 ranked (as per latest QS world ranking) Institutes/Universities 
abroad. This scheme is started from year 1954-55. The Scheme is implemented through the Indian 
Embassies/Missions abroad, Ministry of External Affairs. Twenty awards are given every year. ST 
students with annual family income not exceeding Rs.6.0 lakhs are eligible to apply for the 
Scholarship under the Scheme.

line Ministries and aims to saturate infrastructural gaps in 63,843 villages, provide social 
infrastructure like hostels, Anganwadi facilities and mobile medical units and set up Van Dhan Vikas 
Kendras to provide livelihood

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF JAL SHAKTI

DELAYS IN LAYING DRINKING WATER SUPPLY PIPELINES 
  
†3140. SHRI LALJI VERMA: 
  
Will the Minister of JAL SHAKTI be pleased to state: 
 
(a) the details of the delays in laying drinking water supply pipelines in small habitations, hamlets and 
remote settlements of Bhiti, Katehari, Jalalpur, Alapur and Akbarpur Development Blocks of Ambedkar 
Nagar Lok Sabha Constituency due to geographical constraints, distance and technical reasons; 
(b) whether the Government has any independent monitoring mechanism to verify the actual supply of 
fifty-five litres per capita per day of safe drinking water at the ground level as against the figures reported 
in official records and if so, the details thereof; 
(c) whether any scientific techniques for rainwater harvesting and greywater management have been 
made mandatory for long-term rejuvenation of water sources and if so, the details thereof; and 
(d) the policy of the Government to strengthen the financial capacity of Gram Panchayats for sustainable 
maintenance of the drinking water infrastructure and to create  livelihood opportunities for local youth 
in this regard? 
 
  
ANSWER 
 
THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR JAL SHAKTI  
(SHRI V. SOMANNA) 
 
(a) Drinking Water is a ‘State’ subject, and hence, under JJM, the responsibility of planning, approval, 
implementation, operation  & maintenance of drinking water supply schemes lies with State/UT 
Governments. The Government of India supports the States by providing technical and financial 
assistance. The Union Cabinet has approved extension of the JJM up to December 2028, with an 
enhanced outlay and a restructured implementation framework focusing on structural reforms in the 
rural drinking water supply sector under JJM 2.0. 
State of Uttar Pradesh has informed that  the delays in project implementation and overall execution 
schedules in laying drinking water supply pipelines in small habitations, hamlets and remote settlements 
of Bhiti, Katehari, Jalalpur, Alapur and Akbarpur Development Blocks of Ambedkar Nagar Lok Sabha 
Constituency due to geographical constraints, distance and techn ical reasons are  the COVID -19 
pandemic, non -availability of free land for various structures, delay in obtaining No Objection 
Certificates (NOCs) from various departments such as Railways, Forest & Environment, NHAI, PWD 

Page 2 of 2 
 
and Irrigation & Water Resources, n on-availability of   skilled manpower, equipment, and 
machinery,  limited availability of critical construction materials, including MS pipes, HDPE pipes, 
solar panels, steel, and other essential components etc. 
(b)  Under JJM, to verify the actual supply of safe drinking water and for  ensuring universal coverage 
through tap water connection, the Department has evolved a comprehensive multi -level and multi -
format system of monitoring and evaluation of the implementation of programme, linking AADHAR of 
the head of household for targeted delivery and monitoring of specific outcomes, subject to statutory 
provisions, including geo -tagging of assets created, third -party inspections before making payments, 
measurement and monitoring of water supply in villages thr ough sensor-based IoT solution on pilot 
basis, etc. 
In a significant step towards strengthening service delivery and community ownership under the Jal 
Jeevan Mission,  Jal Seva Aankalan  initiative marks a decisive shift from infrastructure creation to 
sustained service delivery, placing Gram Panchayats and village institutions at the centre of assessing 
the regularity, adequacy, quality and sustainability of drinking water supply in Har Ghar Jal (HGJ) 
villages. 
(c) Under the Mission, States/UTs have been adv ised for source recharging, viz. dedicated bore well 
recharge structures, rainwater recharge, rejuvenation of existing water bodies, reuse of greywater, etc., 
in convergence with other schemes such as MGNREGS, Integrated Watershed Management Programme 
(IWMP), 16th Finance Commission tied grants to RLBs/ PRIs, State schemes, CSR funds, etc. Further, 
Jal Shakti Abhiyan: Catch the Rain (JSA: CTR) campaign aiming to encourage water conservation at 
grass-root levels with people's participation was launched in 20 19 in 256 water stressed districts of the 
country. Moreover, recognizing the importance of sustainable water management especially for drinking 
water availability, JSA -CTR was implemented with the theme “Source Sustainability for Drinking 
Water” in 2023.  
The Government has implemented extensive, community -led measures for water conservation and 
rainwater harvesting under the Jal Jeevan Mission (JJM), which integrates mandatory source 
sustainability components like groundwater recharge and greywater management. 
(d)  Under JJM, Gram Panchayat or its sub -committee/ user group i.e. Village Water

†3142.  Shri UJJWAL RAMAN SINGH: 
Will the Minister of JAL SHAKTI be pleased to state: 
(a) whether the Union Government conducts any surve y of the loss of life and 
property caused by floods in the Ganga, Yamuna and Tons rivers almost every 
year; 
(b) if so, the details of such surveys conducted du ring the last three years along 
with the measures taken/being taken to prevent the recurrence of such floods; 
(c) whether the Government proposes to build embank ments on both banks of 
the rivers in flood-affected areas; and 
(d) if so, the details thereof and if not, the reasons therefor? 
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR JAL SHAKTI  
(SHRI RAJ BHUSHAN CHOUDHARY) 
(a) to (d)  The data regarding the loss of lives an d property due to floods are not 
maintained centrally.  
Flood management and anti-erosion schemes are formu lated and 
implemented by the concerned State Governments as p er their respective 
priorities. The Union Government supplements these efforts by providing 
technical guidance and promotional financial assist ance for flood management 
in critical areas through a centrally sponsored "Fl ood Management and Border 

2 
 
Areas Programme" (FMBAP) for works related to flood  control, anti-erosion, 
drainage development among others. In Ganga Basin, comprising the states of 
Uttar Pradesh, Uttarakhand, Bihar, West Bengall, Jh arkhand and Chhatisgarh, a 
total central assistance of Rs 4131.80 Cr has been released since its inception.  
Government of Uttar Pradesh have informed that 523 embankments have 
been constructed having total length 3869 Km in the  State. Government of 
Uttarakhand have informed that flood protection wor ks have been completed 
over a length of 56.748 Km along the River Ganga in  the districts of Tehri 
Garhwal and Haridwar, and over a length of 34.90 Km  along the tributaries of 
River Ganga in Haridwar district. 
Central Water Commission (CWC) issues short-range f lood forecasts with 
a lead time of up to 24 hours at identified locatio ns. In Ganga Basin, comprising 
the States/Union Territories of Himachal Pradesh, U ttarakhand, NCT of Delhi, 
Rajasthan, Uttar Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh, Bihar, We st Bengal, and Jharkhand, 
there are 141 dedicated flood forecast stations (97  Level Forecast Stations and 
44 Inflow Forecast Stations). CWC also formulates 7 -day advance flood forecast 
advisories using rainfall-runoff mathematical model s that utilize satellite-based 
near-real-time rainfall estimates and numerical wea ther prediction forecasts 
shared seamlessly by the India Meteorological Depar tment for these flood 
forecasting stations. 
Ministry of Jal Shakti has continuously impressed u pon the States the 
need to adopt flood plain zoning. In this regard, M inistry of Jal Shakti issued the 
Technical Guidelines on Flood Plain Zoning (FPZ) in  August, 2025 and circulated 
the same to all States/UTs.

NO. 3143 SHRI M K RAGHAVAN: 
 
Will the Minister of HOUSING AND URBAN AFFAIRS be pleased to state: 
(a) whether the Government proposes to introduce a comprehensive 
National Urban Fire Safety and Building Code Compliance framework 
following recent tragic commercial fire incidents, making the use of 
advanced fire- retardant building materials mandatory in high- density 
public zones and if so, the details thereof; and  
(b) whether the Government intends to amend the Model Building Bye-Laws 
to mandate the integration of Internet of Things (IoT) -based wireless 
fire detection systems and Building Management Systems (BMS) in all 
high-occupancy commercial complexes and if so, the details thereof 
including the proposed timeline fixed for this roll out? 
 
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE  
MINISTRY OF HOUSING AND URBAN AFFAIRS 
(SHRI TOKHAN SAHU)   
 
(a): Fire prevention and fire safety fall within the domain of State 
Governments. As per Article 243W read with entry 7 of the Twelfth 
Schedule of the Constitution of India, ‘Fire Services’ is a function of 
Municipalities. Accordingly, enforcement of fire safety norms and 
compliance monitoring are undertaken by State Governments/Urban 
Local Bodies in accordance with the relevant Act/Statutes.  
 
The Government of India, through the Directorate General Fire 
Service, Civil Defence & Home Guards, Ministry of Home Affairs, plays 
an advisory role by issuing technical advisories, model guidelines and 
promoting best practices for strengthening fire prevention and fire 
safety across the country. 
 
The National Building Construction Standard-  2026 (NBCS) of India, 
published by the Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS), lays down 
comprehensive technical provisions relating to fire and life safety, 
including fire resistance of building elements, use of appropriate  
…2/- 

-2- 
construction materials, compartmentation, means of escape and 
installation of fire protection systems. The NBCS is a model standard 
and is adopted by States/Local Bodies through their respective 
building bye-laws and as per their requirement and policy decisions. 
 
(b): Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs has formulated ‘Model Building 
Bye-Laws (MBBL) 2016’, which is  advisory in nature. The MBBL aims 
to facilitate the adoption of modern building regulations by the States 
& UTs. States/UTs typically modify the model framework to align with 
local geographical, seismic, and demographic realities and notify 
them. The implementation of the provisions of building byelaws 
depends upon the state/local authorities as per their own Act/Bye-
laws/Regulations.

entries.head:
GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF POWER

UNSTARRED QUESTION NO.3145 
ANSWERED ON 06.08.2026 
 
LOAD ON LOW- CAPACITY POWER TRANSFORMERS 
 
†3145. SHRI AJAY KUMAR MANDAL: 
 
 Will the Minister of POWER 
be pleased to state: 
 
(a)  whether the load on low -capacity (low watt/low kVA) power transformers 
in rural areas of the country particularly in Bihar increases significantly due to a 
high number of consumers resulting in frequent failure/impairment of most 
transformers;  
 
(b)  if so, the details thereof, State -wise including Bihar and if not, the main 
technical reasons for the same; and  
 
(c)  the steps taken or being taken by the Government so far to find a permanent 
solution to this serious power issue in rural areas and to upgrade the capacity of 
power transformers? 
A N S W E R 
 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF POWER  
 
(SHRI SHRIPAD NAIK)  
 
(a) to (c): Electricity is a concurrent subject and power distribution is handled by 
distribution utilities that function under the guidance of their respective State 
Electricity Regulatory Commission and State Government. As per the Electricity 
Act, 2003, distribution of electricity is a licensed activity and it is the duty of the 
respective distribution licensee to develop and maintain an efficient and safe 
distribution system in its area of supply. Therefore, the responsibility for taking 
necessary measures for augmentation and maintenance of distribution system to 
avoid power outages and to improve the quality of power supply to the consumers 
rests with the respective distribution utilities in the country including utilities of 
Bihar (NBPDCL and SBPDCL). 
 
The loading of Distribution Transformer increases when the number of 
consumers connected to the same transformer increases or the load of existing 
consumers increases. This is monitored by the distribution utility while managing 
its network.  
 
………2. 
 

 
- 2 - 
 
Government of India (GoI) has supplemented the efforts of the States to 
help them provide quality supply of power, earlier through schemes like Deen 
Dayal Upadhyaya Gram Jyoti Yojana (DDUGJY) launched in 2014, Pradhan Mantri 
Sahaj Bijli Har Ghar Yojana (SAUBHAGYA) launched in October 2017, and 
currently under the Revamped Distribution Sector Scheme (RDSS) launched in 
July 2021. 
 
Under RDSS, financial assistance is being provided to distribution utilities 
for upgradation of distribution infrastructure works such as 
upgradation/augmentation of substations and distribution transformers, 
replacement of conductors, new HT/LT lines, fee der bifurcation, feeder 
segregation, aerial bunched cabling (ABC)/covered conductor, underground 
cableing and smart metering, based on proposals submitted by the Distribution 
Utilities.  
 
Under DDUGJY and SAUBHAGYA, works worth Rs.62,922.15 crores were 
executed at the national level including Rs . 8,676.9 crores in the State of Bihar. 
Under RDSS, loss reduction infrastructure and smart metering works worth       Rs. 
1.53 Lakh crores and Rs. 1.31 lakh crores have been sanctioned at the national 
level. This in cludes works worth Rs . 9,685.79 crores and Rs.2,021.22 crores 
sanctioned for loss reduction infrastructure and smart metering respectively, for 
the State of Bihar.

 Will the Minister of POWER 
be pleased to state: 
 
(a) whether the Government has reviewed t he adequacy and reliability of power 
supply for Mass Rapid Transit Systems (MRTS) and Metro Rail projects across the 
country and if so, the details thereof;  
 
(b) the details of the measures taken to ensure uninterrupted, quality and 
dedicated power supply  to operational and upcoming Metro Rail and MRTS 
projects along with the details of States and cities covered;  
 
(c) whether the Government has promoted the use of renewable energy, energy 
storage systems and energy-efficient technologies for Metro Rail operations and 
if so, the details and outcomes thereof; and  
 
(d) the steps taken by the Government to strengthen transmission and 
distribution infrastructure, improve power reliability and support the expansion 
of Metro Rail and other mass rapid transit systems as sustainable urban transport 
solutions? 
A N S W E R 
 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF POWER  
 
(SHRI SHRIPAD NAIK)  
 
(a) & (b):  Electricity being a concurrent subject, the supply and distribution of 
electricity to the various categories of c onsumers/areas in a State/UT is looked 
after by the respective State Government / Power Utility. Further, The Central 
Government supplements the efforts of the State Governments by establishing 
power plants through Central Public Sector Undertakings (CPSUs ) and through 
development of Inter State Transmission System. 
 
 At the national level, Electric Power Survey (EPS) of the country is 
conducted by Central Electricity Authority (CEA) every five years for estimating 
the electricity demand of the country, as obligated under Section 73(a) of the 
Electricity Act-2003. As per the mid -term review of 20th Electric Power Survey 
(EPS) report, the estimated energy requirement and peak demand of the country 
is 3,365 Billion Units (BUs) and 459 GW by 2035-36. 

Further, CEA has prepared National Generation Adequacy Plan (2026-27 to 
2035-36) covering the capacity addition required to meet the projected electricity 
demand for ten-year period from 2026-27 to 2035-36. 
 
States, in consultation with CEA, have prepared their “Resource Adequacy 
Plans (RAPs)” for generation and transmission, which are dynamic 10-year rolling 
plans with an objective to ensure generation and transmission capacity remains 
ahead of requirement of various end use sectors including Metro / Regional Rapid 
Transit System (RRTS). 
 
(c):  As informed by Ministry of Housing & Urban Affairs (MoHUA), Rooftop solar 
plant has been installed in various metro networks across the country. Metro Rail 
Systems are implemented with State-of-the-Art energy efficient technology such 
as LED (Light Emitting Diode) lighting, Variable Voltage Variable Frequency 
(VVVF) drives in lifts, escalators and air conditioning, Variable Refrigerant Flow 
(VRF) in Station Control Room and Equipment Rooms etc. including deployment 
of rolling stock with regenerative braking system. Such energy efficient systems 
along with roof top solar system reduce energy consumption besides harnessing 
green energy. These steps contribute significantly in making metro projects 
efficient, sustainable and enviro nment friendly. In addition, Government has 
encouraged usage of renewable energy through Open Access. 
 
(d): Government has taken following measures to strengthen the electricity grid 
through generation capacity addition & transmission infrastructure for en suring 
reliable power and support the expansion of Metro Rail & other mass rapid transit 
systems:

(i) As per National Electricity Plan (Generation), installed generation capacity 
in 2031-32 is likely to be 874 GW.  
 
(ii) All the States were advised to initiate process for creating/ contracting 
generation capacities; from all generation sources, as per their 
Resource Adequacy Plans. 
 
(iii)   In order to augment the power generation capacity, the Government of 
India has initiated following capacity addition programme:  
 
a.  Thermal Capacity Addition: The projected thermal (coal and lignite)

capacity. 
 
  Accordingly, Thermal capacities of around 21,080 MW have been 
commissioned since April 2023 till 30.06.2026. In addition, 47,545 MW of 
thermal capacity (including 4,845 MW of stressed thermal power projects) 
is currently under construction. The contracts of 16,000 MW have been 
awarded and are due for construction.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF POWER

IMPACT OF CLIMATE CHANGE ON HYDROPOWER GENERATION 
 
3147. PROF. SOUGATA RAY:  
SHRI KISHORI LAL: 
 
 Will the Minister of POWER 
be pleased to state: 
 
(a) whether the Government has assessed the impact of El Niño conditions and long-term 
climate change on hydropower generation in the country and if so, the details thereof;  
 
(b) the details of hydropower generation during the last five years, year -wise, along with 
the estimated loss in generation, if any, attributed to deficient rainfall, reduced river 
flows, glacial changes and extreme weather events;  
 
(c) whether any major hydropower projects have experienced redu ced reservoir storage, 
lower plant load factor or operational disruptions due to changing rainfall patterns, 
droughts, flash floods or sedimentation and if so, the details thereof, project -wise ;  
 
(d) whether the Government has formulated any long -term st rategy to safeguard 
hydropower generation against the adverse impacts of climate change and if so, the 
details thereof; and  
 
(e) the financial assistance, technological interventions provided during the last five 
years to States for adaptation, modernizat ion and sustainable operation of hydropower 
projects affected by climate variability? 
 
A N S W E R 
 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF POWER  
 
(SHRI SHRIPAD NAIK)  
 
(a) :  Ministry of Power (MoP) regularly reviews the status of power supply across th e 
country and has specifically reviewed the likely impact of El Niño in the quarter July, 
2026 to September, 2026. Historically, El Niño events have been associated with 
significant temporal and spatial variations in monsoon rainfall, which can materially 
influence electricity demand, hydroelectric generation, renewable energy availability 
and overall power system reliability. 
 
It has been assessed that electricity demand during monsoon season is expected 
to remain elevated owing to factors like sustained e conomic activity, agricultural 
irrigation requirements, and weather-related cooling loads. 
 
 

The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has projected monsoon rainfall in 2026 
at roughly 90% of the long-term average. The impact of El Niño on Hydro reservoir levels 
is expected to reasonably reduce hydropower generation in India as compared to the 
previous year.  During the period from 1 st April 2026 to 30 th July 2026, the hydropower 
generation has been 10.75% less than that for corresponding period of previous year 
(2025), as given at Annexure-I. 
  
(b) & (c): The details of Power Generation from Large Hydro Projects during the last 5 
financial years (FY 2021-22 to FY 2025-26) and current financial year i.e. FY 2026 -27 (till 
30 July, 2026) along with year -on-year growth is given at Annexure-II. Due to the flash 
floods in the Teesta Basin in October 2023, the hydropower stations such as Teesta -III, 
Teesta-V, Teesta Low Dam (TLD)-III, and TLD-IV suffered major operational disruptions. 
 
 A comparison of reservoir levels as on 30th July 2026 with the corresponding levels 
as on 30th July 2025 is given at Annexure-III. It indicates that reservoir levels are generally 
lower than those of the previous year, with the decline being particularly significant in 
the Southern Region. The details of comparison of energy content in reservoirs as on 30th 
July from 2023 to 2026 is given at Annexure-IV.  
 
(d) & (e): Government has taken following measures as long -term strategy to 
safeguard hydropower generation against the adverse impacts of climate change: 
 
(i) The Central Electricity Regulatory Commission (Terms and Conditions of Tariff) 
Regulations, 2024, notified on 15.03.2024, provide that where the saleable scheduled 
energy of a hydro generating station during a year is lower than th e saleable Design 
Energy due to reasons beyond the control of the generating station, the generator is 
permitted to recover the corresponding shortfall in Energy Charges from the 
beneficiaries in accordance with the provisions of the Regulations. Further, where the 
actual generation from a hydro generating station remains below the Design Energy for 
a continuous period of four years due to hydrological factors, the generating station is 
required to approach the Central Electricity Authority with the relevant hydrological data 
for revision of the Design Energy of the station. 
 
(ii) Early Warning System (EWS) consisting of systems for monitoring of various 
hazards like Glacial Lake Outburst Flood (GLOF), Landslide Lake Outburst Flood (LLOF), 
Flash Floods and Seismi c activity has been installed at 42 vulnerable Hydro Electric 
Projects for disaster preparedness and mitigating the effects of natural calamities. 
Further, a Central Control Room for integration of EWS at various project sites has been 
developed at NHPC, Faridabad.  
 
(iii) Central Electricity Authority has issued guide

PRICING OF E-20 PETROL 
 
3149. ADV. CHANDRA SHEKHAR: 
 
पेĚोͧलयम और Ĥाकृ Ǔतक गैस मंğी 
Will the Minister of PETROLEUM AND NATURAL GAS be pleased to state: 
(a) the average production cost per litre of twenty per cent Ethanol-Blended Petrol (E-20) vis-à-
vis unblended petrol, considering the notified procurement price of maize-based ethanol; 
(b) the reasons for pricing E-20 petrol at par with conventional petrol despite differences in 
production cost and fluctuations in international crude oil prices; and 
(c) the profit margins or financial outlays recorded by Public Sector Oil Marketing Companies 
from the sale of ethanol blended in the domestic fuel supply chain? 
ANSWER 
पेĚोͧलयम और Ĥाकृ Ǔतक गैस मंğालय मɅ राÏयमंğी 
(Įी सुरेश गोपी) 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF PETROLEUM & NATURAL GAS  
 (SHRI SURESH GOPI) 
(a) & (b): Public Sector Oil Marketing Companies (OMCs) procure ethanol from distilleries 
across the country under the EBP Programme. The procurement framework is designed to ensure 
adequate ethanol availability, provide remunerative prices to producers and support the agriculture 
sector. For the Ethanol Supply Year 2024-25, the average procurement cost of ethanol stands at Rs. 
71.55 per litre (inclusive of transportation and GST). 
The OMCs purchase ethanol under the EBP Programme at remunerative prices so that farmers are 
fairly compensated. For instance, Maize based ethanol prices have increased progressively and its 
current procurement price is Rs 71.86/litre (exclusive Transportation and GST).  
 
During the peak of West Asia crisis when Indian crude basket touched nearly $135 per barrel, the 
market price of petrol could have been around Rs.125 per litre, however Indian consumers continued 
to pay only Rs.94.77 per litre (ex Delhi) also because OMCs could procure ethanol at ~Rs.70/litre. 
By replacing a part of imported petrol with domestically produced ethanol, India has reduced its 
exposure to international crude oil price volatility and exchange-rate fluctuations.The average depot 
price of petrol during March–June 2026 was about Rs.85.8 per litre. Since the retail selling price 
remained below the market-determined level, Public Sector OMCs incurred an average under-
recovery of about Rs.11 per litre on petrol amounting to approximately Rs.21,300 crore during this 
period. 
The retail selling price of E20 petrol is market-determined, and Public Sector OMCs determine 
petrol prices after considering international crude oil prices, exchange rates, freight, taxes, ethanol 

procurement costs and other operational expenses. The Oil Companies have been directed to sell 
ethanol blended petrol with percentage of ethanol up to 20 per cent having minimum Research 
Octane Number (RON) of 95 across the country with effect from 01.04.2026. Ethanol's higher-
octane number supports modern high-compression engines and its higher heat of vaporisation 
improves combustion efficiency.  
(c): The financial performance of Public Sector OMCs is assessed on a consolidated basis across 
the petroleum value chain and not activity-wise. Any additional benefit or cost arising from ethanol 
procurement vis-à-vis petrol is not retained or borne by the OMCs independently. Consequently, no 
separate profit or loss is maintained or computed for the Ethanol Blended Petrol Programme or for 
each litre of ethanol-blended petrol sold. 
Accordingly, the success of the EBP Programme should not be measured in terms of profits earned 
by OMCs. Its true dividends lie in strengthening India's energy independence, reducing import 
dependence, enhancing farmer incomes, conserving foreign exchange, improving environmental 
sustainability and contributing to long-term fuel price stability.

MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF PETROLEUM AND NATURAL GAS

(a) and (b) Providing Piped Natural Gas (PNG) connections is part of the development of City Gas 
Distribution (CGD) Network, which inter alia include creation of pipeline infrastructure and other 
facilities for the supply of PNG to domestic, commercial and institutional consumers. This is being 
carried out by entities authorized by Petroleum and Natural Gas Regulatory Board (PNGRB). After 
completion of 12/12A CGD bidding round, in order to increase usage of Natural Gas, a cleaner fuel, 
PNGRB has authorized entities for the development of CGD network in 309 Geographical Areas 
(GAs), covering the entire mainland area of the country. As on 31.05.2026, the authorized entities 
have provided more than 1.70 crore PNG (D) connections, 52,143 PNG (commercial) connections, 
22,256 PNG (industrial) connections and established 8,936 CNG stations across the country. 
In the state of Tripura, PNGRB has authorized 5 Geographical Areas (GA) covering all districts in 
the state for development of CGD network. As on 31.05.2026, the authorised CGD entities have 
provided 71,344 PNG (D) connections, 567 commercial connections and 48 industrial connections in 
the state. 
Government has taken various steps to expand access to natural gas for the CNG (Transport) and 
PNG (Domestic) sectors across the country. These include priority allocation of domestic natural gas, 
diversion of gas from non-priority sectors, advance allocation on a two-quarter basis, and according 
priority to CNG (T)/PNG (D) in the allocation of gas from Deepwater, Ultra Deepwater and High 
Pressure-High Temperature discoveries, wherever proportionate distribution is required. Further, the 
Government has undertaken infrastructure measures including expansion of the CGD network and 

the National Gas Grid, development of Liquefied Natural Gas (LNG) terminals, grant of Public 
Utility Status to CGD projects, etc. 
Government is also promoting Compressed Biogas (CBG) as a clean alternative fuel through 
initiatives such as SATAT and GOBARdhan, including measures for assured offtake by Oil and Gas 
Marketing Companies, development of infrastructure for injection of CBG into the CGD network and 
National Gas Grid, support for biomass aggregation and phased mandatory sale of CBG in the CNG 
(T) and PNG (D) segments. 
PNGRB, in collaboration with CGD entities, launched the National PNG Drive 2.0 from 1st January 
2026 to 30th June 2026. PNGRB has informed that the initiative aims to ensure optimal utilization of 
existing infrastructure, promote new connections and activate non-billed customers, with an overall 
objective to increase the usage of natural gas across the diverse user categories. Under the initiative, 
various measures have been implemented by the Government and authorized CGD entities, 
including: 
i. Expansion of PNG connectivity to households, commercial establishments and industries; 
ii. Conversion of connected households into active billed consumers; 
iii. Awareness campaigns and consumer outreach programmes; 
iv. Coordination with State Governments and local authorities for expeditious statutory 
permissions; and 
v. Implementation of consumer-friendly measures, including digital registration, simplified 
connection processes and promotional schemes offered by CGD entities. 
Government have also notified a comprehensive control order dated 24.03.2026 under the Essential 
Commodities Act, 1955 to facilitate time-bound expansion of pipeline infrastructure across the 
country, especially CGD. The Order provides a uniform framework for grant of right of way (RoW) 
and permissions by mandating strict timelines, enabling deemed approvals in case of delays, and 
prohibiting imposition of unauthorized charges by public authorities. It also addresses access issues 
in residential and private areas by ensuring non-discriminatory and time-bound permissions, thereby 
removing key bottlenecks in pipeline laying. 
PNGRB has rationalised the Unified Tariff by reducing tariff zones from three to two and notified 
transportation tariffs of Rs. 54.00/MMBTU for Zone-1 (up to 300 km) and Rs. 110.02/MMBTU for 
Zone-2 (beyond 300 km), effe

 Will the Minister of PETROLEUM AND NATURAL GAS be pleased to state: 
 
(a) whether the Government has restored the annual number of subsidised Liquefied Petroleum 
Gas (LPG) cylinder refills available to beneficiaries under the Pradhan Mantri Ujjwala Yojana 
(PMUY) after the temporary changes made during the West Asia conflict, if so, the details 
thereof; 
(b) the present number of subsidised refills available annually to PMUY beneficiaries; 
(c) the total number of PMUY beneficiaries, active consumers and the annual refill rate during 
the last five years, year-wise; 
(d) whether the Government has conducted any assessment of the impact of subsidised LPG 
refills on household health, adoption of clean cooking fuel and reduction in the use of traditional 
fuels, if so, the details thereof; and 
(e) whether the Government proposes to increase the number of subsidised refills or extend

(Įी सुरेश गोपी) 
 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF PETROLEUM AND NATURAL GAS 
(SHRI SURESH GOPI) 
 
(a) to (e): Pradhan Mantri Ujjwala Yojana (PMUY) was launched in May, 2016 with an 
objective to provide deposit free LPG connection to adult women from poor households across 
the country. Year-wise details of PMUY connections (as of 31st March of every financial year) 
and Per Connection Consumption for the last five years are given below: 
FY Per Connection consumption (in terms of 14.2 Kg 
refills/consumer/Year)

Source: IOCL on behalf of PSU OMCs 

 
 
The Retail Selling Price of domestic LPG is being maintained at Rs. 942 per 14.2 Kg cylinder 
(Delhi) since June 2026, which carried an implicit subsidy (under-recovery) of more than Rs 700 
per 14.2 Kg cylinder in June 2026 and Rs 500 per cylinder during July 2026. Even for the month 
of August 2026, the RSP of 14.2 Kg cylinder carries an implicit subsidy of Rs. 188 per cylinder. 
For more than 10.5 crore PMUY consumers, the effective price is only Rs. 642 per cylinder 
(upto 4 refills per year), after a targeted subsidy of Rs. 300 per cylinder. 
 
Government have been ensuring availability of domestic LPG at affordable prices to households 
in the country for which Government have paid to the OMCs a compensation of Rs. 22,000 crore 
in FY 2022-23 and paying Rs. 30,000 crore during FY 2025-26 and FY 2026-27. Even after the 
payment of this compensation, accumulated under-recoveries of the PSU OMCs on domestic 
LPG were more than Rs 51,000 crores as of 30th June 2026 itself. 
 
Based on an assessment of FY 2025–26 refill consumption data, it has been observed that refill 
consumption patterns vary across PMUY beneficiary households, with a substantial proportion 
of beneficiaries availing up to four subsidised refills annually. Accordingly, Government has 
capped annual subsidized refill upto 4 refills of 14.2 Kg cylinder (and proportionately pro-rated 
for 5 Kg connections) to the PMUY consumers 
 
PMUY has had a significant positive impact on the lives of rural households, especially women 
and families in rural and remote areas including shift from traditional cooking methods that 
involve burning solid fuels like wood, dung and crop residues. The use of cleaner fuel lowers 
indoor air pollution, leading to improved respiratory health, particularly among women and 
children who are traditionally more exposed to household smoke. 
 
 
According to a recent PMUY Evaluation Report by NITI Aayog (April 2026), 86.59% of PMUY 
households use LPG as their predominant primary cooking fuel, reflecting widespread adoption 
of clean cooking energy. The evaluation also found that 74.27% of surveyed PMUY 
beneficiaries reported a reduction in indoor air pollution after adopting LPG. In addition, a 
significant proportion of beneficiaries reported reduction in cough and breathlessness, reduced 
eye irritation and smoke inhalation, along with a decline in headaches and dizziness, highlighting 
the positive health benefits associated with LPG usage. 
 
Separate evaluation studies by The Energy and Resource Institute (TERI) and IIT Kanpur have 
also highlighted the positive environmental and health impacts of PMUY. Their findings indicate 
that PMUY has contributed to reducing both ambient and household air pollution. The IIT 
Kanpur evaluation across six states further found that indoor air quality during cooking hours 
was nearly twice as good in LPG-using households compared to households relying on 
traditional chulhas, demonstrating significant health benefits, particularly for primary cooks.

entries.t: Complaints Regarding Engine Components due to Ethanol Blended Petrol
entries.head:
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION No. 3157 
TO BE ANSWERED ON 06th August, 2026 
COMPLAINTS REGARDING ENGINE COMPONENTS DUE TO ETHANOL BLENDED 
PETROL 
 
†3157.  SHRI BABU SINGH KUSHWAHA: 
  SHRI DEVESH SHAKYA: 
 
पेĚोͧलयम और Ĥाकृ Ǔतक गैस मंğी 
Will the Minister of PETROLEUM AND NATURAL GAS be pleased to state: 
 
(a) whether the Government has received any official complaints regarding damage to engine 
components such as rubber pipes, seals and pistons of BS-IV and BS-VI vehicle and decline 
in average mileage after the use of twenty per cent ethanol blended petrol in the country 
including Jaunpur and if so, the details thereof, year-wise;  
(b)  the details of the cases registered at authorised service centres of various automobile 
companies from January, 2024 to May, 2026 due to engine damage, reduced mileage and 
other issues arising from ethanol blended fuel; 
(c) whether vehicle manufacturers have submitted any report to the Government regarding the 
impact of ethanol blended fuel, including financial losses caused due to such issues and if so, 
the details thereof; 
(d) whether the Government is considering any new policy or mandatory standards for blending 
isobutanol or other biofuels with diesel including fifteen percent isobutanol blending and if 
so, the details thereof along with the technical and policy safeguards proposed for ensuring 
engine safety, warranty protection and technical compatibility, particularly for heavy 
commercial vehicles; and 
(e)  whether the Government proposes to undertake public awareness campaigns to provide 
information to consumers regarding vehicle compatibility and maintenance related to biofuel 
blending and if so, the details thereof? 
 
ANSWER 
पेĚोͧलयम और Ĥाकृ Ǔतक गैस मंğालय मɅ राÏय मंğी 
(Įी सुरेश गोपी) 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF PETROLEUM & NATURAL GAS  
 (SHRI SURESH GOPI) 
 
(a) to (c): The Ethanol Blended Petrol (EBP) Programme has been implemented through a 
phased, scientifically validated and consultative process involving NITI Aayog, automobile 
manufacturers, Oil Marketing Companies (OMCs), Automotive Research Association of India 
(ARAI), Society of Indian Automobile Manufacturers (SIAM), Indian Institute of Petroleum (IIP) 
and other technical institutions. 
 
Ethanol is not a new fuel. It has been used globally for over a century, with countries such as Brazil 
operating higher ethanol blends for decades with an average blending of 48% along with base fuel 
with 27% blending (E27). In India, the Ethanol Blended Petrol (EBP) Programme commenced with 
a pilot in 2001, E5 was introduced in 2006, and although blending remained around 1.53% in 2013-
14, it has since been increased progressively in a calibrated manner after creating the necessary 
production capacity, infrastructure and regulatory framework. 
 
The rollout of higher ethanol blends was undertaken only after extensive consultation with 
automobile manufacturers, SIAM, ARAI, component manufacturers, testing agencies and Oil 
Marketing Companies (OMCs). The Government has not received any widespread or substantiated 

complaints from vehicle manufacturers, automobile associations or consumer organisations 
regarding the use of E20 petrol with respect to fuel efficiency, engine performance, maintenance 
costs and the overall driving experience. The Government has, however, taken note of certain 
concerns raised in media and social media, which have been scientifically examined. 
 
Extensive laboratory studies and field trials conducted by ARAI, SIAM, IOCL, IIP and automobile 
manufacturers covering parameters such as engine durability, drivability, startability, corrosion 
resistance, material compatibility, emissions and fuel efficiency have confirmed that E20 is safe for 
use under prescribed standards. 
These studies also established that legacy vehicles do not exhibit any significant variation in 
performance or abnormal wear and tear due to E20. These extensive laboratory studies, field 
validation and real-world operating experience have not established any widespread adverse impact 
on vehicle performance due to E20 fuel. 
 
The Government's assessment is based not only on laboratory research but also on large-scale 
experience after nationwide implementation. India witnesses approximately 8 crore vehicles visiting 
retail outlets every day (around 80% petrol vehicles). 
 
This is evident from the fact that E15+ blended petrol has been in widespread use for over three-and-
a-half years and E19-E20 fuel for over two-and-a-half years. More than 20 crore two-wheelers and 
over 3 crore petrol cars have been operating on these blends without any verified evidence of 
widespread engine failure or vehicle breakdown attributable to ethanol blending. Manufacturer 
service data confirm that there is no abnormal corrosion, wear or reduction in vehicle life due to E20 
fuel. Manufacturers continue to honour warranty obligations for vehicles using E20 fuel, providing 
further confidence

entries.t: NITI Aayog Report on empowering City Governments
entries.head:
GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF HOUSING AND URBAN AFFAIRS 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 3158  
TO BE ANSWERED ON AUGUST 06, 2026 
 
NITI AAYOG REPORT ON EMPOWERING CITY GOVERNMENT S 
 
NO. 3158 DR. SHASHI THAROOR: 
 
  Will the Minister of HOUSING AND URBAN AFFAIRS be pleased to state: 
 
(a) whether the Government has taken note of NITI Aayog’s recent 
report titled "Moving Towards Effective City Government –A 
Framework for Million- plus Cities" which recommends structural 
shifts towards empowered city governments, including a directly 
elected Mayor as the political and executive head of the city with 
a fixed tenure and if so, the details thereof;  
(b) whether the Government proposes to update the Model Municipal 
Law circulated to States in 2003 to reflect the recommendations 
of the NITI Aayog’s report, if so, the details thereof and if not, the 
reasons therefor; and 
(c) the steps being taken by the Union Government to incentivise the 
State Government s to amend their respective Municipal 
Corporation Acts to institutionalise a fixed tenure and executive 
powers for city Mayors?  
 
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE  
MINISTRY OF HOUSING AND URBAN AFFAIRS 
(SHRI TOKHAN SAHU) 
  
(a):   The report inter  alia recommends that the Mayor should be the 
head of the city government with overall executive authority. For 
effective urban governance, executive authority within a Municipal 
Corporation must be clearly vested in the Mayor, with the Municipal 
Commissioner functioning under the Mayor’s oversight and the 
designated reporting authority.  State governments should amend the 
State Municipal Acts or other relevant legislation to clearly designate 
the Mayor as the head of the city government and clearly define the roles 
and responsibilities of the Mayor and the Municipal Commissioner. 
…2/- 

-2- 
However, as per entry 5 of list II -State list of Seventh Schedule of the 
Constitution of India, ‘ Local Government’ is a state subject and urban 
planning is a function of Urban Local Bodies (ULBs) as envisaged in the 
Twelfth Schedule of the Constitution of India. Accordingly , 
strengthening of institutional and fiscal capacity of ULBs is primarily the 
responsibility of the respective State Governments. The Government of 
India supplements the efforts of the States through various schemes, 
policy initiatives and advisories.  
Article 243 R of the Constitution of India provides for the composition of 
the Municipalities . Clause 2 of Article 243 R states that the State 
Legislature may, by law, provide the manner of election of a Chairperson 
of a Municipality.  Accordingly, State governments may amend their 
Municipal laws in order to provide for the direct election of Mayors along 
with fixed tenure. 
(b): Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs (MoHUA) had framed the 
Model Municipal Laws (MML) in the year 2003 which aims to consolidate 
and serves as guidance to state government to amend the laws relating 
to the municipal governments in the S tates/UTs in conformity with the 
provisions of the Constitution of India as amended by the Constitution 
(Seventy-fourth Amendment) Act, 1992, based on the principles of 
participation in, and decentralization, autonomy and accountability of, 
urban self government at various levels, to introduce reforms in financial 
management and accounting systems, internal resource generation 
capacity and organizational design of Municipalities, to ensure 
professionalization of the municipal personnel, and to provide for 
matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.  
(c): As regards Part IXA of the Constitution, the matters relating to the 
composition, powers, functions and tenure of Municipalities, including 
the office, election and powers of the Mayor, fall within the legislative 
domain of the State Governments.

Expansion of LPG Distribution Infrastructure 
 
3159. Shri Baijayant Panda: 
 
पेĚोͧलयम एवं ĤाकृǓतक गैस मंğी 
 
 Will the Minister of PETROLEUM AND NATURAL GAS be pleased to state: 
 
(a) the details of the expansion of Liquefied Petroleum Gas (LPG) distribution infrastructure, 
including bottling plants and distributorships across the country, during the last three years; 
(b) the extent to which the said expansion has improved access to LPG in rural and aspirational 
districts; and 
(c) the steps taken by the Government to ensure reliable LPG supply and consumer convenience? 
 
ANSWER 
पेĚोͧलयम एवं ĤाकृǓतक गैस मंğालय मɅ राÏयमंğी 
(Įी सुरेश गोपी) 
 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF PETROLEUM AND NATURAL GAS 
(SHRI SURESH GOPI) 
 
(a) & (b):   Appointment of LPG distributorships by the Public Sector Oil Marketing Companies 
(OMCs) is a continuous process and locations for setting up of LPG distributorships are 
identified and advertised under Unified Selection Guidelines 2016 for LPG Distributorships. 
As on 01.07.2026, there are a total of 25,611 LPG distributorships operating across the country, 
out of which 17,685 distributorships are serving rural areas. In order to improve access of LPG 
in rural and remote areas, OMCs have commissioned 8,045 distributorships during 01.04.2016 to 
30.06.2026 across the country, out of which 7,452 (i.e. 93 %) are catering to rural areas. Since 
01.04.2023, 298 LPG distributorships have been commissioned by PSU OMCs, out of which 262 
distributorships (88%) cater to the customers in rural areas.   
To further improve last-mile delivery in remote and underserved habitations, OMCs have taken 
several measures, including commissioning of rural and remote-area distributorships, 
appointment of Common Service Center - Village Level Entrepreneur (CSC VLEs), use of 
technology for order booking and tracking. 
There is adequate LPG bottling capacity available in the country. As on 01.07.2026, there are 
214 LPG bottling plants of OMCs serving across the country having bottling capacity of 23.1 
Million Metric Tonnes per annum.  Most bottling plants of PSU OMCs currently operate in 
single or double shifts only. Actual LPG bottling can be further enhanced significantly by 
increasing the number of shifts per day as per need.  
 
Since 01.04.2023, PSU OMCs have commissioned 10 LPG bottling Plants with combined rated 
capacity of 750 Thousand Metric Tonnes Per Annum (TMTPA) and have augmented 18 TMTPA 
at existing LPG Plants. Hence, the total bottling capacity added by PSU OMCs during last three 
years is 768 TMTPA. 
 

Pradhan Mantri Ujjwala Yojana (PMUY) was started in May, 2016 with an objective to provide 
deposit free LPG connection to adult women from poor households across the country including 
aspirational districts. As of 01.07.2026, there are 33.13 crore domestic LPG consumers including 
10.58 crore PMUY connections in the country. Implementation of PMUY coupled with 
expansion of LPG distributorships and bottling infrastructure has contributed to improvement in 
LPG coverage in the country from 62% in April 2016 to near saturation now. 
 
(c): For the convenience of consumers, Oil Marketing Companies (OMCs) have implemented 
multiple digital initiatives across the country, including IVRS/SMS-based refill booking with 
SMS alerts at the booking, cash memo generation and delivery stages, Delivery Authentication 
Code (DAC)-based verified delivery, and digital booking through mobile apps, IVRS, SMS, 
missed call and WhatsApp. Consumers can also avail self-Biometric Aadhaar Authentication 
through OMC mobile applications, obtain new LPG connections through missed call, choose 
from various cylinder package options, and benefit from digitalization of customer documents.  
 
To further enhance customer service, OMCs have introduced dedicated short-code consumer 
helplines, namely 14428 for the general helpline and 14438 for PMUY (Ujjwala) beneficiaries. 
In addition, LPG consumers can lodge their grievances or complaints through multiple channels, 
including the dedicated toll-free helpline (1800 2333 555) for queries, including subsidy-related 
issues, OMCs' official websites and mobile applications, the Centralised Public Grievance 
Redress and Monitoring System (CPGRAMS), chatbots, WhatsApp, social media platforms 
(Twitter/X, Facebook, and Instagram), including MoPNGeSEVA, the dedicated emergency 
helpline 1906 for LPG accidents and leakages, or by lodging complaints directly at their LPG 
distributor's office. 
Diversification of LPG imports is being pursued to ensure supply security and mitigate risks 
arising from regional disruptions or geopolitical events. As part of this strategy, PSU OMCs 
have recently concluded contracts for the import of approximately 2.2 Million Metric Ton 
(MMT) of US-origin LPG for the calendar year 2026, covering nearly 10% of the country’s total

entries.t: Inclusion of Aviation Turbine Fuel under GST
entries.head:
GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF CIVIL AVIATION 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. : 3160 
 ( TO BE ANSWERED ON THE  6th August 2026 )  
INCLUSION OF AVIATION TURBINE FUEL UNDER GST 
3160.    SHRI DUSHYANT SINGH                      
 
Will the Minister of CIVIL AVIATION 
be pleased to state:- 
(a) whether the Government has examined the potential benefits of bringing 
Aviation Turbine Fuel (ATF) under the ambit of the Goods and Services Tax 
(GST) to promote uniform taxation and operational efficiency in the aviation  
sector and if so, the details thereof; 
(b) whether any consultations or indicative assessments have been undertaken 
regarding possible GST rate structures or other arrangements that may help 
maintain revenue stability for States in the event of inclusion of ATF under 
GST and if so, the details thereof; 
(c) whether the Government has assessed the possible impact of such a measure 
on airline operating costs, airfares and expansion of air connectivity, 
particularly in Tier-II and Tier-III cities and if so, the details thereof; and 
(d) the steps taken by the Government to facilitate consultations with States, 
airlines and other stakeholders on this matter? 
ANSWER 
Minister of State in the Ministry of CIVIL AVIATION       
(Shri Murlidhar Mohol) 
(a) to (d) The oper ating costs of airlines are dynamic and their individual 
components vary due to multiple factors which inter alia include, price of 
Aviation Turbine Fuel (ATF) in international markets, foreign exchange rates, 
excise duties and Value Added Tax (VAT), lease  rentals etc. Although ATF 
prices constitute a major aspect of airline operating expenses, airfares are also 
determined by various other factors like real time demand, competitive forces, 
seasonality and operational considerations. An agenda item on bringi ng 
Aviation Turbine Fuel under Goods and Services Tax (GST) was tabled in the 
55th GST Council Meeting held on 21st December, 2024. Several states 
expressed their views against the proposal. Therefore, the status quo i.e. keeping 
ATF out of GST regime has been maintained. 
 

The Government has taken several measures to support the aviation sector and 
help keep air travel affordable, which include, one time budgetary support not 
exceeding Rs. 10,000 crores for Oil Marketing Companies (OMCs) to provide 
ATF pric e stablisation support to the Scheduled Indian Airlines due to 
exceptional fuel price volatility arising from the West Asia crisis. For domestic 
operations, ATF prices were capped at a maximum increase of 25% over the 1st 
March, 2026 base price, effective from 1st April 2026 for the months of April 
and May, 2026. Additionally, the issue of high VAT on ATF has been taken up 
with the States/UTs by the Ministry of Civil Aviation. As a result, 23 
States/UTs have reduced VAT on ATF since September 2021. More rec ently, 
the State of Maharashtra & Delhi have reduced the VAT on ATF from 18% to 
7% & 25% to 7% respectively for a period of 6 months.

Details of houses sanctioned for  Scheduled Castes (SCs), Scheduled

entries.t: Civil Aviation Services at Solapur Airport
entries.head:
GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF CIVIL AVIATION 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. : 3164 
 ( TO BE ANSWERED ON THE  6th August 2026 )  
CIVIL AVIATION SERVICES AT SOLAPUR AIRPORT  
3164.     MS. PRANITI SUSHILKUMAR SHINDE      
Will the Minister of CIVIL AVIATION 
be pleased to state:- 
(a) whether the Government has taken steps to operationalise and enhance civil 
aviation services at Solapur Airport and if so, the details thereof including the 
current status of necessary clearances and infrastructure readiness; 
(b) whether there are any proposals to introduce regular commercial flight 
operations from Solapur to major domestic destinations such as Mumbai, Delhi, 
Bengaluru and Hyderabad; 
(c) the details of the routes identified or proposed under the Regional C onnectivity 
Scheme (RCS) - UDAN for Solapur along with the timelines fixed for 
commencement of services; and 
(d) the steps being taken to address operational constraints including regulatory 
approvals, infrastructure gaps and airline participation to ensur e sustained and 
viable air connectivity for Solapur? 
ANSWER 
Minister of State in the Ministry of CIVIL AVIATION      (Shri Murlidhar Mohol) 
(a) to (d):  M/s Star Air is persently operating four weekly scheduled flight services 
on the Mumbai-Solapur-Mumbai sector. 
 
The next phase of the UDAN Scheme was launched on 04.07.2026 to further 
strengthen regional air connectivity by expanding access to underserved and 
unserved airports across the country. 
 
Further, the scheme incorporates a longer VGF mechanism exte nding up to five 
years, progressively tapered to enable airlines to transition towards commercially 
sustainable operations. The overarching objective of UDAN is to ensure that air 

connectivity becomes self -sustaining over time and does not remain perpetual ly 
dependent on financial support. 
 
Under the Scheme, Solapur Airport is eligible for bidding in the "Underserved 
Airport" category. Further, the Government of Maharashtra may identify and

process, as per the Scheme provisions.

ground water recharge. The initiative is guided by the 3Cs principle—

(b) the reasons for delay in the project and the details of areas/sectors in which 
such delay is occurring; and  
 
(c) whether the Government/NTPC proposes to give priority or preference to the 
former employees of the erstwhile Talcher Thermal Power Station, their family 
members and local residents in employment/recruitment for the new project in 
the new NTPC plant, if so, the details thereof? 
 
A N S W E R 
 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF POWER  
 
(SHRI SHRIPAD NAIK)  
 
(a): The Talcher Thermal Power Project (Stage -III, 2x660 MW) is being 
implemented in Angul district of Odisha State. The present physical progress of 
the project is 51.4%. 
 
 The project works are being expedited with the cooperation and close 
coordination of all stakeholders, including the District Administration, State 
authorities, and other PSUs/Government organizations. The project is targeted for 
completion in the first quarter of FY 2028-29. 
 
(b): The delay in the Talcher Thermal Power Project is due to delay in the 
closure of the road passing through the project site, handing over of physical 
possession / Right of Use (RoU)/Right of Way (RoW) of the la nd by the State 
Government, removal of encroachments in the railway siding area, and the lack 
of availability of critical project materials at the project site. 
 
(c):  Talcher Thermal Power Station (TTPS) was taken over by NTPC with effect 
from 03.06.1995 from the erstwhile Odisha State Electricity Board (OSEB). The 
erstwhile employees of OSEB were absorbed into the services of NTPC. 
 
 Due preference is being given by the contracting agencies to local workers 
for deployment in various jobs, subject to their skills, experience and the project 
requirements.

MINISTRY OF FOOD PROCESSING INDUSTRIES 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 3174

Integrated Cold Chain and Value Addition Infrastructure Projects 
  
3174. Shri Naveen Jindal:  
  
 Will the Minister of FOOD PROCESSING INDUSTRIES be pleased to state: 
  
   (a)  the details of the number of Integrated Cold Chain and Value Addition Infrastructure 
projects sanctioned, completed and under implementation, State/UT-wise; 
(b) the current estimated level of post-harvest losses in horticulture and non-horticulture 
produce; 
(c)  the funds released and utilised under the Cold Chain scheme during the last two years; 
and 
(d)  the steps being taken to expand cold storage capacity in the Eastern and North-Eastern 
States?  
  ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF FOOD PROCESSING INDUSTRIES 
(SHRI CHIRAG PASWAN) 
  
(a) The Ministry of Food Processing Industries (MoFPI) has been implementing a component 
scheme - Integrated Cold Chain and Value Addition Infrastructure (Cold Chain scheme) under 
the Central Sector umbrella scheme - Pradhan Mantri Kisan Sampada Yojana (PMKSY). As 
of 30.06.2026, 409 cold chain projects have been approved, of which 311 projects have already 
been completed and operationalised and 98 projects are ongoing. A comprehensive State/ UT-
wise details of the same is provided at the Annexure.

schemes, Expressions of Interest (EoIs) are invited from eligible entities from time to time, 
subject to the availability of funds, in accordance with the applicable scheme guidelines. Under 
these component schemes, financial assistance is provided as grants-in-aid or subsidy for

general areas, and 50% for difficult areas (including North-Eastern Region States) as well as

entries.head:
GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS 
  
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 3176 
ANSWERED ON 6TH AUGUST, 2026 
  
DPR FOR SERVICE ROAD ON NH-66 
  
3176.  SHRI KOTA SRINIVASA POOJARY:   
  
Will the Minister of ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS 
सड़क परिवहन औि िाजमार्ग मंत्री  
be pleased to state:  
  
(a) whether the Government is aware that the agency for preparation of 
Detailed Project Report for service road from Kundapura to Hejamadi  on 
National Highway (NH)-66 in Udupi District has been appointed but the DPR is 
yet to be prepared and work has not commenced, if so, the details thereof; 
  
(b) whether the Government is aware that absence of service roads on this 
heavily trafficked stret ch passing through densely populated areas is 
causing hardship to residents and serious road safety concerns, if so, the 
details thereof; 
  
(c) whether the Government proposes to issue directions for early 
preparation and approval of the DPR and expeditiou s commencement of 
service road works from Kundapura to Hejamadi, if so, the details thereof; 
and 
  
(d) whether the Government proposes to complete on priority the pending 
service road work near Doni Mane Hotel, Santhekatte which remains 
incomplete and poses safety hazards to motorists and pedestrians, if so, the 
details thereof? 
  
ANSWER 
  
THE MINISTER OF ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS 
(SHRI NITIN JAIRAM GADKARI) 
  
(a) to (c) National Highways Authority of India (NHAI) has appointed 
Consultancy agency for preparation of the Detailed Project Report (DPR) for 

road safety improvement measures on National Highway (NH) -66 from 
Hejamadi to the Kerala Border, which also inc ludes the proposed service 
road from Kundapura to Hejamadi. The DPR agency commenced its services 
from 14.05.2026. 
         The scope of the DPR includes assessment and provision of service 
roads, flyovers, underpasses and other road safety measures based on traffic 
density, roadside development, road safety requirements, technical 
feasibility and availability of land. 
(d)     A 6.0m wide service road from Km 314.0 to Km 315.0 (Both Hand Sides) 
on NH-66 at Santhekatte was constructed in 2017 by the BOT (Bui ld-Operate-
Transfer) Concessionaire. 
Further, during the construction of the Santhekatte Vehicular Overpass 
(VOP) at Km 314.092, the median divider was temporarily removed to 
facilitate traffic diversion. Vehicular Overpass at Santhekatte is completed 
and opened for traffic. However, reinstatement of the kerb separator 
between the main carriageway and the service road has been stalled due to 
objections from the local public, who have demanded additional widening of 
the service road. The District Administrat ion has been requested to provide 
necessary support.

entries.t: Development of Airports in Uttar Pradesh
entries.head:
GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF CIVIL AVIATION 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. : 3177 
 ( TO BE ANSWERED ON THE  6th August 2026 )  
DEVELOPMENT OF AIRPORTS IN UTTAR PRADESH 
3177.    SHRI RAJEEV RAI                          
Will the Minister of CIVIL AVIATION 
be pleased to state:- 
(a) the details and the number of airports including greenfield airports established in Uttar 
Pradesh since 2014, airport-wise; 
(b) the details of expenditure incurred by the Government on each such airport, project-wise; 
(c) the number of such airports presently handling scheduled commercial passenger flights, 
airport-wise; 
(d) whether the Government is aware that several newly inaugurated airports including 
Azamgarh Airport are presently not handling regular commercial fligh ts and if so, the details 
thereof along with the reasons therefor; and 
(e) the steps taken by the Government to restore commercial operations at such airports and 
the time by which each such airport is expected to become fully operational? 
ANSWER 
Minister of State in the Ministry of CIVIL AVIATION      (Shri Murlidhar 
Mohol) 
(a) & (b): Since 2014, two Greenfield Airports i.e. Noida (Jewar) at a cost of approximately 
Rs. 11764 crore and Kushinagar at a cost of Rs. 448 crore have been established in Uttar 
Pradesh. Additionally, under the UDAN scheme, eleven airports namely Agra ( Rs. 8 crore), 
Prayagraj (Rs. 161 crore), Bareilly (Rs. 104 crore), Kanpur (Rs. 135 crore) Aligarh (Rs. 32 
crore), Chitrakoot (Rs. 33 crore), Moradabad (Rs. 30 crore), Azamgarh (Rs. 30  crore), 
Shravasti (Rs. 33 crore), Hindon (Rs. 47 crore) and Ayodhaya (Rs. 347 crore)  have been 
operationalized in Uttar Pradesh.  
 
Noida (Jewar) Airport has been developed by the Government of Uttar Pradesh under Public 
Private Partnership mode.  
 
(c) to (e): With the repeal of the Air Corporations Act in March 1994, the Indian domestic 
aviation was deregulated. It is upto the airline operators to introduce air services to / from any 
airport in the country depending on their operational & commercial viability. 
 
At present, scheduled commercial flight operations at 6 airports in Uttar Pradesh are 
temporarily suspended due to airline -related reasons. These airports are Kushinagar, Aligarh, 
Azamgarh, Chitrakoot, Shravasti & Moradabad. 
 

Under the next phas e of UDAN Scheme launched on 04.07.2026, the above airports are 
eligible for bidding in the "Unserved Airports" category. If any airline submits a valid bid for 
operation of RCS flights on routes connecting these airports, it will be considered as per the 
Scheme provisions. 
******

Will the Minister of PETROLEUM AND NATURAL GAS be pleased to state: 
 
a) whether Indian Oil Corporation Limited (IOCL), Bharat Petroleum Corporation

and other Public Sector Undertakings (PSUs) under the Ministry are ensuring payment to 
Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSME) contractors, vendors and service providers

b) the total value of procurement from MSMEs, the payments released, the outstanding 
dues and the number of cases pending beyond the prescribed period during the last ten years, 
PSU-wise and year-wise; 
c) the details of penal interest payable or paid for delayed payments to MSMEs during 
the last ten years, along with the reasons for such delays, PSU-wise; 
d) whether MSME vendors and contractors participating in procurement, works and 
service contracts floated by IOCL, BPCL, HPCL, GAIL and other PSUs under the Ministry 
are exempted from payment of Earnest Money Deposit (EMD)/Bid Security and Performance 
Security, if not, the reasons therefor; and

पेĚोͧलयम और ĤाकृǓतक गैस मंğालय मɅ राÏयमंğी 
(Įी सुरेश गोपी) 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN MINISTRY OF PETROLEUM & NATURAL GAS 
(SHRI SURESH GOPI) 
(a) to (c): The Public Sector Undertakings (PSUs) under the Ministry of Petroleum and 
Natural Gas, including Indian Oil Corporation Limited (IOCL), Bharat Petroleum 
Corporation Limited (BPCL), Hindustan Petroleum Corporation Limited (HPCL), GAIL 
(India) Limited and other Public Sector Undertakings (PSUs), have instituted robust systems 
and procedures to ensure that payments to Micro and Small Enterprises (MSEs) are made 
within the time limit as prescribed under the Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises 
Development (MSMED) Act, 2006 and the extant instructions issued by the Government 
from time to time. 

Payments are generally released within the prescribed period, subject to fulfilment of 
contractual obligations, acceptance of goods/services, submission of complete and correct 
invoices, and resolution of contractual or technical issues, if any. Instances of delay, wherever 
they occur, are primarily attributable to reasons such as submission of incomplete 
documentation, quality or technical issues, contractual disputes, reconciliation of bills, force 
majeure situations and other operational exigencies. During the last ten years, no significant 
delay in payment to MSMEs was reported by PSUs.  
 (d): As per the Public Procurement Policy for Micro and Small Enterprises (MSEs) Order, 
2012, as amended from time to time, eligible MSEs are exempted from payment of Earnest 
Money Deposit (EMD)/Bid Security in applicable procurements. However, MSE vendors and 
contractors are not exempted from Performance Security as Performance Security is 
governed as per the General Financial Rules (GFR), 2017, issued by the Department of 
Expenditure and other applicable Government instructions issued from time to time.  
 (e): The Ministry and its PSUs have taken several measures to facilitate greater participation 
of MSMEs and to ensure timely payments to them, which, inter-alia, include procurements 
being made through Government e-Marketplace and e-tendering platforms to ensure 
transparency, ease of participation and wide market access; conduct of regular vendor 
outreach programmes and capacity building initiatives; providing purchase preference under 
Public Procurement Policy for Micro and Small Enterprises (MSE) Order, 2012; relaxation in 
prior turnover and prior experience criteria; timely processing of invoice and regular 
monitoring of outstanding payments through MSME-SAMADHAAN Portal.
