GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS 
  
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 3179 
ANSWERED ON 06TH AUGUST, 2026 
  
MULTIPLE TAX ON VEHICLES 
  
3179. DR. SHARMILA SARKAR: 
                           
Will the Minister of ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS  
  
सड़क परिवहन औि िाजमार्ग मंत्री 
  
be pleased to state: 
  
(a) whether the Government has any plan to reduce the multiple tax 
burden on vehicles including Fuel Tax, Road Tax and Toll Tax 
specially during the crisis related to Strait of Hormuz; 
  
(b) if so, the details thereof along with the steps taken in this regard 
and if not, the reasons therefor; and 
  
(c) whether the Government intends to reduce or waive off Toll Tax 
if the waiting time at toll plazas exceeds certain time period and if 
so, the details thereof?  
  
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS 
(SHRI NITIN JAIRAM GADKARI) 
  
(a) to (c).  The Constitution of India empowers the States/Union 
Territories to make law for levy of motor vehicle tax.    
The excise duty or cess  on fuel is imposed by the Central 
Government and utilized for infrastructure development and 
maintenance related activities, including for railways, rural roads, 
National Highways (NH) etc. The Government  undertakes fiscal 
interventions in the petroleum s ector, as and when required, to 

protect consumers from volatility in international crude oil prices. 
Some of them are as follows: 
 In November 2021 and May 2022, the Central Government 
reduced Central Excise Duty by a total of Rs. 13/litre on petrol 
and Rs.  16/litre on diesel in two tranches, which was fully 
passed on to consumers.  
 In March 2024, Oil Marketing Companies (OMCs) reduced retail 
prices of petrol and diesel by Rs. 2 per litre each.  
 In April 2025, the increase of Rs. 2 per litre in excise duty o n 
petrol and diesel was not passed on to consumers.  
 Recently, in view of rising international crude oil prices due to 
the West Asia crisis, the Government has reduced excise duty 
by Rs. 10 per litre each on petrol and diesel to absorb part of 
the burden on consumers 
The user fee i.e. 'toll' is payable by motor vehicles for use of a 
section of a National Highway (NH) and is levied under the 
provisions of section 7 of the National Highways Act, 1956 (48 of 
1956) and rules made thereunder. The User fee at fee  plazas on 
National Highways is collected for services or benefits rendered on 
National Highways in accordance with the provision of National 
Highways Fee (Determination of Rates and Collection) Rules, 2008. 
The revenue collected by the Central Government from user fee 
collection is deposited in Consolidated Fund of India (CFI) and the 
fund provided through budgetary allocation are utilised for further 
maintenance, development and augmentation of National Highways. 
Further there is no proposal/plan currentl y under consideration by 
the Government,  to waive off / reduce the user fee specially  on 
account of the crisis related to the Strait of Hormuz. 
However, the Government from time to time has reviewed the 
tolling policy with the objective of ensuring a balan ced approach 
between revenue requirements for highway development and 
minimizing burden on road users. Further, in order to reduce the 
burden on road users, Government has made various provisions 
through following amendments: 
(i) G.S.R 388 (E) dated 17.06. 2025 introducing an Annual Pass for 
non-commercial cars, jeeps, and vans. This scheme offers 200 NH 
fee plaza crossings or one year validity, whichever is earlier, by 

payment of Rs. 3000/ - (Rupees three thousand) (3,075/ - for 
Financial Year 2026-27). 
(ii) G.S.R 437(E) dated 01.07.2025 to restrict user fee for highways 
with more structure length. 
(iii) G.S.R 734 (E) dated 03.10.2025 for reduction in applicable user 
fee for vehicles without FASTag or active FASTag vehicles from 2 
times to 1.25 times, given the user opts for payment through UPI; 
(iv) G.S.R 01(E) dated 31.12.2025 for reduction of rates in case of 
up gradation from 2 lane paved shoulder highway to 4 or more 
lane. 
(v) G.S.R 107 (E) dated 04.02.2026 for the fee payable for the use of 
a national expressway that is operational for only a part of its 
notified length shall be levied at a rate of one time of the 
applicable fee instead of 1.25 times. 
(vi) As per National Highways Fee (Determination of Rates and 
Collection) Rules, 2008, there are alread y various provisions for 
discounts in user fees and monthly passes for local and regular 
users of National Highways across the country. 
  
The Government is committed to making the tolling system more 
efficient, transparent, and user -friendly, while simulta neously 
ensuring the availability of resources for development and 
maintenance of the National Highways network. 
  
There is no provision in the National Highways Fee (Determination 
of Rates and Collection) Rules, 2008 for waiver of user fee based on 
waiting time at fee plazas.

MINISTRY OF CIVIL AVIATION 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. : 3181 
 ( TO BE ANSWERED ON THE  6th August 2026 )  
EXPANSION OF AIRPORT INFRASTRUCTURE 
3181.    SMT RACHNA BANERJEE            
          
Will the Minister of CIVIL AVIATION 
be pleased to state:- 
(a) whether the Government has undertaken any assessment of the adequacy of 
airport infrastructure and passenger handling capacity at major airports in the 
country in view of the increasing air traffic and if so, the details thereof; 
(b) the details of the airports where expansion and modernisation projects are 
currently under implementation, State-wise; 
(c) the total funds allocated and utilised for such projects during the last three 
years; and 
(d) the steps taken by the Government to ensure timely completion of these 
projects and to improve passenger amenities and safety standards? 
ANSWER 
Minister of State in the Ministry of CIVIL AVIATION       
(Shri Murlidhar Mohol) 
(a): Airport infrastructure, including passenger terminals, runways, aprons, 
cargo facilities and other airside infrastructure, is developed by the Airports 
Authority of India (AAI) and other airport operators based on traffic growth, 
operational requirements, airline demand, financial viability and techno -
economic considerations. Expansion and modernisation projects undertaken at 
airports across the country have enhanced the total passenger -handling capacity 
to over 580 million passengers per annum (MPPA), while passenger traffic 
handled during 2025-26 was about 420 million. 
 
(b): AAI has undertaken various upgradation and development works, including 
construction of new terminal buildings, aprons, Runway End Safety Areas 
(RESA), extension/re -surfacing of runways, construction/strengthening of 
Rapid Exit Taxiways (RETs) an d Link Taxi Tracks, at several airports across 
the country. The major infrastructure projects include Kadapa, Rajahmundry 
and Vijayawada in Andhra Pradesh, Darbhanga in Bihar, Keshod in Gujarat, 

Hisar in Haryana, Jammu in Jammu & Kashmir, Belagavi and Hubb alli in 
Karnataka, Calicut in Kerala, Leh in Ladakh, Imphal in Manipur, Kota and 
Udaipur in Rajasthan, Pakyong in Sikkim, Chennai in Tamil Nadu, Agra and 
Varanasi in Uttar Pradesh and Bagdogra and Kolkata in West Bengal. 
 
(c): The capital expenditure (CAP EX) for the development of airport 
infrastructure is generally incurred by the Airports Authority of India (AAI) and 
private airport operators/developers from their own resources. CAPEX 
expenditure incurred by AAI and Private Airport Operators/Developers d uring 
the last three years has been approximately Rs. 19260 crore (FY 2023 -24), Rs. 
19317 crore (FY 2024-25) and Rs. 17840 Crore (FY 2025-26). 
 
(d): To ensure timely implementation of airport expansion and modernisation 
projects, the Ministry of Civil Av iation and AAI conduct regular project 
reviews in coordination with project authorities and executing agencies.; 
Passenger experience is enhanced through initiatives such as DigiYatra, e-gates, 
in-line baggage screening, Common Use Terminal Equipment 
(CUTE)/Common Use Self -Service (CUSS) check -in systems and Automatic 
Tray Retrieval Systems (ATRS) at security checkpoints. Further, the Directorate 
General of Civil Aviation (DGCA) maintains a robust safety oversight 
mechanism through routine surveillance, spo t checks, regulatory audits and 
special audits to ensure compliance with the Aircraft Rules and Civil Aviation 
Requirements (CARs).

(a) whether the Utraula -Pachperwa-Chandanpur road connecting 
Shrawasti and Balrampur districts in Uttar Pradesh is in an 
extremely dilapidated condition, causing severe hardship to local 
citizens, far mers, traders and commuters traveling towards the 
Nepal border, if so, the details thereof;

demands raised and letters and representations submitted 
periodically by the local Member of Parli ament for the widening and

Jharkhand and Parliamentary Constituency of Dumka; and  
 
(e) the manner in which the India Energy Stack is expected to improve 
digitalisation, interoperability and efficiency in the power sector? 
 
A N S W E R 
 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF POWER  
 
(SHRI SHRIPAD NAIK)  
 
(a) to (e) :  India Energy Stack (IES) is envisioned to create a digital enablement 
for the power sector so that the disparate parts of the power system can connect 
and communicate securely through standard data exchange protocols. The 
Ministry of Power has constituted a task force comprising domain experts and 
various stakeholders, including representatives from Ministries, state utilities, 
Regulators, Gencos and Transcos, to chart a roadmap for the IES, including its 
components and design. 

 
 
 
Distribution utilities of Delhi, Gujarat, Andhra Pradesh, Uttar Pradesh and 
Mumbai have been identified for the pilot (Proof -of-Concept) implementation of 
IES, and the timeline for demonstration of the same is FY 2026 -27. The 
implementation of IES has presently been init iated only in respect of the 
distribution utilities selected for the pilot implementation.  
 
IES aims to develop unified, secure and interoperable data exchange 
mechanism so that services and systems work together seamlessly across the 
power sector value c hain. The enablement created by IES aims to facilitate 
seamless integration of technology solutions related to enhancing efficiency of 
the distribution sector and consumer -centric services like load forecasting, 
demand response programmes, energy transacti on, and overall digitalisation in 
the power sector. 
 
 
**********

3191.    SHRI SELVAGANAPATHI T.M.       
           
Will the Minister of CIVIL AVIATION 
be pleased to state:- 
(a) whether it is a fact that the Government is considering to develop more than 
350 airports by 2047 and if so, the details thereof; 
(b) whether it is also a fact that the civil aviation sector is expected to handle 
close to 500 million passenger s before 2030 and move towards 1 billion 
passengers by 2047 and if so, the details thereof; and 
(c) whether it is also true that the Government aims to reduce dependence on 
foreign hubs for international air traffic and if so, the details thereof? 
ANSWER 
Minister of State in the Ministry of CIVIL AVIATION       
(Shri Murlidhar Mohol) 
(a): In pursuance of the objectives of Viksit Bharat 2047, airport development 
and expansion are being undertaken through Greenfield airports under the 
Greenfield Airports Polic y, revival of unserved and underserved airports under

airports by the Airports Authority of India (AAI) and promotion of private 
investment through the Public -Private Partnership (PPP) mo de. At present, 25 
Greenfield airports have been accorded In-Principle Approval, of which 14 have 
been operationalised, while 6 proposals have been granted Site Clearance. 
Further, 95 aerodromes have been operationalised under RCS -UDAN. The next 
phase of the UDAN Scheme envisages connectivity to 120 new destinations and 
serving 4 crore passengers over the next ten years.

million passengers by 2046-47.

MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF PETROLEUM AND NATURAL GAS 
(SHRI SURESH GOPI) 
 
(a) and (b): Pradhan Mantri Ujjwala Yojana (PMUY) was launched in May, 2016 with an 
objective to provide deposit free LPG connection to adult women from poor households. 
Warangal (SC) Parliamentary Constituency covers districts of Jangaon, Hanmankonda, 
Warangal and Jayashankar Bhupalpally. As on 01.07.2026, there were about 10.58 crore 
PMUY connections across the country including 1.22 lakh connections in Warangal 
Parliamentary Constituency. Year-wise details of PMUY connections released in these 
districts during the last three financial years are given below:

Hanmankonda 1,068 38 253 
Warangal 717 0 43 
Jayashankar Bhupalpally 393 46 1,464

In order to encourage sustained usage among PMUY beneficiaries, various steps have been 
taken, including organizing campaigns for improving awareness about PMUY , promotion 
through Out of Home (OOH) hoardings, radio jingles, Information, Education and 
Communication (IEC) Vans etc. In addition, PMUY beneficiaries have been given Swap 
option from 14.2 kg to 5 Kg to reduce upfront cash outgo and option of 5 Kg Double Bottle 
Connection. 
  

 
India imports majority of its LPG requirement & LPG prices in the country are based on 
Saudi CP. The average Saudi CP (the international benchmark for LPG pricing) rose upto 
US$ 780/MT in April and May 2026. In June 2026, as the Saudi CP rose further to US$ 
796/MT (excluding premium), the Market Determined Price (MDP) of a 14.2 kg domestic 
LPG cylinder went upto Rs. 1,695 per 14.2 Kg cylinder.  
 
The Retail Selling Price of domestic LPG is being maintained at Rs. 942 per 14.2 Kg cylinder 
since June 2026, which carried an implicit subsidy (under-recovery) of more than Rs 700 per 
14.2 Kg cylinder in June 2026 and Rs 500 per cylinder during July 2026. Even for the month 
of August 2026, the RSP carries an implicit subsidy of Rs. 188 per cylinder. For more than 
10.5 crore PMUY consumers, the effective price is only Rs. 642 per cylinder (Delhi), after a 
targeted subsidy of Rs. 300 per cylinder. 
 
Government have been ensuring availability of domestic LPG at affordable prices to 
households in the country for which Government have paid to the OMCs compensation of 
Rs. 22,000 crore in FY 2022-23 and paying Rs. 30,000 crore during FY 2025-26 and FY 
2026-27. Even after the payment of this compensation, accumulated under-recoveries of the 
PSU OMCs on domestic LPG were more than Rs 51,000 crores as of 30th June 2026 itself. 
 
As a result of various steps taken by Government to improve access and affordability of 
domestic LPG for PMUY consumers, per connection consumption of PMUY beneficiaries (in 
terms of no. of 14.2 kg LPG cylinders taken per year) has increased from 3.68 in FY 2021-22 
to 4.71 in FY 2025-26.

UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 3193 
TO BE ANSWERED ON: 06.08.2026 
 
HUMAN-CENTERED ENTREPRENEURSHIP IN MSMEs 
 
3193.   SHRI EATALA RAJENDER: 
 
Will the Minister of MICRO, SMALL AND MEDIUM ENTERPRISES be pleased to state: 
(a)  whether the United Nations MSME Day 2026 theme is "Human -Centered 
Entrepreneurship in an AI-Driven Future", with a broader global focus on "Empowering Micro, 
Small and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs)  through Innovation and Sustainable Industrial 
Development" and if so, the details thereof; 
 
(b)  whether these themes focus on ensuring that small businesses —which make up over 
ninety per cent of global businesses and seventy per cent of employment —are not left behind in 
the rapid AI transformation and drive toward green energy and if so, the details thereof; 
 
(c)  whether the Government is taking steps to encourage MSMEs to innovate, scale up, 
build globally competitive businesses and develop "Me -First" p roducts instead of "Me -too" 
products and if so, the details thereof, the results achieved so far and the funds spent in 
Telangana; and 
 
(d)  whether industry leaders urged MSMEs to transition from low-cost "me-too" products to 
innovation-led, "me -first" scale and develop deep scientific capability to build global 
competitiveness and prioritize intellectual property and if so, the details thereof? 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE FOR MICRO, SMALL AND MEDIUM ENTERPRISES 
(SUSHRI SHOBHA KARANDLAJE) 
(a) to (d):  The themes for the observance of the United Nations MSME Day are determined 
independently, and information in this regard is not maintained by the Ministry of Micro, Small 
and Medium Enterprises (MSME). However, the Ministry is implementing various schemes and 
initiatives to promote sustainability, innovation, competitiveness, and green manufacturing 
among MSMEs, thereby enabling them to remain competitive in an evolving global business 
environment. 
 
These include the MSME Champions Scheme [comprising the M SME Sustainable 
(ZED) Certification Scheme, MSME Competitive (LEAN) Scheme and MSME Innovative  
(Incubation, Design & IPR)  Scheme], MSE Green Investment and Financing for 
Transformation (MSE -GIFT) Scheme and Scheme for Promotion and Investment in Circular 
Economy (MSE-SPICE) to promote innovation, quality improvement, circular economy, green 
manufacturing and intellectual property creation among MS Es. These initiatives support 
MSMEs in developing globally competitive products and processes. In addition, the 
Government is promoting adoption of Artificial Intelligence through the IndiaAI Mission 
implemented by the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY), which 
complements the Ministry's efforts towards technology adoption and innovation among  
MSMEs. 
 
***

entries.t: Undocumented Habitations on Private Owned Lands
entries.head:
GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF HOUSING AND URBAN AFFAIRS 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 3195 
ANSWERED ON AUGUST 06, 2026 
 
UNDOCUMENTED HABITATIONS ON PRIVATE OWNED LANDS 
 
NO. 3195 DR. C N MANJUNATH: 
    
Will the Minister of HOUSING and URBAN AFFAIRS be pleased to state: 
 
(a) whether the Government is aware that several undocumented 
habitations have emerged on privately owned lands adjoining village 
boundaries (Gramathana) over the decades due to population 
growth, if so, the details thereof; 
(b) whether the Government has taken note that many families residing 
in such areas have built houses on privately purchased plots but are 
unable to obtain ownership documents or recognition from Gram 
Panchayats, if so, the details thereof; 
(c) whether the Government proposes to treat such adjacent lands as 
deemed converted for residential use and extend regularisation 
benefits, in continuation of Government Circular No. 08 CCRV 2022 
dated 08.11.2022, if so, the details thereof; 
(d) whether the Government has issued any directions to the 'Gram 
Panchayats' to treat these buildings as regular properties and issue 
Form 11(A) for tax assessment purposes, if so, the details thereof; 
and 
(e) the steps proposed by the Government to ensure lawful ownership 
rights for these residents to access institutional credit and avoid 
exploitation by private moneylenders? 
 
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE  
MINISTRY OF HOUSING AND URBAN AFFAIRS 
(SHRI TOKHAN SAHU) 
  
(a) to (e): As per entry 18 of List II-State List of the Seventh Schedule of 
the Constitution, "Land, that is to say, rights in or over land, land tenures 
including the relation of landlord and tenant, and the collection of rents; 
transfer and alienation of agricultural land; land improvement and  
…2/- 
 

 
-2- 
agricultural loans; colonization" is a State subject. Moreover,  as per 
entry 35 of the above said List, "Works, lands and buildings vested in or 
in the possession of the State" is in purview of respective states. 
Accordingly, Land administration, maintenance of land records, land 
use conversion, regularization of properties, and levy of property tax by 
Gram Panchayats are matters under the jurisdiction of the respective 
State Governments and are governed by the provisions of the relevant 
State Acts, Rules and policies. 
In regard to the habitation areas adjoining the notified village inhabited 
(abadi) developed over time due to population growth and changing 
settlement patterns, it is stated that the identification, recognition and 
regularization of such habitations, wher ever permissible, are 
undertaken by the concerned State Governments in accordance with 
the applicable State laws and policies. 
No directions have been issued by the Ministry of Panchayati Raj to 
Gram Panchayats to treat buildings situated on such lands as regular 
properties or to issue any State-specific property tax assessment forms, 
including Form 11(A). Such matters fall within the jurisdiction of th e 
respective State Governments.  
The Ministry of Panchayati Raj co ntinues to support States/UTs in 
strengthening rural property records through the SVAMITVA Scheme, 
thereby enabling recognized property owners to obtain documented 
property rights, facilitating improved access to institutional credit, 
reducing property -related disputes, and promoting better rural 
governance. Any extension of such benefits to additional habitations or 
categories of land would be subject to the provisions of the applicable 
State laws and policies. As per data compiled in coordination with State 
Level Bankers’ Committees (SLBCs), approximately 11,000 loans 
amounting to ₹1,713 crore have been sanctioned using SVAMITVA 
property cards as collateral.

entries.t: Setting up of Agro Processing Clusters for Sugarcane By-products
entries.head:
GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF FOOD PROCESSING INDUSTRIES 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 3196 
ANSWERED ON 06TH AUGUST, 2026 
 
SETTING UP OF AGRO PROCESSING CLUSTERS FOR SUGARCANE BY-
PRODUCTS 
  
3196. SHRI HARENDRA SINGH MALIK: 
             
Will the Minister of FOOD PROCESSING INDUSTRIES be pleased to state: 
    
(a) whether there is any new budgetary proposal under the Pradhan Mantri Kisan Sampada 
Yojana to set up special Agro Processing Clusters for sugarcane by-products such as 
jaggery, vinegar and liquid jaggery in Muzaffarnagar and Bijnor and if so, the details 
thereof; 
(b) whether the Government proposes to set up modern testing laboratories and curation 
centres in Muzaffarnagar and Bijnor districts under the One District One Product (ODOP) 
initiative to make jaggery export-worthy in accordance with international standards and if 
so, the details thereof; 
(c) whether the Government proposes to cover the small processing units of the region under 
the Operation Greens to enhance their energy efficiency and encourage to adopt solar-based 
cold storages and if so, the details thereof; and 
(d) the details of the direct and indirect employment generated through the food processing 
units under Muzaffarnagar Lok Sabha Constituency during the last three years, block-wise? 
  
  
ANSWER 
 
THE MINISTER OF FOOD PROCESSING INDUSTRIES 
(SHRI CHIRAG PASWAN) 
  
(a): The Ministry of Food Processing Industries (MoFPI) has been implementing the Scheme for 
Creation of Infrastructure for Agro Processing Clusters (APC) since 2017 as a component Scheme 
of the Pradhan Mantri Kisan Sampada Yojana (PMKSY). The APC Scheme aims to create modern 
infrastructure for food processing based on a cluster approach, reduce post-harvest losses, add 
value to agricultural produce, increase farmers' income and generate employment. Under the 
Scheme, financial assistance in the form of grant-in-aid/subsidy is provided at the rate of 35% of 
the eligible project cost in General Areas and 50% in North Eastern States, including Sikkim, 
Himalayan States, notified ITDP areas and Islands, subject to a maximum of ₹10 crore. 
  
The APC Scheme is not District/ State/ Product-specific. The APC Scheme is demand-
driven and proposals are invited from prospective investors / entrepreneurs through Expressions 
of Interest (EoIs) issued by the Ministry from time to time, subject to availability of funds. At 

present, no project has been approved under the APC Scheme in Muzaffarnagar and Bijnor districts 
of Uttar Pradesh. 
  
(b): MoFPI does not establish food testing laboratories on its own. The Ministry only provides 
financial assistance for setting up Food Testing Laboratories under the Scheme for Food Safety 
and Quality Assurance Infrastructure (FSQAI). It is a demand-driven scheme. Proposals are 
invited on an all India basis through EoIs floated from time to time on the Ministry’s SAMPADA 
Portal. Selection of locations is not pre-determined and is based on the eligibility criteria, technical 
and financial viability, and merit of proposals, as per the Scheme Guidelines available on the 
Ministry’s website. At present, no proposal for establishment of Food Testing Lab in 
Muzaffarnagar and Bijnor districts is pending in the Scheme for FSQAI. 
  
Under the Pradhan Mantri Formalization of Micro food processing Enterprises (PMFME) 
Scheme, Jaggery has been identified as One District One Product (ODOP) in Muzaffarnagar and 
Bijnor districts. The Scheme is demand-driven and implemented through the respective State 
Governments/UTs. Proposals for establishment of such facilities are identified and recommended 
by the State Governments based on local requirements and approved in accordance with the 
Scheme Guidelines. No specific proposal for establishment of modern testing laboratories or 
curation centres in Muzaffarnagar and Bijnor districts has been received by the Ministry under the 
Scheme. 
  
(c): Under Operation Greens Scheme a component of PMKSY Umbrella Scheme, the Ministry is 
providing financial assistance @ 35% of the eligible project cost for projects in general category 
areas, and @ 50% for projects in difficult category areas, as well as for projects involving SC/ST, 
Farmer Producer Organizations (FPOs) and Self-Help Groups (SHGs) for value chain 
development of 10 fruit crops, 11 vegetable crops and shrimp in the identified production clusters. 
Sugarcane by-products are not covered under the Operation Greens Scheme for financial 
assistance. Further, setting up of standalone cold storage facility is also not supported under the 
Operation Greens Scheme. However, projects approved under various component Schemes of 
PMKSY are encouraged to adopt energy efficient power systems including installation of solar 
panels, as per applicable Scheme Guidelines of the component Schemes. 
  
(d): All component Schemes of the Pradhan Mantri Kisan SAMPADA Yojana (PMKSY) are 
demand-driven and applications are invited t

 Will the Minister of POWER

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF CIVIL AVIATION 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. : 3200 
 ( TO BE ANSWERED ON THE  6th August 2026 )  
CAP ON AIRFARE 
3200.    SMT BHARTI PARDHI                       
             SHRI RAVINDRA DATTARAM WAIKAR            
             DR. SHRIKANT EKNATH SHINDE              
             SHRI SHRIRANG APPA CHANDU BARNE          
             SHRI NARESH GANPAT MHASKE                
Will the Minister of CIVIL AVIATION 
be pleased to state:- 
(a) the details of the regulatory mec hanism currently available with the Government to prevent 
financial exploitation of passengers by domestic airlines through steep fare hikes - surging from Rs. 
5000 upto Rs. 50,000 - during peak travel dates or festive seasons; 
 
(b) whether the Government is aware that due to dynamic pricing algorithms used by airlines, air 
travel has become unaffordable for the common man and if so, the details thereof; 
 
(c) whether the Government proposes to fix an upper cap on domestic airfares and if so, the details 
thereof; 
 
(d) whether the Government proposes to amend Rule 135 of the Aircraft Rules, 1937, to bring 
transparency and prevent airlines from misusing the pricing autonomy granted to them under the said 
Rule; and 
 
(e) the special measures being taken by the Go vernment to check predatory pricing across all routes 
during emergencies or peak periods in view of the Tariff Monitoring Unit of the Directorate General 
of Civil Aviation (DGCA) monitoring airfares only on limited routes? 
ANSWER 
Minister of State in the Ministry of CIVIL AVIATION      (Shri Murlidhar Mohol) 
(a) to (e): With the repeal of Air Corporation Act in March 1994, airfares are not subject to be 
regulated by the Government. Airlines have the autonomy to establish airfare based on their 
operational &  economic viability on a particular route while adhering to Rule 135 of the Aircraft 
Rules, 1937.; 
; 
The pricing of airfares is subject to dynamic fluctuations influenced by the forces of supply and 
demand. Various determinants such as current seat occupancy, fuel costs, aircraft capacity, seasonal 
fluctuations and other relevant factors significantly impact airline ticket pricing.; 
; 
Airline pricing runs in multiple levels {buckets or RBDs} which are in line with the practice being 
followed globally. The lower fare is always available for the passengers for advance booking which 
enables passengers to get more affordable fares even during peak travel dates or festive seasons. As 

time lapses and date of journey approaches closer, the fare moves to high er buckets, since lower 
buckets fare get sold out.; 
; 
The Government generally refrains from regulating airfares to maintain market competitiveness, 
however, it retains vigilant oversight role, intervening in exceptional circumstances by redistributing 
capacity across various sectors and imposing temporary fare caps, such as during the Covid 
Pandemic, festivals like Maha kumb or other extraordinary instances like Pahalgam incident & the 
Indigo flight disruptions.; 
; 
In order to enhance the transparency in airfare, Directorate General of Civil Aviation (DGCA) has set-
up Tariff Monitoring Unit  (TMU) that monitors airfares on selected 78 routes on a random basis by 
using airlines websites on monthly basis to ensure that the airlines do not charge airfares outs ide the 
range declared by them. This covers about 27% of the domestic traffic. By doing so, the TMU plays a 
critical role in maintaining airfare levels within the boundaries of the airlines' prescribed tariffs.;

scheme and launched PMAY -U 2.0 ‘Housing for All’ Mission with effect 
from 01.09.2024 for implementation in  
urban areas across the country to support 1 crore additional eligible

grounded and 99.07 lakh are completed/delivered to the beneficiaries

COMPRESSED BIO-GAS PLANTS UNDER SATAT SCHEME

Will the Minister of PETROLEUM AND NATURAL GAS be pleased to state: 
 
(a) the actual percentage of financial assistance utilised at the ground level out of the total 
funds released during the year 2025-26 for setting up Compressed Bio-Gas (CBG) plants 
under the Sustainable Alternative Towards Affordable Transportation (SATAT) Scheme in 
the country, including Uttar Pradesh and the Jaunpur Parliamentary Constituency, along with 
the total number of CBG plants sanctioned and established;  
(b) the total number of sanctioned plants where construction work remains incomplete due to 
land-related issues, feedstock supply issues, including waste and crop stubble, technical 
constraints or other reasons, in the rural areas of Uttar Pradesh and the Jaunpur Parliamentary 
Constituency, along with the major reasons therefor; 
(c) whether the Government has taken cognizance of or has assessed that excessive 
administrative delays are being caused by Oil Marketing Companies in the procurement of 
bio-gas, execution of Gas Supply Agreements and the development of pipeline and other 
required infrastructure under this scheme, if so, the details thereof; and 
(d) whether the Government has formulated any plan or is implementing any special scheme 
to generate sustainable employment opportunities in technical and non-technical sectors for 
local rural youth through bio-gas plants and agricultural residue management units, 
particularly in the Jaunpur Parliamentary Constituency, if so, the details thereof?

MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF PETROLEUM AND NATURAL GAS  
(SHRI SURESH GOPI) 
 
(a) to (d) Government, with a view to promoting the setting up of Compressed Biogas (CBG) 
plants across the country has adopted a “Whole of Government” approach involving multiple 
Ministries and Departments under the Galvanizing Organic Bio-Agro Resources Dhan 
(GOBARdhan) initiative. The Government is providing various policy and institutional 
enablers to create a supportive ecosystem for CBG projects across the country including Uttar 
Pradesh and Jaunpur Parliamentary Constituency, of which Sustainable Alternative Towards 
Affordable Transportation (SATAT) is one such initiative.  

Under the SATAT initiative, Oil and Gas Marketing Companies (OGMCs) invite Expressions 
of Interest (EOIs) from entrepreneurs for procurement of CBG. Government does not provide 
any financial assistance for establishment of CBG plants under SATAT initiative. 
CBG plants are established by entrepreneurs based on the techno-commercial feasibility of 
their projects. As per information compiled from the GOBARdhan Portal, 217 CBG plants, 
with an aggregate production capacity of approximately 1,773 tonnes per day, have been 
commissioned as on 31st July, 2026, including 180 CBG plants under SATAT and CBG-
CGD Synchronisation Scheme.  
In Uttar Pradesh, 41 CBG plants have been commissioned, including 40 under the SATAT 
initiative and the CBG-CGD Synchronisation Scheme.  
The Government periodically reviews matters relating to constraints in construction of CBG 
plant, procurement of CBG, development of pipeline, other supporting infrastructure etc. in 
consultation with OGMCs, CBG producers and other stakeholders, and take up the matter to 
address the challenges.  
During these reviews it was observed that constraints hindering the establishment of CBG 
projects inter-alia includes land-related issues, feedstock availability and aggregation, 
statutory clearances, financing, technical and commercial considerations and other project-
specific factors.  
Under the Development of Pipeline Infrastructure (DPI) Scheme, financial assistance is 
provided to eligible CBG producers, City Gas Distribution (CGD) entities and natural gas 
pipeline operators for establishing pipeline connectivity between CBG plants/clusters and the 
CGD or natural gas pipeline network to facilitate CBG evacuation and offtake. 
The factors that deter the connecting pipeline project are CBG plant readiness, techno-
commercial feasibility of the project, execution of tripartite agreement under CBG-CGD 
synchronization scheme, statutory clearances, and connectivity-related issues.  
CBG plants promote a circular economy by converting agricultural residues, cattle dung and 
organic waste into clean fuel and organic manure. They generate direct and indirect 
employment in feedstock aggregation, transportation, plant construction, operation and

3204. SHRI HASMUKHBHAI SOMABHAI PATEL: 
SHRI VIVEK THAKUR: 
 
 Will the Minister of POWER 
be pleased to state: 
 
(a) the present status of Pumped Storage Projects (PSPs) under construction at 
various stages of approval across the country;  
 
(b) the  measures taken to facilitate timely environmental and statutory 
clearances for such projects;  
 
(c) the role envisaged for Pumped Storage in integrating renewable energy and 
managing peak demand; and  
 
(d) the steps taken to encourage greater participation of the private sector in the 
development of PSPs? 
A N S W E R 
 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF POWER  
 
(SHRI SHRIPAD NAIK)  
 
(a) : Presently, 11 PSPs with an aggregate installed capacity of 15,870 MW are 
under construction in the country (Annexure-I). Further, 6 PSPs with total 
installed capacity of 8,140 MW have been concurred/appraised by Central 
Electricity Authority (CEA) and are yet to be taken up for construction (Annexure-
II), and 1 PSP with an installed capacity of 640 MW is under examination in CEA 
(Annexure-III). 
 
(b) : The measures taken to facilitate timely environmental and statutory 
clearances for such projects are as under: 
 
(i)  Ministry of Environment, Forest & Climate Change (MoEF&CC), vide its 
notification dated 18.05.2023, has enabled appraisal of PSPs under B2 category 
subject to certain conditions.  
  
(ii)  The MoEF&CC on 14.08.2023, has issued specific Terms of Reference (TOR) 
for the proposals involving off stream PSPs wherein collection of baseline data 
for one season (other than monsoon) is prescribed for off stream closed loop PSPs 
and collection of baseline data for two seasons (pre-monsoon & post-monsoon) is 
prescribed for off stream open loop PSPs.

(iii)  The MOEF&CC on 20.08.2024, has extended the  provisions relating to 
survey in the forest areas for mining projects to other development projects 
including hydel/PSPs.  
 
(iv)  MOEF&CC vide letter dated 10.09.2025  has enhanced the number of 
boreholes for undertaking survey and explorations in the fore st area for mining 
and developmental projects including hydel / PSPs. 
 
(v)  CEA has revised Guidelines for formulation and concurrence of Detailed 
Project Report (DPR) of PSPs. Under the revised guidelines, the timeline for 
concurrence of DPR has been reduced from 90 days to 50 days for PSPs. Further, 
the clearance of Inter-State Aspects is not required for PSPs. 
 
(vi)  The Government of India, vide Gazette notification dated 01.08.2025, has 
revised the capital expenditure limit for schemes related to s etting up hydro 
generating stations to ₹3,000 crore, requiring the concurrence of the CEA. 
Further, the Government has exempted off -stream closed-loop pumped storage 
schemes, irrespective of the quantum of capital expenditure, from the 
requirement of concurrence by the CEA.  
 
(c) : Pumped Storage Projects (PSPs) support the integration of renewable 
energy by storing surplus energy during off -peak periods and supplying power 
during peak demand. They provide long-duration energy storage, balancing power 
and a ncillary grid services such as frequency regulation, voltage support and 
black start capability, thereby supporting grid stability, reliability and higher 
renewable energy penetration.  
 
(d) : Central Government has taken a number of measures to encourage greater 
private sector participation in the development of PSPs as listed below: 
 
(i) Ministry of Power has notified Guidelines to promote development of 
Pumped Storage Projects in the country on 10.04.2023. 
 
(ii) Budgetary Support towards Cost of Enabling  Infrastructure, i.e., 
roads/bridges, railway sidings, ropeways, communication infrastructure and 
transmission line from power house to nearest pooling point. 
 
(iii) To provide a transparent, fair, standardized procurement framework based 
on open competiti ve bidding with appropriate risk -sharing between various 
stakeholders, MoP vide Gazette notification dated 06.02.2025, has notified tariff 
based competitive bidding (TBCB) guidelines for procurement of storage 
capacity/stored energy from pumped storage plants.  
 
(iv) The Central Electricity Regulatory Commission (CERC), vide its Notification 
dated 26.06.2025, has provided for 100% waiver of Inter -State Transmission 
System (ISTS) charges for PSPs for a period of 25 years from the Commercial 
Operation Date (COD), in respect of projects for which the construction work is 
awarded on or before 30.06.2028.

†3205. Shri Ramashankar Vidharthi Rajbhar:  
 
पेĚोͧलयम एवं Ĥाकृ Ǔतक गैस मंğी 
 
 Will the Minister of PETROLEUM AND NATURAL GAS be pleased to state: 
 
(a) the details of the number of families provided with Liquefied Petroleum Gas (LPG) 
connections under the Pradhan Mantri Ujjwala Yojana (PMUY) across the country and in 
Uttar Pradesh and the number of beneficiaries currently using LPG cylinders regularly; 
 
(b) whether the Government has assessed that poor families are reverting to traditional fuels 
due to the rising prices of gas cylinders, if so, the details thereof along with the corrective 
measures taken by the Government in this regard; 
 
(c) the details of the number of LPG distribution centres in the Purvanchal region, including 
Deoria and Ballia districts, along with the steps taken to ensure timely supply to rural 
consumers; and 
 
(d) whether the Government is considering establishing a permanent mechanism to provide 
regular supply of LPG at affordable prices to the beneficiaries of Ujjwala Yojana, if so, the 
details thereof? 
ANSWER 
 
पेĚोͧलयम एवं Ĥाकृ Ǔतक गैस मंğालय मɅ राÏयमंğी 
(Įी सुरेश गोपी) 
 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF PETROLEUM AND NATURAL GAS 
(SHRI SURESH GOPI) 
 
(a) to (d): Pradhan Mantri Ujjwala Yojana (PMUY) was launched in May, 2016 with an 
objective to provide deposit free LPG connection to adult women from poor households 
across the country. As on 01.07.2026, there were about 10.58 crore PMUY connections. India 
imports majority of its LPG requirement & LPG prices in the country are based on Saudi CP.  
 
The average Saudi CP (the international benchmark for LPG pricing) rose upto US$ 780/MT 
in April and May 2026. In June 2026, as the Saudi CP rose further to US$ 796/MT 
(excluding premium), the Market Determined Price (MDP) of a 14.2 kg domestic LPG 
cylinder went upto Rs. 1,695 per 14.2 Kg cylinder.  

 
The Retail Selling Price of domestic LPG is being maintained at Rs. 942 per 14.2 Kg cylinder 
since June 2026, which carried an implicit subsidy (under-recovery) of more than Rs 700 per 
14.2 Kg cylinder in June 2026 and Rs 500 per cylinder during July 2026. Even for the month 
of August 2026, the RSP carries an implicit subsidy of Rs. 188 per cylinder. For more than 
10.5 crore PMUY consumers, the effective price is only Rs. 642 per cylinder (Delhi), after a 
targeted subsidy of Rs. 300 per cylinder. 
  
Government have been ensuring availability of domestic LPG at affordable prices to 
households in the country for which Government have paid to the OMCs compensation of 
Rs. 22,000 crore in FY 2022-23 and paying Rs. 30,000 crore during FY 2025-26 and FY 
2026-27. Even after the payment of this compensation, accumulated under-recoveries of the 
PSU OMCs on domestic LPG were more than Rs 51,000 crores as of 30th June 2026 itself. 
 
To further improve availability through last-mile delivery in remote & rural habitations, 
several measures have been taken, including commissioning of rural and remote-area 
distributorships, appointment of Common Service Center - Village Level Entrepreneur (CSC 
VLEs), availability of various electronic options for booking and tracking.  
 
Purvanchal region of Uttar Pradesh covers the districts of Varanasi, Ghazipur, Chandauli, 
Jaunpur, Bhadohi, Mirzapur, Sonbhadra, Mau, Azamgarh, Ballia, Deoria, Kushi Nagar, 
Gorakhpur, Maharajganj, Sant Kabir Nagar, Basti, Siddharth Nagar, Prayagraj, Pratapgarh, 
Fatehpur and Kaushambi. The district-wise total number of LPG distributors and number of 
distributors catering to rural areas in Purvanchal region including Ballia and Deoria is as at 
Annexure-A.

FHTCs UNDER JJM IN BIHAR 
 
3208. SHRI ARUN BHARTI: 
 SHRI RAJESH VERMA: 
 DR. LATA WANKHEDE: 
 SMT. SHAMBHAVI: 
Will the Minister of JAL SHAKTI be pleased to state: 
(a) the physical progress achieved in providing Functional Household Tap Connections 
(FHTCs) under the Jal Jeevan Mission (JJM) in Bihar during 2025-26; 
(b) the total Central financial assista nce allocated, released and utilised by the State 
implementing agencies for rural water supply projects in Bihar during the last one year; 
(c) the total number of Gram Panchayats in Bihar that have been declared as 'Har Ghar Jal' 
certified by the Village Water and Sanitation Committees; 
(d) whether the Government has identified recurring delays in laying water distribution 
networks due to flooding or difficult terrain in the northern districts of Bihar and if so, the 
details thereof; and 
(e) the steps taken by the Government to ensure the continuous operation and maintenance of 
piped water supply schemes by local Panchayats in Bihar? 
 
ANSWER 
 
THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR JAL SHAKTI 
(SHRI V. SOMANNA)  
(a) Drinking water is a State  subject, and therefore, the responsibility for planning, approval, 
implementation, operation and maintenance of drinking water supply schemes, including those 
under Jal Jeevan Mission (JJM), lies with the respective State/UT Governments. The 
Government of  India supplements the efforts of the States/UTs by providing financial and 
technical assistance for implementation of the Mission. 
Since August 2019, Government of India, in partnership with States/UTs including Bihar, has 
been implementing JJM – Har Ghar Jal to make provision of tap water supply to every rural 
household of the country.  In March 2026, the Union Cabinet has approved extension of the 
JJM up to December 2028, with an enhanced outlay and a restructured implementation 

Page 2 of 2 
 
framework focusing on structural reforms in the rural drinking water supply sector under JJM 
2.0. 
At the start of the Mission, around 3.16 lakh (1.89 %) rural households were reported to have 
tap water connections in State of Bihar. So far, as reported by the State on JJM -IMIS, around 
1.57 crore rural households have been provided with tap water connections. Thus, as on 
19.07.2026, out of 1.67 crore rural households in the State, around 1.60 crore (95.71%) 
households are reported to have tap water connections in their homes. Further , as reported by 
the State, during 2025-26, the state has provided 737 tap water connections.  
(b) No central financial assistance has been allocated or released to State of Bihar during 2025-
26.  
(c) As reported by State of Bihar on JJM -IMIS, 741 Gram Panchayats have been certified as 
Har Ghar Jal.  
(d) As informed by State government of Bihar, certain districts in North Bihar are prone to 
annual flooding, waterlogging, river course changes and difficult geographical conditions, 
which occasionally affect t he execution of water supply schemes, including laying of 
distribution of pipelines. Such challenges are generally experienced in districts adjoining major 
rivers such as Kosi, Gandak, Bagmati, Kamla, Burhi Gandak and Mahananda. The State 
Department addresses these challenges through suitable engineering interventions, revise work 
planning, elevated structures wherever required, protective measures and close monitoring for 
timely completion of schemes.  
(e) As informed by State government of Bihar, several measures have been undertaken to 
ensure sustainable operation and maintenance of rural piped water supply schemes. These 
include: 
i. Capacity building and training of local functionaries; 
ii. Regular water quality monitoring and surveillance through NABL accredited 
laboratories; 
iii. Periodic inspection and monitoring by Public Health Engineering officials; and 
iv. Prompt rectification of operational issues to ensure uninterrupted supply of safe 
drinking water. 
Further, Ward Implementation Management Committees (WIMCs)/Pan chayats have been 
entrusted with responsibilities relating to testing of water quality using Field Testing Kits 
(FTKs), collection of water user charges, monitoring the functioning of water supply schemes, 
and organizing Jal Chaupals.

A N S W E R 
 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF POWER  
 
(SHRI SHRIPAD NAIK)  
 
(a): Government of India has taken the following actions to increase power 
generation, transmission and distribution capacity in the country: 
 
 1. Generation and Storage Planning: 
 
(i) As per National Electricity Plan (Generation), installed generation 
capacity in 2031 -32 is likely to be 874 GW. With a view to ensure 
generation capacity remains ahead of projected demand, all the States, 
in consultation with CEA, have prepared their “Resource Adequacy Plans 
(RAPs)”, which are dynamic 10 -year rolling plans and includes power 
generation as well as power procurement planning. 
 

(ii) All the States were advised to initiate process for creating/ contracting 
generation capacities; from al l generation sources, as per their 
Resource Adequacy Plans. 
 
(iii)   In order to augment the power generation capacity, the Government of 
India has initiated following capacity addition programme:  
 
a.  Thermal Capacity Addition: The projected thermal (coal and lignite) 
capacity requirement by the year 2035 –36 is estimated at approximately 
3,15,000 MW as against the 2,11,855 MW installed capacity as on 
31.03.2023. To meet this requirement, Ministry of Power has envisaged to 
set up an additional minimum 1,05,000 M W coal and lignite based thermal 
capacity. 
 
  Accordingly, Thermal capacities of around 21,080 MW have been 
commissioned since April 2023 till 30.06.2026. In addition, 47,545 MW of 
thermal capacity (including 4,845 MW of stressed thermal power projects) 
is currently under construction. The contracts of 16,000 MW have been 
awarded and are due for construction.  
 
 b.  Central Electricity Authority (CEA) has projected hydro power 
capacity addition of about 16,448 MW during the period 2026 –27 to 2031–
32. Of this, 400 MW has been commissioned as on 30.06.2026 and 12,973 
MW are presently under construction. 
  
 c.  Nuclear Capacity Addition: 8,000 MW of Nuclear Capacity is under 
construction and targeted to be completed by 2031-32. 5,600 MW of Nuclear 
Capacity is under various stages of planning and approval. 
 
 d.  Renewables Capacity Addition: 1,47,720 MW Renewable Capacity 
including 119,580 MW of Solar (including Hybrid -Solar) and 27,720 MW of 
Wind (including Hybrid -wind) is under construction while 47,830 MW of 
Renewable Capacity including 44,440 MW of Solar is at various stages of 
planning and targeted to be completed by 2029-30.   
 
    e.  Addition of Energy Storage Systems:  As on 30.06.2026, 15,870 
MW/95,220 MWh Pumped Storage Projects (PSPs) are under constru ction. 
Further, a total of 6,580 MW/39,480 MWh capacity of Pumped Storage 
Projects (PSPs) are concurred and yet to be taken up for construction. As 
on 30.06.2026, 15,754 MW / 42,530 MWh Battery Energy Storage System 
(BESS) capacity are under construction, 11,747 MW / 38,425 MWh has been 
awarded and 19,192 MW / 67,574 MWh BESS capacity are under tendering 
stage. 
 
2. Promotion of Renewable Energy (RE) Generation:  
 
(i) 100% Inter State Transmission System (ISTS) charges have been waived 
for inter -state sale of so lar and wind power for projects to be 
commissioned by 30th June 2025 (with waiver tapering off 25% annually 
till June 2028), for co -located BESS projects commissioned by June 

2028, for Hydro PSP projects where construction work awarded by June 
2028, for Gr een Hydrogen Projects commissioned till December 2030 
and for offshore wind projects commissioned till December 2032. 
 
 
(ii) Standard Bidding Guidelines for tariff based competitive bidding process 
for procurement of Power from Grid Connected Solar, Wind, Wind -Solar 
Hybrid and Firm & Dispatchable RE (FDRE) projects have been issued. 
 
(iii) Renewable Energy Implementing Agencies (REIAs) are regularly inviting 
bids for procurement of RE power.  
 
(iv) Foreign Direct Investment (FDI) has been permitted up to 100 percent 
under the automatic route.  
 
(v) To augment transmission infrastructure needed for steep RE trajectory, 
transmission plan has been prepared

ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR JAL SHAKTI 
(SHRI V. SOMANNA)  
(a) to (c) Drinking Water is a ‘State’ subject, and therefore,  the responsibility of planning, approval, 
implementation, operation & maintenance of drinking water supply schemes including those under Jal 
Jeevan Mission (JJM) lies with State/UT Governments. The Government of India supports the States 
by providing technical and financial assistance for the implementation of the mission.  
Since August 2019, Government of India, in partnership with States/UTs including Jammu & 
Kashmir, has been implementing JJM – Har Ghar Jal to make provision of tap water supply to every  
rural household of the country. In March 2026, the Union Cabinet has approved extension of the JJM 
up to December 2028, with an enhanced outlay and a restructured implementation framework focusing 
on structural reforms in the rural drinking water supply sector under JJM 2.0.  
As informed by UT of Jammu & Kashmir, approximately 77% (2,44,337) of the total 3,18,600 
households have been provided with tap water connection as on date in Baramulla Lok Sabha

Of these 525 schemes, 250 schemes have been physically completed, while the remaining 275 
schemes are at various stages of execution. These schemes are expected to be completed by December 
2028, in accordance with the timeline of extension of JJM 2.0. 
Under JJM, this Department releases funds to States/UTs only. Further, district -wise fund allocations 
are made and maintain ed by State/UTs Governments. Under first phase of JJM, the UT of Jammu & 
Kashmir was allocated Rs. 18,514.25 crore, of which only Rs.6,496.48 crore was drawn. Under JJM 
2.0, for the FY 2026 -27, the UT has been allocated Rs.905.74 crore, of which mother san ction of

(a) whether the Government has received complaints regarding illegal 
collection of money  from commercial vehicles on National Highways, 
particularly in the name of "Mechanical Pass" or  other unauthorized 
charges, if so, the details thereof; 
(b) whether the Government has identified National Highway stretches 
where such illegal  collections and harassment of transporters are 
frequently reported and if so, the details thereof; 
(c) whether the Government has issued any guidelines or directions to 
NHAI, concessionaires  and enforcement agencies to prevent 
unauthorized collections and ensure smooth movement of  commercial 
vehicles; and 
(d) the details of the action taken or proposed to be taken by the 
Government t o eliminate  such illegal practices and safeguard the 
interests of transporters?  

2 
 
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS 
(SHRI NITIN JAIRAM GADKARI) 
(a) User fee at fee plazas on National Highways is collected only in 
accordance with the provisions of the National Highways Fee 
(Determination of Rates and Collection) Rules, 2008 and the respective 
Concession Agreements. 
No such pass, namely "Mechanical Pass", is issued to commercial 
vehicles at National Highway fee plazas. 
(b)  No such Nati onal Highway stretch has been identified for illegal 
collection. 
(c) The Government has issued various instructions and Standard 
Operating Procedures (SOPs) to ensure transparency and operational 
integrity in user fee collection at National Highway fee pla zas. In this 
regard, the National Highways Authority of India (NHAI) has issued a 
Standard Operating Procedure dated 25.01.2024 for Operational 
Transparency in Tolling Operations, which provides for surprise 
inspections and regular monitoring to ensure tha t all cash and FASTag 
transactions are processed only through the Toll Management System 
Software. 
(d) To ensure operational integrity, transparency and safeguard the 
interest of road users in user fee collection on National Highways, the 
Government has implemented FASTag -based Electronic Toll Collection 
system. Presently, approximately more than 98% of  user fee collection 
takes place through FASTag under National Electronic Toll Collection 
(NETC) program. All the FASTag transactions are processed in a secured 
ecosystem involving Toll Management System Software, Acquirer Bank 
at fee plaza, National Payme nt Corporation of India (NPCI) as Central 
Clearing House (CCH) and FASTag Issuer Bank. The transaction involves 
a transparent process wherein the deducted user fee (Toll) is informed to 
the highway users and recorded in a central repository. The Electronic  
Toll Collection (ETC) system is designed in such a way that no FASTag 

3 
 
transaction can take place without the participation of all three 
stakeholders i.e., Acquirer Bank at user fee plaza, NPCI and Issuer Bank. 
In order to ensure the smooth functioning of fee plazas and enhance 
transparency, the Government has discontinued cash collection at all NH 
fee plazas with effect from April 2026. Accordingly, User Fee is being 
collected through FASTag/UPI only. 
Further, In order to enhance toll operations and enable  seamless 
movement of vehicles, the Government has adopted a phased rollout of 
Multi-Lane Free Flow (MLFF) user fee collection on 4 -lane and above 
National Highways, based on the outcomes and efficacy of the awarded 
projects. Under the MLFF tolling system,  gantry-mounted high -
performance Radio Frequency Identification (RFID) readers and 
Automatic Number Plate Recognition (ANPR) cameras are used for the 
deduction of user fees through the existing FASTag system,  thereby 
eliminating manual intervention or cash  handling at fee collection 
points. This facilitates barrier -less tolling, wherein user fees are 
collected from vehicle users without requiring them to stop, slow down, 
or remain in a designated lane.  
The Government, through NHAI Rajmarg Yatra App, takes prompt 
corrective action in cases of any complaints, violations, including 
issuance of show -cause notices and penalties as per the applicable 
contractual provisions.

entries.head:
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 3213 
TO BE ANSWERED ON 06 AUGUST, 2026 
Transportation Subsidy for LPG Cylinders in Lakshadweep 
 
3213. SHRI MUHAMMED HAMDULLAH SAYEED: 
 
पेटŌोिलयम और Ůाक ृ ितक गैस मंũी 
Will the Minister of PETROLEUM AND NATURAL GAS be pleased to state: 
(a) whether the Government is aware of the high costs borne by the residents of Lakshadweep 
Islands for domestic cooking gas due to steep maritime transportation charges, if so, the 
details thereof; 
(b) whether there is any proposal to introduce a dedicated transportation subsidy for 
Liquefied Petroleum Gas (LPG) cylinders supplied to the Islands, if so, the details thereof; 
and 
(c) the details of the measures taken to ensure affordable and seamless access to domestic 
fuel for consumers living in the Islands? 
ANSWER 
पेटŌोिलयम और Ůाक ृ ितक गैस मंũालय मŐ राǛ मंũी 
(ŵी सुर ेश गोपी) 
 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF PETROLEUM AND NATURAL GAS 
 (SHRI SURESH GOPI) 
(a) to (c): Distribution of LPG in Lakshadweep islands is currently done by Indian Oil 
Corporation Limited (IOCL) through Lakshadweep Co-operative Marketing Federation 
(LCMF), designated as the wholesale agent of Lakshadweep Administration under Public 
Distribution System. 
The Retail Selling Price of domestic LPG at Kochi as on 31.07.2026 is Rs. 949 per 14.2 Kg 
cylinder. While the pricing of Lakshadweep is based on Kochi market in Kerala, additional 
transportation and handling charges for bringing the cylinder to various islands of the UT are 
charged from consumers by LCMF. As a result, the Retail Selling Price of domestic LPG in 
Lakshadweep islands is higher than that of Kochi. 
The Retail Selling Prices in various islands of Lakshadweep vary from island to island based 
on the expenditure incurred on placement of cylinders by Lakshadweep Co-operative 
Marketing Federation (LCMF). The amount of expenditure incurred on transportation 
charges, handling and port charges, etc. is worked out by LCMF and is charged from LPG 
consumers. 
To ensure seamless LPG supplies in Lakshadweep islands, IOCL has hired two marine 
vessels MV Elikalpeni and MV Ganga for placement of LPG cylinders at various islands of 
Lakshadweep, incurring additional costs which are currently being borne by IOCL.

3217.   SHRI AJAY BHATT: 
 
Will the Minister of MICRO, SMALL AND MEDIUM ENTERPRISES be pleased to state: 
 
(a)  whether the Government has launched the Udyam Sakhi Portal to promote self -reliance 
among women in the country and if so, the details thereof; 
(b)  whether any budgetary allocation has been made for the said Portal and if so, the details 
thereof; 
(c)  the total number of beneficiaries who have availed benefits through the said Portal, year -
wise and State-wise; 
(d) whether the Government has launched any scheme for the economic  
empowerment of women entrepreneurs and women -led startups and if so,   
the details thereof along with the number of women beneficiaries under the  
said scheme, State-wise; and

including in Uttarakhand? 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE FOR MICRO, SMALL AND MEDIUM ENTERPRISES 
 (SUSHRI SHOBHA KARANDLAJE) 
 
(a), (b), (c) & (e):  The Udyam Sakhi Portal was conceptualized and launched in 2018 to promote 
women entrepreneurship by providing a digital platform offering information on Government 
schemes, policies, programmes, business planning, financial assistance, mentoring, training, 
exhibitions and other support services to enable women to establish and expand their enterprises. An 
expenditure of ₹43.52 lakh was incurred towards the development of the Portal in 2018. Thereafter, 
no separate budgetary allocation or project -wise fund allocation/utili sation has been made for the 
Udyam Sakhi Portal. A total of 4580 women entrepreneurs had registered on the Portal, and the 
State-wise details of beneficiaries, including Uttarakhand are placed at Annexure-I. 
 
Subsequently, in view of the Government's effor ts to mainstream support for women 
entrepreneurs through a unified digital ecosystem comprising the Udyam Registration Portal (URP), 
Udyam Assist Platform (UAP) and the Ministry's Yashasvini Initiative, the objectives of the Udyam 
Sakhi Portal have been subsumed under these platforms. Accordingly, the Udyam Sakhi Portal has 
been discontinued and a communication in this regard has been issued vide OM dated 01.01.2026. 
Women entrepreneurs registered on the Udyam Sakhi Portal have been onboarded to the Udyam 
Registration Portal/Udyam Assist Platform. 
  
(d):  Ministry of MSME has launched several schemes for the economic empowerment of 
MSMEs (including women owned MSMEs) such as Prime Minister's Employment Generation 
Programme (PMEGP), Credit Guarantee Fund Trus t for Micro and Small Enterprises (CGTMSE), 
IC Scheme, Coir Vikas Yojana, SFURTI, ESDP and other interventions. The State -wise details of 
registered beneficiaries under the said scheme are placed as Annexure-II.

DIESEL PURCHASE LIMIT FOR FARMERS 
 
 
† 3219. SHRI KULDEEP INDORA: 
 
पेᮝोिलयम और ᮧाक ृ ितक गैस मंᮢी 
 
Will the Minister of PETROLEUM AND NATURAL GAS be pleased to state: 
 
(a) whether the Government has taken cognizance of the hardship faced by farmers in major 
agricultural belts, including Sri Ganganagar and Hanumangarh, due to the 200-litre purchase 
limit on diesel for agricultural activities, affecting Kharif season cultivation and irrigation, if so, 
the details thereof; 
(b) whether the Government has conducted an assessment of the actual diesel requirements of 
farmers for operating tractors, harvesters, irrigation pumps and other agricultural machinery, if 
so, the details thereof; 
(c) whether the Government proposes to review the agricultural diesel purchase ceiling to  
restore adequate supplies as before; and 
(d) if so, the details thereof along with the proposed timeline for its implementation? 
 
ANSWER 
 
पेᮝोिलयम और ᮧाक ृ ितक गैस मंᮢालय मᱶ रा᭔यमंᮢी 
(᮰ी सुरेश गोपी) 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF PETROLEUM AND NATURAL GAS 
(SHRI SURESH GOPI) 
 
(a) to (d) : Owing to the West Asia Crisis, International Crude Oil prices increased sharply. To 
protect retail consumers, though the full increase in the price of High-Speed Diesel (HSD) was 
passed on to bulk consumers, only a partial increase was passed on to retail consumers resulting 
in a significant price differential between bulk price and retail price of HSD. This resulted into 
uneven extraordinary demand growth in some retail outlets due to shifting of bulk diesel volume 
to PSU Oil Marketing Retail Outlets (ROs). This was driven by industrial, commercial and 
institutional consumers shifting their procurement from their dedicated consumer pumps to  ROs 
due to the said price difference between bulk and retail diesel prices.  The diversion of HSD by 
bulk consumers led to localized supply issues and potential disruptions for bona fide retail 
consumers and essential services.  
 
To address this situation and to ensure the availability and equitable distribution of HSD, the 
Central Government notified the Motor Spirit and High-Speed Diesel (Temporary Regulation of 
Supply through Retail Outlets) Order, 2026 on 11.06.2026 and on 12.06.2026, it issued 
directions to PSU OMCs introducing temporary restrictions on Sale of HSD from their 
RetailOutlets.  These measures were aimed at preventing black marketing, hoarding and 
diversion of HSD while ensuring uninterrupted availability of MS and HSD to retail consumers.  
 
Following a review of the supply situation of petroleum products in the country, the 
Government decided to withdraw the temporary restrictions in public interest   w.e.f. 1st July 
2026 thereby restoring the normal supply arrangements of MS and HSD across the country 
including Ganganagar and Hanumangarh.

entries.t: Discoveries of New Oil and Natural Gas Reserves
entries.head:
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 3220 
TO BE ANSWERED ON 6th AUGUST, 2026 
 
Discoveries of New Oil and Natural Gas Reserves 
†3220. Shri Arun Govil: 
 
Will the Minister of PETROLEUM AND NATURAL GAS be pleased to state: 
 
(a) whether the discovery of new oil and natural gas reserves or the presence of hydrocarbons in 
Uttar Pradesh, Rajasthan, Bihar, Andaman and other areas has been confirmed in recent years, if 
so, the details thereof; 
(b) the areas where commercial production is likely to commence on the basis of such discoveries 
and the time by which the same is likely to commence; 
(c) the extent to which the country's domestic production of oil and natural gas and its import 
dependence are likely to be reduced through such discoveries; and 
(d) whether the Government is taking any special initiatives to expedite the exploration of new oil 
and natural gas fields in the country, if so, the details thereof? 
 
ANSWER 
 
पेटŌोिलयम और Ůाक ृ ितक गैस मंũालय मŐ राǛमंũी 
(ŵी सुरे श गोपी) 
 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF PETROLEUM AND NATURAL GAS 
(SHRI SURESH GOPI) 
 
 
(a)      28 hydrocarbon discoveries have been notified during the last 3 years. 
(b)    Hydrocarbon discoveries undergo a series of technical and commercial evaluations before 
commencement of commercial production. These include appraisal drilling,reservoir studies, 
extended well testing, preparation of Field Development Plan (FDP), obtaining statutory and 
environmental clearances and development drilling along with installation of production 
facilities. The commencement of commercial production depends upon the successful completion 
of all these activities and the commercial viability of the discoveries. 
(c)     The contribution of newly discovered hydrocarbon fields to domestic oil and natural gas 
production can be assessed only after completion of appraisal activities, estimation of 
recoverable reserves, approval of Field Development Plans (FDPs) and commencement of 
commercial production. 
(d)     Government has implemented multiple policies to expedite the exploration of new oil and 
natural gas fields in the country the details are placed at Annexure-I. 
***

Hydrocarbon discoveries, 2014;

iv. Policy for Extension of PSCs, 2016 and 2017;   
v. Policy for early monetization of Coal Bed Methane, 2017;

vii. Approval of Un-appraised areas in Sedimentary Basins under National Seismic  
Programme, 2017;   
viii. Policy to Promote/Incentivize Enhanced Recovery Methods of Oil/Gas 2018;   
ix. Policy for exploration and exploitation of Unconventional Hydrocarbons under  
Existing Fields, 2018;   
x. Lower Royalty Rates, Zero Revenue Share (till Windfall Gain) and no drilling

xi. Natural Gas Marketing Reforms, 2020;   
xii. Release of about 1 Million Sq. Km. (SKM) “No-Go” area in offshore which were  
earlier blocked for exploration for decades, 2022;  
xiii. Revised Domestic Price Guidelines were issued in 2023;  
xiv. Amendments in the Oilfields (Regulation and Development) Act, 1948 to promote

resolution, 2025;  
xv. Notification of Petroleum and Natural Gas Rules, 2025.  
xvi. Announcement of National Deepwater Exploration Mission under Samudra Manthan 
with an objective to augment hydrocarbon resources and reserves and to enable their timely 
conversion into production.

xix. Government have approved acquisition of additional 2D Seismic data of 20,000 LKM in 
onland and 30,000 LKM in offshore beyond Exclusive Economic Zone (EEZ) of India.  
xx. Hydrocarbon Resource Assessment Study (HRAS 2025) has been launched on 
17.07.2025 for resource assessment across all Indian sedimentary basins. 
xxi. The Royalty rates for production of crude oil and casing head condensate has been 
notified vide notification dated 08.05.2026 and 04.06.2026. 
xxii. The Union Cabinet has approved ‘Samudra Manthan’ on 31 July 2026 towards National 
Offshore Exploration Scheme with a Phase-I outlay of Rs. 84084 crore upto 2030-31.
